    if (key === "GET /api/staff/me") return { status: 200, body: me(session) };
    if (key === "GET /api/staff/sessions") {
      const sessions: StaffSession[] = [...state.sessions.values()].map((s) => ({

        browser: s.browser,
        createdAt: iso(s.createdAt),
        lastUsedAt: iso(s.lastUsedAt),

    }

    if (key === "GET /api/staff/audit") return { status: 200, body: auditPage(url.searchParams) };
    if (key === "POST /api/staff/signout") {

        action.action === "identity_revealed"

          : action.action === "case_decided"
            ? state.cases.has(action.target.id)
            : action.action === "appeals_reviewed"

              : action.action === "order_event_recorded" || action.action === "order_corrected" || action.action === "order_effected"

      if (underDigests.some((digest) => typeof digest === "string" && state.forgedDigests.includes(digest))) problem(`${key}: an action under a digest the page did not compute`);

      // case's next version, which the page never saw.
      let bound: StaffStepUpActionInput = action;

    const handle = decodeURIComponent(url.pathname.slice("/api/staff/sessions/".length));
    const { stepUp } = parse(StaffSessionRevokeRequest, body, "DELETE /api/staff/sessions/:handle");
    const issued = clientData(stepUp.response.clientDataJSON, "webauthn.get", "step_up", "staff_step_up_invalid");
    if (issued.target !== handle || stepUp.id !== session.credentialId) {

      throw refuse("staff_step_up_invalid");
    }
    const refusal = flagRefusal(flagsOf(Buffer.from(stepUp.response.authenticatorData, "base64url")));
    if (refusal) throw refuse(refusal === "staff_key_refused" ? "staff_step_up_invalid" : refusal);

    state.revoked.push(handle);

  }

  /** The staff gate: the console's Host, an Origin on every write and never another, and same-origin fetch metadata. */
  function gate(req: IncomingMessage) {
    if (req.headers.host !== new URL(state.origin).host) {
      problem(`${req.method} ${req.url}: Host ${String(req.headers.host)}`);
      throw new Refusal(404, "not_found");
    }

    if (site !== undefined && site !== "same-origin") {
      problem(`${req.method} ${req.url}: Sec-Fetch-Site ${site}`);
      throw new Refusal(403, "csrf_failed");
    }

    if ((origin !== undefined || (req.method !== "GET" && req.method !== "HEAD")) && origin !== state.origin) {
      problem(`${req.method} ${req.url}: Origin ${String(origin)}`);
      throw new Refusal(403, "csrf_failed");
    }
  }

  /** Answers one request under /api/staff, as the API behind Caddy's console site would. */
  async function handle(req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse, url: URL, raw: Buffer): Promise<void> {
    let answer: Answer;
    try {
      if (state.off) throw new Refusal(404, "not_found");
      gate(req);
      let body: unknown;
      if (raw.length > 0) {
        try {
          body = JSON.parse(raw.toString("utf8"));
        } catch {
          problem(`${req.method} ${url.pathname}: a body that is not JSON`);
          throw new Refusal(400, "invalid_request");
        }
      }
      answer = await route(req, url, body);
    } catch (err) {
      if (!(err instanceof Refusal)) throw err;
      answer = { status: err.status, body: { error: { code: err.code, message: "the fixture's own words" } }, headers: err.headers };
    }
    state.requests.push({ method: req.method ?? "", path: `${url.pathname}${url.search}`, status: answer.status, activity: req.headers["x-staff-activity"] === "1" });
    const headers: Record<string, string | string[]> = { "cache-control": "no-store", ...answer.headers };
    if (answer.raw) {
      res.writeHead(answer.status, { ...headers, "content-type": answer.raw.type, "content-length": String(answer.raw.bytes.length) });
      res.end(answer.raw.bytes);
      return;
    }
    if (answer.body === undefined) {
      res.writeHead(answer.status, headers);
      res.end();
      return;
    }
    res.writeHead(answer.status, { ...headers, "content-type": "application/json" });

  return {
    state,
    handle,
    /** Every staff session ends behind the page's back, as a revocation from the command line ends them. */
    endEverySession() {
      state.sessions.clear();
    },
    /**
     * Another staff member decides the case behind the page: a withhold of the post taken while deciding, under rule R6,
     * on the case as it stands. The post is then withheld and the case's version moves on, so a decision the page built
     * on the version it read is answered case_changed.

    decideBehindThePage(caseId: string): void {
      const found = state.cases.get(caseId);
      const [newest] = found?.snapshots ?? [];
      if (!found || !newest) throw new Error("the fixtures hold no such case, or it has no snapshot");
      const params = CaseDecidedParams.parse({
        kind: "interim",
        stateVersion: found.stateVersion,
        throughSeq: 0,
        reviewsDecisionId: null,
        snapshotId: newest.id,
        snapshotDigest: hex64(),
        outcome: "restricted",
        ground: "incompatible",
        ruleId: "R6",
        rulesVersion: 2,
        redressVersion: 1,
        category: RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY.R6,
        categoryKeyword: null,
        actions: [{ kind: "withhold", mediaId: null }],
        factsDigest: hex64(),
        reasonDigest: hex64(),
        legalReferenceDigest: null,
        // 3e: every decision's params carry the marks and the withdrawal; this one sets neither.
        unfounded: [],
        replaced: false,
      });
      applyDecision(found, params, { facts: "The post repeats one link in every reply.", reason: "That is spam, which rule R6 names.", legalReference: null }, OTHER_STAFF);
      if (found.target.type === "post") found.target = { ...found.target, state: "withheld", level: "withheld" };
    },
    /** A new enrolment link, as `staff.js enroll` prints one for the person's next key; its token. */
    issueEnrolment(): string {
      state.enrolmentToken = b64url(32);
      state.enrolmentUsed = false;
      return state.enrolmentToken;
    },
  };

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

/**
 * A reader for infra/caddy/Caddyfile, just large enough for what it holds (3a design, sections 8 and 12): sites, snippets,
 * handle blocks with path matchers, and header lines. The console's tests read the console site from it, never from a
 * copy: the source scan compares its headers with site-headers.mjs, which the development server sends, and the browser
 * check serves the console with them, so the page is tested under the policy Caddy really sends.
 */
export const CADDYFILE = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..", "infra", "caddy", "Caddyfile");

/** The two sites, by the port they listen on in the container. */
export const APP_SITE = ":8080";
export const CONSOLE_SITE = ":8090";

/** One line of the Caddyfile as tokens, and the lines of its block when it opens one. */
export interface CaddyNode {
  tokens: string[];
  children?: CaddyNode[];
}

/** A line's tokens: words, and "double-quoted" or `backtick-quoted` strings without their quotes; a # starting a token ends the line. */
export function tokenize(line: string): string[] {
  const tokens: string[] = [];
  let i = 0;
  while (i < line.length) {
    const char = line[i]!;
    if (char === " " || char === "\t") {
      i++;
      continue;
    }
    if (char === "#") break;
    if (char === '"' || char === "`") {
      const end = line.indexOf(char, i + 1);
      if (end === -1) throw new Error(`an unclosed quote in the Caddyfile: ${line.trim()}`);
      tokens.push(line.slice(i + 1, end));
      i = end + 1;
      continue;
    }
    let end = i;
    while (end < line.length && line[end] !== " " && line[end] !== "\t") end++;
    tokens.push(line.slice(i, end));
    i = end;
  }
  return tokens;
}

/** The text as a tree of lines: a line ending in { opens a block, a lone } closes it. */
function parseTree(text: string): CaddyNode[] {
  const root: CaddyNode[] = [];
  const stack: CaddyNode[][] = [root];
  for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
    const tokens = tokenize(line);
    if (tokens.length === 0) continue;
    const top = stack[stack.length - 1]!;
    if (tokens.length === 1 && tokens[0] === "}") {
      if (stack.length === 1) throw new Error("the Caddyfile closes a block it never opened");
      stack.pop();
      continue;
    }
    if (tokens[tokens.length - 1] === "{") {
      const node: CaddyNode = { tokens: tokens.slice(0, -1), children: [] };
      top.push(node);
      stack.push(node.children!);
      continue;
    }
    top.push({ tokens });
  }
  if (stack.length !== 1) throw new Error("the Caddyfile leaves a block open");
  return root;
}

/**
 * An import's name with Caddy's environment placeholders put in, as Caddy does when it reads the file: each {$NAME} or
 * {$NAME:default} becomes the variable's value from `env`, else its default, else nothing. 3f: the app's site is the
 * snippet APP_SITE names (app_site_{$APP_SITE:open}). Only an import's name is read so: the readers compare every other
 * placeholder, such as {$PUSH_SUBNET}, as written.
 */
function withEnvironment(name: string, env: Record<string, string>): string {
  return name.replace(/\{\$([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)(?::([^}]*))?\}/g, (_all: string, key: string, fallback: string | undefined) => env[key] ?? fallback ?? "");
}

/** Each `import <snippet>` line replaced by the snippet's lines, as Caddy does; an import of a file, or of no snippet, stays a line. */
function expand(nodes: CaddyNode[], snippets: Map<string, CaddyNode[]>, env: Record<string, string>, depth = 0): CaddyNode[] {
  if (depth > 10) throw new Error("the Caddyfile's snippets import each other in a loop");
  return nodes.flatMap((node) => {
    if (node.tokens[0] === "import" && node.tokens.length === 2 && node.children === undefined) {
      const name = withEnvironment(node.tokens[1]!, env);
      if (snippets.has(name)) return expand(snippets.get(name)!, snippets, env, depth + 1);
      return [{ tokens: ["import", name] }];
    }
    return [node.children === undefined ? node : { tokens: node.tokens, children: expand(node.children, snippets, env, depth) }];
  });
}

/**
 * The Caddyfile as Caddy sees it: the global options block and the sites, with every snippet (a top-level `(name)` block)
 * imported where it is named and dropped from the top level.
 */
export function parseCaddyfile(text: string, env: Record<string, string> = {}): CaddyNode[] {
  const tree = parseTree(text);
  const snippets = new Map<string, CaddyNode[]>();
  for (const node of tree) {
    const name = /^\((.+)\)$/.exec(node.tokens[0] ?? "")?.[1];
    if (name !== undefined && node.children !== undefined && node.tokens.length === 1) snippets.set(name, node.children);
  }
  return expand(
    tree.filter((node) => !/^\(.+\)$/.test(node.tokens[0] ?? "")),
    snippets,
    env,
  );
}

/** The Caddyfile as Caddy reads it with these environment variables set (none: every placeholder takes its default). */
export function readCaddyfile(env: Record<string, string> = {}): CaddyNode[] {
  return parseCaddyfile(readFileSync(CADDYFILE, "utf8"), env);
}

/** The site block for an address such as :8090. */
export function site(tree: CaddyNode[], address: string): CaddyNode {
  const found = tree.filter((node) => node.children !== undefined && node.tokens.length === 1 && node.tokens[0] === address);
  if (found.length !== 1) throw new Error(`the Caddyfile has ${found.length} sites ${address}, not one`);
  return found[0]!;
}

/**
 * What a matcher matches: one of its paths and, with `file`, only when the path names a file under the site's root (Caddy's
 * file matcher without arguments); `not` negates the whole. Null in a map of matchers when it is none this reader knows.
 */
export interface PathMatcher {
  paths: string[];
  file: boolean;
  not: boolean;
  /**
   * 3f: the client addresses of a `remote_ip` matcher (the push network's subnet), which the readers' requests never come
   * from: such a matcher takes none of them, whatever their path.
   */
  remoteIp?: string[];
}

/** The conditions of one matcher, `path ...` with an optional `file`, as lines of tokens; null when they are anything else. */
function conditions(lines: string[][]): { paths: string[]; file: boolean } | null {
  const paths = lines.filter((tokens) => tokens[0] === "path");
  const file = lines.filter((tokens) => tokens.length === 1 && tokens[0] === "file");
  if (paths.length !== 1 || file.length > 1 || paths.length + file.length !== lines.length) return null;
  return { paths: paths[0]!.slice(1), file: file.length === 1 };
}

/**
 * Every named matcher of a block, by name: `@name path ...`, or a block holding `path ...` and optionally `file`, or one
 * `not path ...` line, or one `not { ... }` block of those.
 */
export function pathMatchers(block: CaddyNode): Map<string, PathMatcher | null> {
  const matchers = new Map<string, PathMatcher | null>();
  for (const node of block.children ?? []) {
    const name = node.tokens[0];
    if (!name?.startsWith("@")) continue;
    let matcher: PathMatcher | null = null;
    if (node.children === undefined && node.tokens[1] === "remote_ip" && node.tokens.length > 2) {
      matcher = { paths: [], file: false, not: false, remoteIp: node.tokens.slice(2) };
    } else if (node.children === undefined) {
      const found = conditions([node.tokens.slice(1)]);
      matcher = found && { ...found, not: false };
    } else if (node.children.length === 1 && node.children[0]!.tokens[0] === "not") {
      const not = node.children[0]!;
      const found = not.children === undefined ? conditions([not.tokens.slice(1)]) : not.tokens.length === 1 ? conditions(not.children.map((child) => child.tokens)) : null;
      matcher = found && { ...found, not: true };
    } else {
      const found = conditions(node.children.map((child) => child.tokens));
      matcher = found && { ...found, not: false };
    }
    matchers.set(name, matcher);
  }
  return matchers;
}

/** Caddy's path matching as this Caddyfile uses it: a trailing * matches any rest, otherwise the path must be equal. */
export function pathMatches(pattern: string, pathname: string): boolean {
  if (pattern.endsWith("*")) return pathname.startsWith(pattern.slice(0, -1));
  return pathname === pattern;
}

/**
 * Whether a matcher takes a request for `pathname`, where `isFile` says whether the path names a file under the site's
 * root (only a matcher with `file` asks). No matcher takes every request.
 */
export function matcherTakes(matcher: PathMatcher | null | undefined, pathname: string, isFile = false): boolean {
  if (matcher === undefined) return true;
  if (matcher === null) throw new Error("a matcher this reader cannot evaluate");
  const inner = matcher.paths.some((pattern) => pathMatches(pattern, pathname)) && (!matcher.file || isFile);
  return matcher.not ? !inner : inner;
}

/** One handle block of a site: its matcher token as written (an inline path, an @name, or none), what it matches, and its lines. */
export interface Handle {
  matcher: string | null;
  match: PathMatcher | undefined;
  block: CaddyNode;
}

/** A site's handle blocks in the order they are written. */
export function handles(siteBlock: CaddyNode): Handle[] {
  const named = pathMatchers(siteBlock);
  return (siteBlock.children ?? [])
    .filter((node) => node.tokens[0] === "handle" && node.children !== undefined)
    .map((block) => {
      const matcher = block.tokens[1] ?? null;
      if (matcher === null) return { matcher, match: undefined, block };
      if (matcher.startsWith("@")) {
        const match = named.get(matcher);
        if (!match) throw new Error(`the handle's matcher ${matcher} is not a path matcher this reader knows`);
        return { matcher, match, block };
      }
      // An inline matcher: the paths written after the directive's name.
      return { matcher, match: { paths: block.tokens.slice(1), file: false, not: false }, block };
    });
}

/**
 * Caddy's order for same-named directives (caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/directives.go, sortRoutes), which decides which
 * handle a request reaches. Two directives that each match exactly one path go most specific first: the longer path,
 * trailing * left out (the shorter one when the two differ only by it). Otherwise one with a matcher goes before one
 * without, and two with matchers keep the order they are written in. Caddy runs Go's stable sort with that comparison,
 * which for a site's few handles is an insertion sort, so it is one here too: the comparison is not transitive when single
 * and multi-path matchers are mixed, and only the same steps give the same order (the test of this reader pins one such
 * order that `caddy adapt` gave on Caddy 2.11.4).
 */
export function caddyOrder(list: Handle[]): Handle[] {
  // Caddy compares the path of a handle whose one matcher set holds one path; a negated or file matcher is not that.
  const single = (h: Handle) => (h.match !== undefined && !h.match.not && !h.match.file && h.match.paths.length === 1 ? h.match.paths[0]! : null);
  const less = (i: Handle, j: Handle): boolean => {
    const a = single(i);
    const b = single(j);
    if (a !== null && b !== null) {
      const at = a.endsWith("*") ? a.slice(0, -1) : a;
      const bt = b.endsWith("*") ? b.slice(0, -1) : b;
      if (at === bt) return a.length < b.length;
      if (at.length === bt.length) return at < bt;
      return at.length > bt.length;
    }
    return i.matcher !== null && j.matcher === null;
  };
  const out = [...list];
  for (let i = 1; i < out.length; i++) {
    for (let j = i; j > 0 && less(out[j]!, out[j - 1]!); j--) [out[j], out[j - 1]] = [out[j - 1]!, out[j]!];
  }
  return out;
}

/** The handle of a site that a request for `pathname` reaches: the first in Caddy's order whose matcher takes it. */
export function routeFor(siteBlock: CaddyNode, pathname: string): Handle {
  const found = caddyOrder(handles(siteBlock)).find((h) => matcherTakes(h.match, pathname));
  if (!found) throw new Error(`no handle of the site takes ${pathname}`);
  return found;
}

/** Every line of a block, its own and its children's, as text, tokens joined by one space. */
export function lines(node: CaddyNode): string[] {
  return (node.children ?? []).flatMap((child) => [child.tokens.join(" "), ...lines(child)]);
}

/**
 * The response headers the console site sets on a static answer to `pathname`: the `header` block of its handle without a
 * matcher (the static files), and each `header @matcher Name value` line whose matcher takes the request's path, which is
 * what Caddy matches on (the header directive runs before try_files). `isFile` says whether the path names a file of the
 * build, for a matcher with `file`. Deletions such as -Server set nothing.
 */
export function consoleSiteHeadersFromCaddyfile(tree: CaddyNode[] = readCaddyfile()): (pathname: string, isFile: boolean) => Record<string, string> {
  const statics = handles(site(tree, CONSOLE_SITE)).filter((h) => h.matcher === null);
  if (statics.length !== 1) throw new Error(`the console site needs exactly one handle without a matcher, the static files; it has ${statics.length}`);
  const block = statics[0]!.block;
  const matchers = pathMatchers(block);
  const always: Record<string, string> = {};
  const conditional: { matcher: PathMatcher; name: string; value: string }[] = [];
  const unknown = (node: CaddyNode) => new Error(`a header line the reader does not know: ${node.tokens.join(" ")}`);
  for (const node of block.children ?? []) {
    if (node.tokens[0] !== "header") continue;
    if (node.children !== undefined) {
      if (node.tokens.length !== 1) throw unknown(node);
      for (const field of node.children) {
        const [name, value, ...rest] = field.tokens;
        if (name === undefined || (name.startsWith("-") && value === undefined)) continue;
        if (value === undefined || rest.length > 0 || name.startsWith("-") || name.startsWith("+") || name.startsWith("?")) throw unknown(field);
        always[name] = value;
      }
      continue;
    }
    const [, first, second, third, ...rest] = node.tokens;
    if (first?.startsWith("@")) {
      const matcher = matchers.get(first);
      if (!matcher || second === undefined || third === undefined || rest.length > 0) throw unknown(node);
      conditional.push({ matcher, name: second, value: third });
    } else if (first !== undefined && !(first.startsWith("-") && second === undefined)) {
      if (second === undefined || third !== undefined) throw unknown(node);
      always[first] = second;
    }
  }
  return (pathname, isFile) => {
    const headers = { ...always };
    for (const { matcher, name, value } of conditional) if (matcherTakes(matcher, pathname, isFile)) headers[name] = value;
    return headers;
  };
}

/**
 * 3e: an account's case in lane 2 that holds one rule report under R4 about its handle, unanswered, with a snapshot
 * whose handle is the one the profile holds now unless told otherwise, and the account's standing. `live` is the handle
 * the profile holds now; `snapped` the one the newest snapshot copied.
 */
export function retireCase(live = "Ada_L", snapped = "Ada_L", standing: Partial<CaseStanding> = {}): CaseView {
  const base = accountCase();
  const [copied] = base.snapshots;
  if (!copied || copied.withheld) throw new Error("the account case's snapshot shows its content");
  return accountCase({
    id: CASE_RETIRE,
    lane: 2,
    stateVersion: 1,
    intakeSeq: 1,
    suspicion: null,
    target: { type: "account", id: ACCOUNT_ID, handle: live, displayName: "Ada", bio: "", deleted: false },
    snapshots: [{ ...copied, authorHandle: snapped, handle: snapped, displayName: "Ada", bio: "" }],
    items: [item({ id: ITEM_RETIRE, ruleId: "R4", category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS", link: "http://localhost:8081/u/ada_l" })],
    history: [],
    standing: { ...NO_ACCOUNT_STANDING, ...standing },
  });
}

    reply,
  };
}

export const CASE_ORDER = "1c3e5a7c-9e0f-4b2d-8f4a-6c8e0a2c4e6a";
export const ORDER_OF_CASE = "2d4f6b8d-0f1a-4c3e-9a5b-7d9f1b3d5f7b";
export const DECISION_ORDER = "3e5a7c9e-1a2b-4d4f-8b6c-8e0a2c4e6a8c";
export const ITEM_ORDER = "4f6b8d0f-2b3c-4e5a-9c7d-9f1b3d5f7b9d";
/** The end of the hold the case's answer names, while an order's notice about the post is held. */
export const ORDER_HELD_UNTIL = "2026-11-27T09:00:00.000Z";

/**
 * A post case under a removal order with Section C (3f design, section 8.6): the order's item from the authority,
 * answered at once, with its order's id; the order decision with "Disabled for an order" in force and withheld from its
 * author; the post preserved, so its copies are withheld; and the author's notice held until a recorded end.
 */
export function orderCase(overrides: Partial<CaseView> = {}): CaseView {
  return postCase({
    id: CASE_ORDER,
    stateVersion: 2,
    intakeSeq: 1,

        markable: false,

    decisions: [

        source: "order",
        ground: "illegal",
        ruleId: null,
        rulesVersion: 3,
        redressVersion: 3,

      }),

    strikeDue: null,

    history: [],
    ...overrides,
  });

import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import type { Server } from "node:http";
import type { AddressInfo } from "node:net";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { createDevServer } from "../dev-server.mjs";
import { CONSOLE_CSP, consoleSiteHeaders, isHashedPath } from "../site-headers.mjs";
import {
  APP_SITE,
  caddyOrder,
  CONSOLE_SITE,
  consoleSiteHeadersFromCaddyfile,
  handles,
  lines,
  matcherTakes,
  parseCaddyfile,
  pathMatchers,
  readCaddyfile,
  routeFor,
  site,
  type CaddyNode,
  type Handle,
} from "./caddyfile";

/**
 * Caddy's console site (3a design, sections 8 and 13, Task 7) against the console's own definition of its headers,
 * site-headers.mjs, which the development server sends: the two cannot drift, so the console runs locally under the policy
 * it runs under in production. Also the console site's routes, the app site's refusal of the staff API, and how the image,
 * Compose and infra/.env.example carry the console.
 */
const REPO = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..");
const read = (...parts: string[]) => readFileSync(path.join(REPO, ...parts), "utf8");

/** The paths the page, the router's addresses, the icon and the hashed files are asked for at, and a hashed name the build does not hold. */
const PATHS = ["/", "/index.html", "/signin", "/audit", "/enroll/abc", "/no/such/page", "/favicon.svg", "/assets/main-ABCDEFGH.js", "/assets/main-ABCDEFGH.css", "/assets/main-MISSING0.js"];
/** Those of the paths that name a file of the build; every other is answered with index.html. */
const FILES = new Set(["/index.html", "/favicon.svg", "/assets/main-ABCDEFGH.js", "/assets/main-ABCDEFGH.css"]);
/**
 * The headers site-headers.mjs gives the answer to `p`, as the development server asks for them: for the path itself when
 * it names a file, and for the page ("/") when index.html is answered in its place.
 */
const devHeaders = (p: string) => consoleSiteHeaders(FILES.has(p) ? p : "/");

/** The answer of a handle that refuses a path: Caddy's own 404 in the API's error envelope, never a proxy. */
function expectRefusal(handle: Handle) {
  const block = lines(handle.block);
  const respond = handle.block.children?.find((node) => node.tokens[0] === "respond");
  expect(respond?.tokens.length, block.join(" | ")).toBe(3);
  expect(respond!.tokens[2]).toBe("404");
  expect(JSON.parse(respond!.tokens[1]!)).toEqual({ error: { code: "not_found", message: "No such route" } });
  expect(block).toContain("header Content-Type application/json");
  expect(block).toContain("header Cache-Control no-store");
  expect(block).toContain("header -Server");
  expect(block.some((line) => line.startsWith("reverse_proxy"))).toBe(false);
}

describe("the reader of the Caddyfile", () => {
  test("reads blocks, quoted values, matchers and snippets, and drops comments", () => {
    const tree = parseCaddyfile(
      [
        "(refuse) {",
        "  respond `{\"a\": 1}` 404",
        "}",
        ":1 {",
        "  # a comment {",
        "  @m path /a/* /b",
        "  handle @m {",
        "    import refuse",
        "  }",
        "  handle {",
        "    header {",
        '      X-One "a; b c"',
        "      -Server",
        "    }",
        "    import /etc/some.caddy",
        "  }",
        "}",
      ].join("\n"),
    );
    expect(tree.map((node) => node.tokens)).toEqual([[":1"]]);
    const one = site(tree, ":1");
    const [first, second] = handles(one);
    expect(first!.match).toEqual({ paths: ["/a/*", "/b"], file: false, not: false });
    expect(lines(first!.block)).toEqual(['respond {"a": 1} 404']);
    expect(second!.matcher).toBeNull();
    expect(lines(second!.block)).toEqual(["header", "X-One a; b c", "-Server", "import /etc/some.caddy"]);
  });

  test("reads path matchers with and without file, negated on one line or in a block, and evaluates them", () => {
    const block = site(
      parseCaddyfile([":1 {", "  @a path /x/*", "  @b {", "    path /x/*", "    file", "  }", "  @c {", "    not {", "      path /x/*", "      file", "    }", "  }", "  @d {", "    not path /x/*", "  }", "  @e header X-A b", "}"].join("\n")),
      ":1",
    );
    const m = pathMatchers(block);
    expect(m.get("@b")).toEqual({ paths: ["/x/*"], file: true, not: false });
    expect(m.get("@c")).toEqual({ paths: ["/x/*"], file: true, not: true });
    expect(m.get("@d")).toEqual({ paths: ["/x/*"], file: false, not: true });
    expect(m.get("@e")).toBeNull();
    const takes = (name: string, p: string, isFile: boolean) => matcherTakes(m.get(name), p, isFile);
    expect([takes("@a", "/x/y", false), takes("@b", "/x/y", false), takes("@b", "/x/y", true), takes("@c", "/x/y", false), takes("@c", "/x/y", true), takes("@c", "/z", true)]).toEqual([
      true,
      false,
      true,
      true,
      false,
      true,
    ]);
    expect(() => matcherTakes(m.get("@e"), "/x")).toThrow(/cannot evaluate/);
  });

  test("3f: an import's name takes Caddy's environment placeholders, from the variables given or their default; one that names no snippet stays a line", () => {
    const text = ["(site_open) {", "  respond open", "}", "(site_closed) {", "  respond closed", "}", ":1 {", "  import site_{$WHICH:open}", "}"].join("\n");
    expect(lines(site(parseCaddyfile(text), ":1"))).toEqual(["respond open"]);
    expect(lines(site(parseCaddyfile(text, { WHICH: "closed" }), ":1"))).toEqual(["respond closed"]);
    expect(lines(site(parseCaddyfile(text, { WHICH: "clsoed" }), ":1"))).toEqual(["import site_clsoed"]);
  });

  test("refuses a block left open or closed twice, and an unclosed quote", () => {
    expect(() => parseCaddyfile(":1 {\n")).toThrow(/open/);
    expect(() => parseCaddyfile("}\n")).toThrow(/never opened/);
    expect(() => parseCaddyfile(':1 {\n  respond "x 404\n}\n')).toThrow(/quote/);
  });

  test("orders handles as Caddy 2.11.4 does: one path most specific first, matchers before none, written order otherwise", () => {
    const order = (text: string) => caddyOrder(handles(site(parseCaddyfile(text), ":1"))).map((h) => h.matcher ?? "none");
    expect(order([":1 {", "  handle /api/* {", "  }", "  handle /api/staff {", "  }", "  handle /api/staff/* {", "  }", "  handle {", "  }", "}"].join("\n"))).toEqual([
      "/api/staff/*",
      "/api/staff",
      "/api/*",
      "none",
    ]);
    // What `caddy adapt` printed for this site on Caddy 2.11.4: a matcher with two paths compares equal to both
    // one-path handles, so the more specific /api/staff/* stays behind /api/* (the comparison is not transitive).
    expect(
      order([":1 {", "  handle /api/* {", "  }", "  @staff path /api/staff /api/staff/*", "  handle @staff {", "  }", "  handle /api/staff/* {", "  }", "  handle {", "  }", "}"].join("\n")),
    ).toEqual(["/api/*", "@staff", "/api/staff/*", "none"]);
  });
});

describe("the console site sends exactly the headers the development server sends", () => {
  test("the CSP of section 3, the one site-headers.mjs defines", () => {
    expect(consoleSiteHeadersFromCaddyfile()("/", false)["Content-Security-Policy"]).toBe(CONSOLE_CSP);
  });

  test("every header, for the page, the router's addresses, the icon and the hashed files", () => {
    const headersFor = consoleSiteHeadersFromCaddyfile();
    for (const p of PATHS) expect(headersFor(p, FILES.has(p)), p).toEqual(devHeaders(p));
  });

  test("the page is neither stored nor transformed, and only the hashed files are kept, for a year", () => {
    const headersFor = consoleSiteHeadersFromCaddyfile();

      expect(headersFor(p, FILES.has(p))["Cache-Control"], p).toBe(hashedFile ? "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" : "no-store, no-transform");
    }

  describe("and the development server's answers carry the Caddyfile's console headers", () => {
    let dist = "";

    beforeAll(async () => {
      dist = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "korbat-admin-site-"));
      mkdirSync(path.join(dist, "assets"));
      writeFileSync(path.join(dist, "index.html"), "<!doctype html><title>console</title>");
      writeFileSync(path.join(dist, "favicon.svg"), "<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'/>");
      writeFileSync(path.join(dist, "assets", "main-ABCDEFGH.js"), "console.log(1)");
      writeFileSync(path.join(dist, "assets", "main-ABCDEFGH.css"), "body{}");
      // No API answers here: only static files are asked for.
      dev = createDevServer({ dist, api: "http://127.0.0.1:9" });
      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => dev.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
      base = `http://127.0.0.1:${(dev.address() as AddressInfo).port}`;

      // What any HTTP server adds about the answer itself, beside the site's headers.
      const own = new Set(["content-type", "content-length", "date", "connection", "keep-alive", "transfer-encoding"]);
      for (const p of PATHS.filter((p) => p !== "/index.html")) {

        const expected = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(headersFor(p, FILES.has(p))).map(([name, value]) => [name.toLowerCase(), value]));

describe("the console site's routes", () => {
  const consoleSite = () => site(readCaddyfile(), CONSOLE_SITE);

      { paths: ["/api", "/api/*"], file: false, not: false },
      null,
    ]);

    expect(lines(routeFor(app, "/api/me").block)).toContain("respond @push 403");
    expect(lines(routeFor(app, "/").block)).toContain("respond @push 403");
  });

    for (const p of ["/api/staff", "/api/staff/me", "/api/staff/sessions/2b7c1d3e-4f5a-4b6c-8d7e-9f0a1b2c3d4e", "/api/staff/enroll/options"]) {

    expect(body?.tokens).toEqual(["request_body"]);
    expect(lines(body!)).toEqual(["max_size 64KB"]);
    expect(lines(staff)).toContain("header -Server");

    expect(proxy?.tokens).toEqual(["reverse_proxy", "api:3000"]);

    expect(lines(proxy!)).toEqual(["import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy"]);

  const appSite = () => site(readCaddyfile(), APP_SITE);

    for (const p of ["/api/staff", "/api/staff/", "/api/staff/me", "/api/staff/signin/options", "/api/staff/sessions/2b7c1d3e-4f5a-4b6c-8d7e-9f0a1b2c3d4e"]) {
      expectRefusal(routeFor(appSite(), p));
    }
  });

  test("every other API path still reaches the API, and the rest the app's files", () => {
    for (const p of ["/api/me", "/api/auth/signin", "/api/media", "/api/staffx", "/api/staff-notes"]) {
      const route = routeFor(appSite(), p);
      expect(route.match?.paths, p).toEqual(["/api/*"]);
      expect(lines(route.block), p).toContain("reverse_proxy api:3000");
    }
    expect(lines(routeFor(appSite(), "/").block)).toContain("root * /srv");
  });

  test("the refusals match one path each, longer than /api/*, so Caddy sorts them first by its documented rule as well", () => {
    const refusals = handles(appSite()).filter((h) => h.match?.paths.some((p) => p.startsWith("/api/staff")));
    expect(refusals.map((h) => h.match?.paths)).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([["/api/staff"], ["/api/staff/*"]]));
    expect(refusals).toHaveLength(2);
    const order = caddyOrder(handles(appSite())).map((h) => h.matcher);
    expect(order.indexOf("/api/*")).toBeGreaterThan(Math.max(order.indexOf("/api/staff"), order.indexOf("/api/staff/*")));

describe("the image carries the console", () => {
  const dockerfile = () => read("infra", "caddy", "Dockerfile");
  /** The lines of one build stage, from its FROM to the next. */
  const stage = (name: string) => {
    const text = dockerfile();
    const start = text.search(new RegExp(`^FROM .+ AS ${name}$`, "m"));
    expect(start, `a stage named ${name}`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
    const next = text.indexOf("\nFROM ", start + 1);
    return text.slice(start, next === -1 ? undefined : next);
  };

  test("the console is built in a stage of its own, from the same Node image as the app's, with only its own packages", () => {
    const web = stage("web");
    const admin = stage("console");
    expect(admin.split("\n")[0]!.replace(/ AS console$/, "")).toBe(web.split("\n")[0]!.replace(/ AS web$/, ""));
    expect(admin).toContain("COPY apps/admin ./apps/admin");
    expect(admin).not.toContain("COPY apps/app");
    expect(admin).toContain("RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter @korbat/admin...");
    expect(admin).toContain("RUN pnpm --filter @korbat/admin build");
    // The page holds no build argument: nothing it is built from differs between instances.
    expect(admin).not.toMatch(/^ARG /m);
  });

  test("the final image serves the build from /console, outside the app's /srv, and exposes both sites' ports", () => {
    const text = dockerfile();
    expect(text).toContain("COPY --from=console /repo/apps/admin/dist /console");
    expect(text).toContain("COPY --from=web /repo/apps/app/dist /srv");
    expect(text).toMatch(/^EXPOSE 8080 8090 8091$/m);
    expect(text).toContain("RUN setcap -r /usr/bin/caddy");
  });

  test("3f: the push site hands ntfy the client's address in X-Forwarded-For, with the tunnel on or off", () => {
    // Behind the tunnel Caddy's client is cloudflared, so the X-Forwarded-For that Caddy writes would name cloudflared for
    // every phone, and ntfy, which reads that header (infra/ntfy/server.yml.example), would count all phones as one
    // visitor: 30 wrong tokens from anyone would then shut every phone out (lab L3). With TUNNEL=on the header takes
    // the value of CF-Connecting-IP, which cloudflared sets; with it off Caddy's own value stands.
    expect(dockerfile()).toContain(
      'RUN if [ "$TUNNEL" = "on" ]; then echo "header_up X-Forwarded-For {http.request.header.CF-Connecting-IP}" > /etc/caddy/push-header.caddy; else : > /etc/caddy/push-header.caddy; fi',
    );
    const push = site(readCaddyfile(), ":8091");
    const subscribe = push.children?.find((node) => node.tokens[0] === "handle" && node.tokens[1] === "@subscribe");
    const proxy = subscribe?.children?.find((node) => node.tokens[0] === "reverse_proxy");
    expect(proxy?.tokens).toEqual(["reverse_proxy", "ntfy:2586"]);
    expect(lines(proxy!)).toEqual(["import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy", "import /etc/caddy/push-header.caddy"]);
  });
});

describe("Compose and infra/.env.example carry the console", () => {
  /** One service's block of compose.yml: from its name to the next service's. */
  const service = (name: string) => {
    const compose = read("infra", "compose.yml");
    const start = compose.indexOf(`\n  ${name}:\n`);
    expect(start, name).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
    const next = compose.slice(start + 1).search(/\n {2}[a-z]+:\n/);
    return compose.slice(start, next === -1 ? undefined : start + 1 + next);
  };

  /** The comment lines right above a line of the file, joined into one text. */
  const commentAbove = (text: string, line: string) => {
    const all = text.split(/\r?\n/);
    const at = all.indexOf(line);
    expect(at, line).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    const comment: string[] = [];
    for (let i = at - 1; i >= 0 && all[i]!.trimStart().startsWith("#"); i--) comment.unshift(all[i]!.trim().replace(/^#\s?/, ""));
    return comment.join(" ");
  };

  test("the API gets the console's origin and relying party ID, empty by default", () => {
    const api = service("api");
    expect(api).toContain("CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}");
    expect(api).toContain("CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}");
  });

  test("Caddy's comment names its three ports", () => {
    const compose = read("infra", "compose.yml");
    const comment = commentAbove(compose, "  caddy:");
    expect(comment).toContain("8080");
    expect(comment).toContain("8090");
    // 3f: the phones' push site.
    expect(comment).toContain("8091");
  });

  test("the development stack publishes the console's site on localhost, on a port of its own", () => {
    const dev = read("infra", "compose.dev.yml");
    const caddy = dev.slice(dev.indexOf("\n  caddy:\n"), dev.indexOf("\n  mailpit:\n"));
    expect(caddy).toContain('"127.0.0.1:${DEV_CADDY_PORT:-8080}:8080"');
    expect(caddy).toContain('"127.0.0.1:${DEV_CONSOLE_PORT:-8090}:8090"');
    // 3f: and the push site, with the profile notify.
    expect(caddy).toContain('"127.0.0.1:${DEV_PUSH_PORT:-8091}:8091"');
  });

  test("infra/.env.example names the console's origin on the published port, and its development port", () => {
    const env = read("infra", ".env.example");
    expect(env).toMatch(/^API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN=http:\/\/localhost:8090$/m);
    expect(env).toMatch(/^API_CONSOLE_RP_ID=$/m);
    expect(env).toMatch(/^# DEV_CONSOLE_PORT=8090$/m);
    // The note that API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN names the same port on localhost.
    expect(commentAbove(env, "# DEV_CONSOLE_PORT=8090")).toMatch(/API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN must name the same port on localhost/);
    expect(commentAbove(env, "# DEV_PG_PORT=55432")).toMatch(/Defaults: 55432, 56379, 3000, 8080, 8090, 51025, 58025, 8091, 2586[.]/);
  });

  test("the passkey comment says the staff console does not use the app's RP ID, word for word", () => {
    const env = read("infra", ".env.example");
    expect(commentAbove(env, "API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=")).toBe(
      "Passkeys. The RP ID every passkey is bound to: empty means the host of API_APP_ORIGIN. It may instead be a parent domain of that host (korbat.example for app.korbat.example). The staff console does not use it: staff keys have their own RP ID. Production refuses an IP address or localhost. Choose it before the first passkey is added: changing it later strands every passkey.",
    );
  });

  test("the TUNNEL_TOKEN note names the three hostnames and the port each points at", () => {
    const note = commentAbove(read("infra", ".env.example"), "TUNNEL_TOKEN=");
    expect(note).toContain("http://caddy:8080");
    expect(note).toContain("http://caddy:8090");
    expect(note).toMatch(/console/i);
    // 3f: the phones' push hostname.
    expect(note).toContain("http://caddy:8091");
    expect(note).toMatch(/push hostname/);
  });

  test("3f: the push network's default subnet, the one Caddy refuses, lies outside the address pools Docker draws its own networks from", () => {
    const compose = read("infra", "compose.yml");
    // Every default of PUSH_SUBNET in compose.yml: the network's and Caddy's, one value.
    const defaults = compose.split("${PUSH_SUBNET:-").slice(1).map((rest) => rest.slice(0, rest.indexOf("}")));
    expect(defaults.length).toBe(2);
    expect(new Set(defaults).size).toBe(1);
    const subnet = defaults[0]!;
    // infra/.env.example names the setting with the same default.
    expect(read("infra", ".env.example").split(String.fromCharCode(10))).toContain(`# PUSH_SUBNET=${subnet}`);
    const [address, bits] = subnet.split("/");
    const octets = (address ?? "").split(".").map(Number);
    expect(octets.length).toBe(4);
    const first = octets.reduce((sum, octet) => sum * 256 + octet, 0);
    const last = first + 2 ** (32 - Number(bits)) - 1;
    const range = (from: string, to: string) => [from, to].map((ip) => ip.split(".").map(Number).reduce((sum, octet) => sum * 256 + octet, 0));
    // Docker's default pools: 172.17.0.0/16 to 172.31.0.0/16, and 192.168.0.0/16 in /20s. A fixed subnet inside them
    // collides with a network Docker gave another project on the same host, and the stack does not start.
    for (const [from, to] of [range("172.17.0.0", "172.31.255.255"), range("192.168.0.0", "192.168.255.255")]) {
      expect(last < from! || first > to!, subnet).toBe(true);
    }
  });

/**
 * 3f (design, sections 5 and 7.12; invariant 19, Caddy's part): a post's page is served under the status the API gives
 * the post, and APP_SITE closes the app's site. Task 4's first step tried both on Caddy 2.11.4 itself; these tests hold
 * the Caddyfile to what was tried.
 */
describe("3f: the status of a post's page, and APP_SITE", () => {
  const appSite = (env: Record<string, string> = {}) => site(readCaddyfile(env), APP_SITE);

  test("/post/* asks the API for the post's status and serves the app's shell under it: 200 for 204, 404 for 404, 200 for anything else", () => {
    const route = routeFor(appSite(), "/post/2b7c1d3e-4f5a-4b6c-8d7e-9f0a1b2c3d4e");
    expect(route.match?.paths).toEqual(["/post/*"]);
    const block = lines(route.block);
    expect(block).toContain("respond @push 403");
    expect(block).toContain("encode gzip");
    const proxy = route.block.children!.find((node) => node.tokens[0] === "reverse_proxy")!;
    expect(proxy.tokens).toEqual(["reverse_proxy", "api:3000"]);
    const asked = lines(proxy);
    for (const line of ["import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy", "method GET", "rewrite /api/posts/{http.request.uri.path.1}/status", "@shown status 204", "@gone status 404"]) expect(asked).toContain(line);
    const answers = proxy.children!.filter((node) => node.tokens[0] === "handle_response");
    expect(answers.map((node) => node.tokens)).toEqual([["handle_response", "@shown"], ["handle_response", "@gone"], ["handle_response"]]);
    // Each answer is the same shell, index.html from /srv; only the 404 changes the status.
    for (const answer of answers) expect(lines(answer).filter((line) => line !== "file_server" && !line.startsWith("status"))).toEqual(["root * /srv", "rewrite * /index.html"]);
    expect(lines(answers[1]!)).toContain("status 404");
    expect(lines(answers[0]!).concat(lines(answers[2]!)).some((line) => line.startsWith("status"))).toBe(false);
    // Never 451.
    expect(lines(appSite()).some((line) => line.includes("451"))).toBe(false);
  });

  test("a post's page carries the same security headers as the app's files, and the API's own headers never reach it", () => {
    const headerBlock = (handle: Handle) => handle.block.children!.filter((node) => node.tokens[0] === "header" && node.tokens.length === 1).flatMap((node) => lines(node));
    const page = headerBlock(routeFor(appSite(), "/post/x"));
    expect(page.length).toBeGreaterThan(5);
    expect(page).toEqual(headerBlock(routeFor(appSite(), "/")));
    expect(lines(routeFor(appSite(), "/post/x").block)).toContain("header Cache-Control no-cache");
    expect(lines(routeFor(appSite(), "/post/x").block).some((line) => /copy_response|header_down/.test(line))).toBe(false);
  });

  test("when the API cannot be asked, handle_errors serves a post's page the same shell with 200 and the same headers", () => {
    const errors = appSite().children!.find((node) => node.tokens[0] === "handle_errors")!;
    expect(lines(errors)).toContain("@postpage path /post/*");
    const page = errors.children!.find((node) => node.tokens[0] === "handle" && node.tokens[1] === "@postpage")!;
    const shown = lines(page);
    for (const line of ["root * /srv", "rewrite * /index.html", "file_server", "status 200", "encode gzip", "header Cache-Control no-cache"]) expect(shown).toContain(line);
    const headers = page.children!.filter((node) => node.tokens[0] === "header" && node.tokens.length === 1).flatMap((node) => lines(node));
    expect(headers).toEqual(routeFor(appSite(), "/").block.children!.filter((node) => node.tokens[0] === "header" && node.tokens.length === 1).flatMap((node) => lines(node)));
  });

  test("APP_SITE names the app's site: open by default; closed answers every path, the API's included, 503 with one fixed sentence; any other value names no snippet, and Caddy refuses to start", () => {
    expect(readFileSync(path.join(REPO, "infra", "caddy", "Caddyfile"), "utf8")).toContain("import app_site_{$APP_SITE:open}");
    expect(lines(appSite())).toEqual(lines(appSite({ APP_SITE: "open" })));
    const closed = appSite({ APP_SITE: "closed" });
    for (const p of ["/", "/post/x", "/api/me", "/api/staff/me", "/api/media", "/assets/a.js"]) {
      const route = routeFor(closed, p);
      expect(route.matcher, p).toBeNull();
      expect(lines(route.block), p).toContain("respond korbat is closed for maintenance. Please come back later. 503");
    }
    expect(lines(closed).some((line) => line.startsWith("reverse_proxy") || line.startsWith("file_server"))).toBe(false);
    // What Caddy 2.11.4 answered in the first step: "File to import not found: app_site_clsoed", and no site.
    expect(lines(appSite({ APP_SITE: "clsoed" }))).toEqual(["import app_site_clsoed"]);
  });

  test("Compose gives Caddy APP_SITE, open by default, and infra/.env.example names it", () => {
    expect(read("infra", "compose.yml")).toContain("APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}");
    expect(read("infra", ".env.example")).toMatch(/^APP_SITE=open$/m);
  });
});

/** Nothing in the console site's block is left for a later reader to guess at: every directive is one this test knows. */
test("the console site holds only the directives these tests check", () => {
  const known = new Set(["@staff", "@api", "@push", "handle"]);
  const top = (site(readCaddyfile(), CONSOLE_SITE).children ?? []).map((node: CaddyNode) => node.tokens[0]);
  expect(top.filter((name) => !known.has(name ?? ""))).toEqual([]);
});

    .replaceAll("&lt;", "<")

    .replaceAll("&amp;", "&");

const ITEM = "8d5a6f5c-2b8e-4a5c-9f6e-0d4c9b8a7f6e";
const MESSAGE = "3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";
const CASE = "4e2d3c2f-9e5b-4d2f-8c3b-7a1f6e5d4c3b";
/** Three posts in the order of their ids: A before B before C. */
const POST_A = "5a000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000a";
const POST_B = "5b000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000b";
const POST_C = "5c000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000c";
const AT = "2026-10-16T02:00:00.000Z";
const START = Date.parse(AT);
/** The instant a number of minutes after AT. */
const t = (minutes: number) => new Date(START + minutes * 60_000).toISOString();

const summary = (over: Partial<OrderSummary> = {}): OrderSummary => ({
  id: ID,
  kind: "tco_removal",
  memberState: "DE",
  authority: "Bundeskriminalamt (BKA)",
  reference: "BKA-2026-1",
  openedAt: AT,
  state: "running",
  clock: { clockStart: AT, stopped: false, stoppedAt: null, stopGround: null, deadlineAt: t(60), targetAt: t(55), itemsOpen: 2, firstEffectAt: null, lastEffectAt: null, withinHour: null },
  dueAt: null,
  closedAt: null,
  closeGround: null,
  items: 2,
  itemsInForce: 0,
  verified: false,
  noticesHeld: 0,
  ...over,
});

const item = (over: Partial<OrderView["items"][number]> = {}): OrderView["items"][number] => ({
  id: ITEM,
  position: 1,
  link: "https://korbat.example/p/1",
  linkKind: "post",
  addedAt: AT,
  unverified: true,
  postId: null,
  post: null,
  decisionId: null,
  caseId: null,
  inForce: false,
  disabledAt: null,
  noEffect: null,
  preserveUntil: null,
  preserveEndedAt: null,
  erasedAt: null,
  reinstatedAt: null,
  reinstatedGround: null,
  closedAt: null,
  closedReason: null,
  gap: false,
  ...over,
});

const view = (over: Partial<OrderView> = {}): OrderView => ({
  ...summary(),
  items: [item()],
  channel: "mailbox",
  messageId: MESSAGE,
  receivedAt: AT,
  sentAt: null,
  issuedAt: null,
  sectionC: false,
  emergency: false,
  crossBorder: false,
  withholdFromAuthor: true,
  preserve: true,
  openedBy: "anna",
  openedVia: "console",
  importedAt: null,
  tellPerson: null,
  events: [{ id: "9e6b7a6d-3c9f-4b6d-8a7f-1e5d0c9b8a7f", kind: "opened", ground: null, at: AT, effectiveAt: null, itemId: null, by: "anna", via: "console" }],
  owed: { received: false, verification: true, issuedAt: true, texts: true, document: true, holdUntil: false, tellPerson: false, scrutinyUntil: null },
  hold: null,
  mayClose: true,
  mayEvents: ["annex3_sent", "closed_without_effect"],
  mayCorrect: "entry",
  ...over,
});

const message = (over: Partial<ContactMessage> = {}): ContactMessage => ({
  id: MESSAGE,
  folder: "inbox",
  receivedAt: AT,
  seenAt: AT,
  stale: false,
  disposition: null,
  handledAt: null,
  handledBy: null,
  orders: [],
  ...over,
});

describe("an order's clock line (8.4's table)", () => {
  test("running: the deadline, the minutes left and the target, each from the clock", () => {
    expect(clockLine(summary(), START + 10 * 60_000)).toBe(
      `Due ${bothTimes(t(60))}: 50 minutes left. Target ${bothTimes(t(55))}: an image may stay in an edge cache for up to 5 minutes after the disabling.`,
    );
  });

  test("overdue, partly given effect, and stopped by an Annex III", () => {
    expect(clockLine(summary({ state: "overdue" }), START + 61 * 60_000)).toBe(`Overdue since ${bothTimes(t(60))}: 2 of 2 items are neither disabled nor closed. Act now.`);
    const partial = summary({ clock: { ...summary().clock!, itemsOpen: 1, firstEffectAt: t(20) } });
    expect(clockLine(partial, START + 30 * 60_000)).toBe(`1 of 2 items disabled, the first at ${bothTimes(t(20))}. 1 are still open: the deadline ${bothTimes(t(60))} still runs for them.`);
    const stopped = summary({ state: "stopped", clock: { ...summary().clock!, stopped: true, stoppedAt: t(10), stopGround: "force_majeure", deadlineAt: null } });
    expect(clockLine(stopped, START + 30 * 60_000)).toBe(
      `Clock stopped at ${bothTimes(t(10))}: Annex III sent (${ANNEX3_GROUND_LABELS.force_majeure}). No deadline runs. A fresh ${ORDER_RULES.hourMinutes} minutes start when the grounds cease or the clarification arrives, never the rest of the old hour.`,
    );
  });

  test("given effect: inside the hour, outside it, and while the clock was stopped", () => {
    const effect = (lastEffectAt: string, withinHour: boolean) =>
      summary({ state: "given_effect", clock: { ...summary().clock!, itemsOpen: 0, firstEffectAt: lastEffectAt, lastEffectAt, withinHour } });
    expect(clockLine(effect(t(40), true), START)).toBe(`Given effect: the last post was disabled at ${bothTimes(t(40))}, 40 minutes after the clock started: inside the hour.`);
    expect(clockLine(effect(t(75), false), START)).toBe(`Given effect: the last post was disabled at ${bothTimes(t(75))}, 75 minutes after the clock started: outside the hour.`);
    expect(clockLine(effect(t(75), true), START)).toContain("while the clock was stopped: inside the hour.");
  });

  test("no time of receipt: the deadline is unknown and the line says to act now", () => {
    const unknown = summary({ state: "unknown_deadline", clock: { ...summary().clock!, clockStart: null, deadlineAt: null, targetAt: null } });
    expect(clockLine(unknown, START)).toBe("Deadline unknown: act now. Whoever has the server records the time of receipt with staff.js order-received.");
  });

  test("a DSA order has no clock: its stated deadline or none; a closed order says when, and on which ground", () => {
    expect(clockLine(summary({ kind: "dsa_art9", state: "no_clock", clock: null }), START)).toBe("No deadline recorded: act without undue delay.");
    expect(clockLine(summary({ kind: "dsa_art10", state: "no_clock", clock: null, dueAt: t(600) }), START)).toBe(`Due ${bothTimes(t(600))}, as the order states.`);
    expect(clockLine(summary({ state: "closed", closedAt: t(5), closeGround: "withdrawn" }), START)).toBe(`Closed on ${bothTimes(t(5))} without effect: ${ORDER_GROUND_LABELS.withdrawn}.`);
    expect(clockLine(summary({ state: "closed", closedAt: t(5) }), START)).toBe(`Closed on ${bothTimes(t(5))}.`);
  });
});

describe("the list of orders (8.4)", () => {
  test("each order a block: its kind, its state, the authority and the reference as an outsider's words, its clock line, a link built from its checked id", () => {
    const hostile = summary({ authority: HOSTILE.script, reference: HOSTILE.quote });
    const out = html(<OrdersList page={{ open: [hostile], closed: [] }} now={START} onOpenOrder={noop} />);
    expect(out).toContain(HOSTILE_ESCAPED.script);
    expect(out).toContain(HOSTILE_ESCAPED.quote);
    expect(out).not.toContain("<script>");
    expect(out).toContain(`href="/orders/${ID}"`);
    expect(text(out)).toContain("As written in the order");
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Germany (DE)");
    expect(text(out)).toContain(clockLine(hostile, START));
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Open this order");
  });

  test("the closed ones under their title; nothing recorded says so; an id that is not a lower-case uuid gets no link", () => {
    const closed = text(html(<OrdersList page={{ open: [], closed: [summary({ state: "closed", closedAt: t(5) })] }} now={START} onOpenOrder={noop} />));
    expect(closed).toContain("Closed in the last 30 days");
    expect(text(html(<OrdersList page={{ open: [], closed: [] }} now={START} onOpenOrder={noop} />))).toBe("No order is recorded.");
    expect(html(<OrdersList page={{ open: [summary({ id: ID.toUpperCase() })], closed: [] }} now={START} onOpenOrder={noop} />)).not.toContain("href=");
  });
});

describe("the form Open an order (8.4)", () => {
  const filled = (over: Partial<OrderFormState> = {}): OrderFormState => ({
    ...emptyOrderForm(),
    message: "none",
    channel: "portal",
    kind: "tco_removal",
    memberState: "DE",
    authorityChoice: "bka",
    reference: "BKA-2026-1",
    links: ["https://korbat.example/p/1", "", "  https://korbat.example/p/2  "].join(String.fromCharCode(10)),
    sectionC: "no",
    ...over,
  });
  const form = (state: OrderFormState, over: Partial<Parameters<typeof OrderForm>[0]> = {}) =>
    html(<OrderForm me={{ homeState: "DE" }} form={state} messages={[message()]} busy={false} problem={null} duplicate={null} onChange={noop} onSubmit={noop} onOpenOrder={noop} {...over} />);

  test("Section C untouched is never sent: the form says no choice is made for you", () => {
    expect(orderRequest(filled({ sectionC: null }))).toEqual({ ok: false, problem: "Choose whether the author must not be told: no choice is made for you." });
  });

  test("a removal order: the register's name for the authority, the links one a line, the post kept from its author", () => {
    const sent = orderRequest(filled());
    expect(sent).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      request: {
        messageId: null,
        channel: "portal",
        kind: "tco_removal",
        memberState: "DE",
        authority: "Bundeskriminalamt (BKA)",
        reference: "BKA-2026-1",
        links: ["https://korbat.example/p/1", "https://korbat.example/p/2"],
        sectionC: false,
        emergency: false,
        withholdFromAuthor: true,
      },
    });
    // A message picked is the mailbox, and its id is sent; I cannot tell holds like a tick.
    const picked = orderRequest(filled({ message: MESSAGE, channel: null, sectionC: "unsure", authorityChoice: "other", otherAuthority: HOSTILE.script }));
    expect(picked.ok && picked.request).toMatchObject({ messageId: MESSAGE, channel: "mailbox", sectionC: true, withholdFromAuthor: true, authority: HOSTILE.script });
  });

  test("a DSA order: the withholding only when ticked or forced by Section C; an order to provide information takes no link", () => {
    const art9 = orderRequest(filled({ kind: "dsa_art9" }));
    expect(art9.ok && art9.request.withholdFromAuthor).toBe(false);
    const ticked = orderRequest(filled({ kind: "dsa_art9", withhold: true }));
    expect(ticked.ok && ticked.request.withholdFromAuthor).toBe(true);
    const silent = orderRequest(filled({ kind: "dsa_art9", sectionC: "yes" }));
    expect(silent.ok && silent.request).toMatchObject({ sectionC: true, withholdFromAuthor: true });
    const art10 = orderRequest(filled({ kind: "dsa_art10" }));
    expect(art10.ok && art10.request).toMatchObject({ links: [], withholdFromAuthor: false, emergency: false });
    // Nothing named and nothing to send: the schema refuses it.
    expect(orderRequest(filled({ links: "" })).ok).toBe(false);
  });

  test("nothing is preselected that decides anything; the home state is listed first; the message not listed warns that no deadline shows", () => {
    const empty = form(emptyOrderForm());
    expect(empty).not.toMatch(/checked=""/);
    expect(empty).toMatch(/<option value="" selected="">-<[/]option><option value="DE">Germany [(]DE[)]<[/]option>/);
    expect(text(empty)).toContain("The message is not listed");
    expect(text(empty)).not.toContain("The order is opened without a time of receipt");
    expect(text(form(emptyOrderForm("none")))).toContain("The order is opened without a time of receipt, so korbat cannot show its deadline. Act now, as if the hour were almost over.");
    expect(text(form(emptyOrderForm("none")))).toContain("How it arrived");
  });

  test("DSA Article 9: the withholding is ticked and locked while the author must not be told, or while nobody can tell; free when Section C is not set", () => {
    const box = (out: string) => out.match(/<input type="checkbox"[^>]*>/g) ?? [];
    for (const sectionC of ["yes", "unsure"] as const) {
      const locked = form(filled({ kind: "dsa_art9", sectionC }));
      expect(box(locked)).toEqual(['<input type="checkbox" disabled="" checked=""/>']);
      expect(text(locked)).toContain("An author who must not be told cannot be shown their post marked as removed.");
    }
    const free = form(filled({ kind: "dsa_art9", sectionC: "no" }));
    expect(box(free)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(box(free)[0]).not.toContain("disabled");
    expect(box(free)[0]).not.toContain("checked");
    expect(text(free)).toContain("Tick it only if the order's text says the content must be kept from its author too.");
    // The removal order's own box is the emergency, never the withholding.
    expect(text(form(filled()))).toContain("The order says it is an emergency");
    expect(text(form(filled()))).not.toContain("Withheld from the author");
  });

  test("order_exists links to the order that stands", () => {
    const out = form(filled(), { duplicate: parseOrderId(ID) as OrderId, problem: "x" });
    expect(out).toContain(`href="/orders/${ID}"`);
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Open the order that is recorded");
  });
});

describe("an order's page (8.5, Task 2's blocks)", () => {
  const me = { homeState: "DE", contactPoint: "orders@korbat.example", role: "moderator" } as const;
  const page = (order: OrderView, over: Partial<Parameters<typeof OrderPage>[0]> = {}) =>
    html(
      <OrderPage
        order={order}
        me={me}
        now={START}
        messages={[message()]}
        busy={false}
        notice={null}
        error={null}
        reasons={{}}
        links=""
        onReason={noop}
        onCloseItem={noop}
        onLinks={noop}
        onAddLinks={noop}
        onRecord={noop}
        onCorrect={noop}
        {...over}
      />,
    );

  test("the clock comes first, under the kind; block 4 only while an item names a post that can be disabled", () => {
    const out = text(page(view()));
    expect(out.indexOf(clockLine({ ...view(), items: 1 }, START))).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(out.indexOf(clockLine({ ...view(), items: 1 }, START))).toBeLessThan(out.indexOf("As written in the order"));
    expect(out).not.toContain("Disable for an order");
    expect(out).not.toContain("Extension received");
    expect(text(page(view({ items: [item({ postId: POST_A })] })))).toContain("Disable for an order");
  });

  test("block 2: a removal order is checked against the register, the authority drawn as text, with the home state's entries", () => {
    const out = html(<CheckBlock order={view({ authority: HOSTILE.script })} me={me} />);
    expect(out).toContain(HOSTILE_ESCAPED.script);
    expect(text(out)).toContain(`Before you act, check the order against your offline copy of the Commission's register: is ${HOSTILE.script} listed for Germany, and does the address`);
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Bundeskriminalamt (BKA): Bundeskriminalamt (BKA), contact point TCO@bka.bund.de");
    expect(text(out)).toContain("If you are in doubt and the hour is running, give effect");
    const dsa = text(html(<CheckBlock order={view({ kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null })} me={me} />));
    expect(dsa).toContain("No register lists who may issue such an order.");
    expect(dsa).toContain("it is given effect only after the check is recorded");
    expect(text(html(<CheckBlock order={view({ kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null, verified: true })} me={me} />))).not.toContain("given effect only after the check");
  });

  test("block 3: each link as an outsider's words; an account's and a missing link's lines; closing an open item needs a reason", () => {
    const items = [item({ link: HOSTILE.url, linkKind: "account" }), item({ id: "1f7c8b7e-4d0a-4c7e-9b8a-2f6e1d0c9b8a", position: 2, linkKind: "other" })];
    const out = page(view({ items }));
    expect(out).toContain(HOSTILE.url);
    expect(out).not.toContain(`href="${HOSTILE.url}"`);
    expect(text(out)).toContain("This link names an account, not a post.");
    expect(text(out)).toContain("This link names nothing that korbat serves.");
    expect(out.match(/<button type="button" disabled="">Close this item without effect<[/]button>/g)).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(page(view({ items }), { reasons: { [ITEM]: "no_post" } }).match(/<button type="button">Close this item without effect<[/]button>/g)).toHaveLength(1);
    // A disabled item, and an order nobody may correct, offer no closing.
    expect(text(page(view({ items: [item({ disabledAt: t(30) })] })))).toContain(`Disabled at ${bothTimes(t(30))}`);
    expect(text(page(view({ items: [item({ disabledAt: t(30) })] })))).not.toContain("Close this item without effect");
    expect(text(page(view({ mayCorrect: null })))).not.toContain("Close this item without effect");
  });

  test("block 5: only the events the database would take now; each is confirmed by the key, with its ground or message chosen first", () => {
    const out = html(<EventsBlock order={view({ mayEvents: ["annex3_sent", "clarification_received", "hold_extended"] })} messages={[message()]} busy={false} onRecord={noop} />);
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Annex III sent: Confirm with your staff key");
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Clarification received: Confirm with your staff key");
    // Task 3: an admin's "Extension received", with the message it came in and the end the database would release at.
    expect(text(out)).toContain("Extension received: Confirm with your staff key");
    expect(text(out)).toContain(`The notice is then held ${ORDER_RULES.holdExtensionDays} days longer, once.`);
    expect(text(out)).toContain(ANNEX3_GROUND_LABELS.insufficient_information);
    expect(text(out)).toContain(`Received ${bothTimes(AT)}, Inbox`);
    expect(text(out)).not.toContain("Close without effect");
    expect(out.match(/<button type="button" disabled="">/g)).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(html(<EventsBlock order={view({ mayEvents: [] })} messages={[]} busy={false} onRecord={noop} />)).toBe("");
  });

  test("block 6: the forms' values as text, the time in UTC with its offset, the contact point and the copy from the home state's facts", () => {
    expect(utcWithOffset("2026-10-10T01:00:12.345Z")).toBe("2026-10-10 01:00:12 +00:00");
    const stopped = view({ clock: { ...summary().clock!, stopped: true, stoppedAt: t(10), stopGround: "manifest_error" } });
    const out = text(html(<FormsBlock order={stopped} me={me} />));
    expect(out).toContain("Reference of the removal order: BKA-2026-1");
    expect(out).toContain("Issuing authority: Bundeskriminalamt (BKA), Germany (DE)");
    expect(out).toContain("Time and date of receipt of removal order: 2026-10-16 02:00:00 +00:00");
    expect(out).toContain(`Reason: ${ANNEX3_GROUND_LABELS.manifest_error}`);
    expect(out).toContain("Contact point: orders@korbat.example");
    expect(out).toContain("Copy to: TCO@bka.bund.de");
    expect(text(html(<FormsBlock order={view()} me={{ homeState: null, contactPoint: null }} />))).toContain("Contact point: not filled in: see the README, Before going public");
    expect(html(<FormsBlock order={view({ kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null })} me={me} />)).toBe("");
  });

  test("block 7: what the command line owes, one line each; nothing owed, no block", () => {
    const out = text(html(<OwedBlock order={view()} />));
    expect(out).toContain("The check is not recorded (staff.js order-verify).");
    expect(out).toContain("The order's own date and time are not recorded (staff.js order-issued).");
    expect(out).toContain("The authority's reasons and remedies are not recorded (staff.js order-texts).");
    expect(out).toContain("The document's digest is not recorded (staff.js order-document).");
    const none = { received: false, verification: false, issuedAt: false, texts: false, document: false, holdUntil: false, tellPerson: false, scrutinyUntil: null };
    expect(html(<OwedBlock order={view({ owed: none })} />)).toBe("");
    const dsa = text(html(<OwedBlock order={view({ kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null, owed: { ...none, texts: true } })} />));
    expect(dsa).toContain("Record the authority's reasons, its remedies and the order's territorial scope before you give effect");
  });

  test("block 8: told at the effect, or held: with no end, until the computed end, released", () => {
    expect(text(html(<NoticeBlock order={view({ items: [item({ disabledAt: t(30) })] })} />))).toContain(`Told at ${bothTimes(t(30))}.`);
    const hold = { until: null, basis: "regulation", open: true, extended: false, endedAt: null, endReason: null, releasedAt: null, noticesHeld: 1 } as const;
    expect(text(html(<NoticeBlock order={view({ sectionC: true, hold })} />))).toContain("Held with no end");
    const until = text(html(<NoticeBlock order={view({ sectionC: true, hold: { ...hold, open: false, until: t(60_000), releasedAt: t(60_000) } })} />));
    expect(until).toContain(`Held until ${bothTimes(t(60_000))}: the end the database computes from the Regulation's six weeks, counted from the receipt.`);
    expect(until).toContain(`Released at ${bothTimes(t(60_000))}.`);
    expect(html(<NoticeBlock order={view()} />)).toBe("");
  });

  test("block 9: the events newest first, each with who wrote it, a handle as text", () => {
    const events: OrderView["events"] = [
      { id: "9e6b7a6d-3c9f-4b6d-8a7f-1e5d0c9b8a7f", kind: "opened", ground: null, at: AT, effectiveAt: null, itemId: null, by: HOSTILE.script, via: "console" },
      { id: "0a7c8b7e-4d0a-4c7e-9b8a-2f6e1d0c9b8b", kind: "annex3_sent", ground: "force_majeure", at: t(10), effectiveAt: null, itemId: null, by: null, via: "cli" },
    ];
    const out = html(<EventsList order={view({ events })} />);
    expect(out).toContain(HOSTILE_ESCAPED.script);
    const read = text(out);
    expect(read.indexOf(`${bothTimes(t(10))}: Annex III sent: ${ANNEX3_GROUND_LABELS.force_majeure}`)).toBeLessThan(read.indexOf(`${bothTimes(AT)}: Order opened`));
    expect(read).toContain("command line");
    expect(read).toContain(`@${HOSTILE.script}, console`);
  });

  test("block 10: the rule decides the controls; a correction sends what changes and nothing else", () => {
    expect(html(<CorrectBlock order={view({ mayCorrect: null })} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />)).toBe("");
    const caution = text(html(<CorrectBlock order={view({ mayCorrect: "caution" })} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />));
    expect(caution).toContain("Section C is ticked: the author must not be told");
    expect(caution).not.toContain("Issuing state");
    expect(html(<CorrectBlock order={view({ mayCorrect: "caution", sectionC: true })} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />)).toBe("");
    const entry = html(<CorrectBlock order={view()} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />);
    expect(entry).toMatch(/<button type="button" disabled="">Correct<[/]button>/);
    // An order opened from a message keeps its channel: the field is offered only without one.
    expect(text(entry)).not.toContain("How it arrived");
    expect(text(html(<CorrectBlock order={view({ messageId: null, channel: "portal" })} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />))).toContain("How it arrived");
    expect(text(html(<CorrectBlock order={view({ mayCorrect: "admin" })} busy={false} onCorrect={noop} />))).toContain("Correct: Confirm with your staff key");
    const order = view();
    const same = { kind: order.kind, memberState: order.memberState, authority: order.authority, reference: order.reference, channel: order.channel, sectionC: order.sectionC, emergency: order.emergency, withholdFromAuthor: order.withholdFromAuthor };
    expect(changedFacts(order, same)).toEqual({});
    expect(changedFacts(order, { ...same, reference: "BKA-2026-2", channel: "post" })).toEqual({ reference: "BKA-2026-2" });
    expect(changedFacts(view({ messageId: null }), { ...same, channel: "post" })).toEqual({ channel: "post" });
  });
});

describe("block 4, Disable for an order (8.5, Task 3)", () => {
  const ids = ["1a000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001", "1a000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002", "1a000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"];
  const posts = [POST_C, POST_A, POST_B];
  const three = () => ids.map((id, i) => item({ id, position: i + 1, postId: posts[i]!, link: `https://korbat.example/p/${i + 1}` }));
  const block = (order: OrderView, over: Partial<Parameters<typeof EffectBlock>[0]> = {}) =>
    html(<EffectBlock order={order} role="moderator" ticks={{}} urgent={false} busy={false} effected={null} onUrgent={noop} onEffect={noop} {...over} />);
  const me = { homeState: "DE", contactPoint: "orders@korbat.example", role: "moderator" } as const;
  const page = (order: OrderView, over: Partial<Parameters<typeof OrderPage>[0]> = {}) =>
    html(
      <OrderPage
        order={order}
        me={me}
        now={START}
        messages={[]}
        busy={false}
        notice={null}
        error={null}
        reasons={{}}
        links=""
        onReason={noop}
        onCloseItem={noop}
        onLinks={noop}
        onAddLinks={noop}
        onRecord={noop}
        onCorrect={noop}
        {...over}
      />,
    );

    expect(out).toContain("preserved for six months from now");

    expect(params).toEqual({
      kind: "tco_removal",
      memberState: "DE",
      authority: order.authority,
      reference: order.reference,
      sectionC: false,
      emergency: false,
      withholdFromAuthor: true,
      urgent: false,
      items: [
        { itemId: ids[1], postId: POST_A },
        { itemId: ids[2], postId: POST_B },
        { itemId: ids[0], postId: POST_C },
      ],
    });

    expect(OrderEffectedParams.safeParse(params).success).toBe(true);
    // An item unticked by the person leaves the params; one in force or closed is never offered.
    expect(isTicked(order, { [ids[0]!]: false }, ids[0]!)).toBe(false);
    expect(effectable(view({ items: [item({ postId: POST_A, inForce: true }), item({ id: ids[1]!, postId: POST_B, closedAt: AT, closedReason: "not_named" })] }))).toEqual([]);

    expect(out).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectMax);

    // Ticking an eleventh greys the button: the database takes ten an action.
    const over = block(view({ items: many }), { ticks: { [many[ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction]!.id]: true } });
    expect(over).toMatch(/<button type="button" disabled="">Disable 11 posts/);
  });

  test("the silence: a removal order with Section C is held until the computed end; a DSA order's until the authority's time, or with no end", () => {
    const hold = { until: t(60_000), basis: "regulation", open: false, extended: false, endedAt: null, endReason: null, releasedAt: null, noticesHeld: 0 } as const;
    const held = text(block(view({ items: three(), sectionC: true, hold })));

    expect(dsaHeld).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectHeldDsa(bothTimes(t(60_000))));
    expect(dsaHeld).not.toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectPreserve);
    expect(text(block(view({ ...dsa, items: three(), withholdFromAuthor: true, hold: { ...hold, basis: "authority", open: true, until: null } })))).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectHeldOpen);
    // A DSA order that does not withhold removes, as a korbat rule does, and tells the author.
    const removed = text(block(view({ ...dsa, items: three(), withholdFromAuthor: false })));
    expect(removed).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectRemoved);
    expect(removed).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectTold);
    expect(removed).not.toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectWhat);
  });

  test("a DSA Article 9 order that is not verified: no button for a moderator; an admin ticks urgent first, and the params carry it", () => {
    const order = view({ kind: "dsa_art9", clock: null, verified: false, preserve: false, items: three() });
    const moderator = text(block(order));
    expect(moderator).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.verifyFirst);
    expect(moderator).not.toContain("confirm with your staff key");
    const admin = block(order, { role: "admin" });
    expect(text(admin)).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectUrgent);
    expect(admin).toMatch(/<button type="button" disabled="">Disable 3 posts/);
    expect(block(order, { role: "admin", urgent: true })).toMatch(/<button type="button">Disable 3 posts/);
    expect(effectParamsOf(order, ids, true).urgent).toBe(true);
  });

  test("after an effect: the check from outside, each address as text; [effect.rest] while items are open; an item's preservation, reinstatement and case", () => {
    const disabled = item({ id: ids[0]!, postId: POST_A, link: HOSTILE.script, inForce: true, disabledAt: t(20), caseId: CASE, decisionId: CASE, preserveUntil: t(300_000) });
    const order = view({ items: [disabled, item({ id: ids[1]!, position: 2, postId: POST_B })], clock: { ...summary().clock!, itemsOpen: 1, firstEffectAt: t(20) } });
    const out = block(order, { effected: { at: t(20), links: [HOSTILE.script] } });
    expect(text(out)).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.checkOutside(bothTimes(t(20)), 1));
    expect(out).toContain(HOSTILE_ESCAPED.script);
    expect(out).not.toContain("<a");
    expect(text(out)).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.effectRest(1, bothTimes(t(60))));
    const read = page(order, { onOpenCase: noop });
    expect(text(read)).toContain(`Preserved until ${bothTimes(t(300_000))}`);
    expect(read).toContain(`href="/cases/${CASE}"`);
    const reinstated = text(page(view({ items: [item({ postId: POST_A, disabledAt: t(20), reinstatedAt: t(40), reinstatedGround: "withdrawn" })] })));
    expect(reinstated).toContain(`Reinstated at ${bothTimes(t(40))}: ${ORDER_GROUND_LABELS.withdrawn}`);
    expect(text(page(view({ items: [item({ postId: POST_A, inForce: true, disabledAt: t(20), noEffect: "already" })] })))).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.alreadyNow);    // Task 4 ([item.erased]): the preservation's end erased the content; the day is UTC's, and "Preserved until" goes.
    const erasedAt = "2027-04-17T00:10:00.000Z";
    const erased = text(page(view({ items: [item({ postId: POST_A, inForce: true, disabledAt: t(20), preserveUntil: t(-10), preserveEndedAt: erasedAt, erasedAt })] })));
    expect(erased).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.erased("2027-04-17"));
    expect(erased).not.toContain("Preserved until");
    expect(text(read)).not.toContain("the content was erased");
  });

  test("block 8's [hold.warn] in the last days before a running hold's end, and not before", () => {
    const hold = { until: t(3 * 24 * 60), basis: "regulation", open: false, extended: false, endedAt: null, endReason: null, releasedAt: null, noticesHeld: 1 } as const;
    expect(text(html(<NoticeBlock order={view({ sectionC: true, hold })} now={START} />))).toContain(ORDER_WORDS.order.holdWarn(bothTimes(t(3 * 24 * 60))));
    const later = { ...hold, until: t((ORDER_RULES.holdWarningDays + 1) * 24 * 60) };
    expect(text(html(<NoticeBlock order={view({ sectionC: true, hold: later })} now={START} />))).not.toContain("is released on");
    expect(text(html(<NoticeBlock order={view({ sectionC: true, hold: { ...hold, releasedAt: t(10) } })} now={START} />))).not.toContain("is released on");
  });
});

import { createHash, randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";

import { loadConfig } from "../../src/config";
import { STAFF_USAGE, runStaffCommand } from "../../src/cli/staff";
import { deciderWorld, type DeciderWorld, type RealStaff } from "./moderation-decide";
import { CHANNEL_TABLES, imagePost, newPostRow, newTestStaff, removeDecided, removeFixtures, rowCounts, staffProfile, type TestStaff } from "./moderation-fixtures";
import { noticesWorld, type NoticesWorld } from "./notices-harness";
import { closeNotifyFixtures, contactMessageForTest, removeMessages } from "./notify-fixtures";

import { newProfile } from "./social-fixtures";

vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 90_000 });
