```ts
    test("one function writes a seal's list, and one the moderation columns of posts and images", async () => {
      const all = await functions();
      const matching = (statement: RegExp) => all.filter((f) => statement.test(f.definition)).map((f) => f.name);
      // A statement that writes the table, as SQL may spell it: an insert, an update, a delete or a merge, the name bare or
      // schema-qualified, quoted or not; for a column, an update, a merge or an insert that updates on a conflict.
      const sealList = /(insert\s+into|update|delete\s+from|merge\s+into)\s+(only\s+)?("?public"?\s*\.\s*)?"?seal_posts"?(?![\w"])/i;
      const imageState = /(update\s+(only\s+)?|merge\s+into\s+(only\s+)?|insert\s+into\s+)("?public"?\s*\.\s*)?"?post_media"?(?![\w"])[^;]*\bset\b[^;]*"?moderation_state"?\s*=/i;
      const postColumns = /(update\s+(only\s+)?|merge\s+into\s+(only\s+)?|insert\s+into\s+)("?public"?\s*\.\s*)?"?posts"?(?![\w"])[^;]*\bset\b[^;]*"?(moderation_level|state|erased_at)"?\s*=/i;
      const calls = /\bmoderation_apply\s*\(/i;
      expect(matching(sealList)).toEqual(["public.decision_actions_apply"]);
      expect(matching(imageState)).toEqual(["public.moderation_apply"]);
      // Of the three columns of posts, the level and the state are moderation_apply's alone; the erasure mark is the R4
      // redaction's and (3f, 0029) the end of an order's preservation's.
      expect(matching(postColumns)).toEqual(["public.moderation_apply", "public.order_preservation_end", "public.redact_r4_body"]);
      const written = (table: string, columns: string) =>
        new RegExp(String.raw`(update\s+(only\s+)?|merge\s+into\s+(only\s+)?|insert\s+into\s+)("?public"?\s*[.]\s*)?"?${table}"?(?![\w"])[^;]*\bset\b[^;]*"?(${columns})"?\s*=`, "i");
      const postLevel = written("posts", "moderation_level|state");
      const postErased = written("posts", "erased_at");
      const imageErased = written("post_media", "erased_at");
      const snapshotErased = written("evidence_snapshots", "erased_at");
      expect(matching(postLevel)).toEqual(["public.moderation_apply"]);
      expect(matching(postErased)).toEqual(["public.order_preservation_end", "public.redact_r4_body"]);
      expect(matching(imageErased)).toEqual(["public.order_preservation_end", "public.redact_r4_body"]);
      // Gate E: one function writes a snapshot's erasure, no function deletes a snapshot, and that one function is called
      // by the two erasures of 0018 and by nothing else.
      expect(matching(snapshotErased)).toEqual(["public.erase_snapshots"]);
      expect(matching(/delete\s+from\s+(only\s+)?("?public"?\s*[.]\s*)?"?evidence_snapshots"?(?![\w"])/i)).toEqual([]);
      expect(matching(/\berase_snapshots\s*\(/i)).toEqual(["public.erase_case_evidence", "public.erase_snapshots", "public.order_preservation_end", "public.redact_r4_body"]);
      // The writer is called by the two triggers that follow a stored decision and a stored measure, by the R4 redaction,
      // and (3f) by order_correct, whose changed withholding derives the level of its measures' posts again.
      // And (3f, 0029) the end of an order's preservation, by which an erased post is removed for good.
      expect(matching(calls)).toEqual(["public.decision_actions_apply", "public.decisions_apply", "public.moderation_apply", "public.order_correct", "public.order_preservation_end", "public.redact_r4_body"]);
      for (const statement of [
        "UPDATE public.evidence_snapshots s SET erased_at = now(), body = NULL",
        'update only "public"."evidence_snapshots" set "erased_at" = $1',
        "merge into evidence_snapshots s using v on s.id = v.id when matched then update set erased_at = now()",
      ]) {
        expect(snapshotErased.test(statement), statement).toBe(true);
      }
      expect(snapshotErased.test("select 1 from public.evidence_snapshots s where s.erased_at is null; update public.staff_texts t set erased_at = now()")).toBe(false);
      expect(imageErased.test("UPDATE public.post_media m SET erased_at = coalesce(m.erased_at, now())")).toBe(true);
      expect(imageErased.test("UPDATE public.media_holds h SET released_at = now(); select m.erased_at = now() from public.post_media m")).toBe(false);
      expect(postErased.test("UPDATE public.posts p SET body = '', erased_at = now()")).toBe(true);
      expect(postErased.test("UPDATE public.posts p SET moderation_level = v.level WHERE p.erased_at IS NOT NULL")).toBe(false);
      // Each search finds such a statement in every form, and no other statement.
      for (const statement of [
        "INSERT INTO public.seal_posts (action_id, post_id, images)",
        'insert into "public"."seal_posts" (action_id)',
        "update seal_posts s set images = 1",
        'DELETE FROM ONLY "seal_posts" s',
        "merge into public.seal_posts s using listed l on l.post_id = s.post_id",
      ]) {
        expect(sealList.test(statement), statement).toBe(true);
      }
      expect(sealList.test("select 1 from public.seal_posts s; delete from public.seal_posts_kept")).toBe(false);
      for (const statement of [
        "UPDATE public.post_media i SET status = 'ready', moderation_state = v.state",
        'update only "public"."post_media" set "moderation_state" = $1',
        "insert into post_media (id) values ($1) on conflict (id) do update set moderation_state = excluded.moderation_state",
        "merge into public.post_media m using v on m.id = v.id when matched then update set moderation_state = v.state",
      ]) {
        expect(imageState.test(statement), statement).toBe(true);
      }
      expect(imageState.test("UPDATE public.post_media m SET hold_until = latest WHERE m.id = NEW.media_id; SELECT moderation_state = 'x'")).toBe(false);
      expect(imageState.test("insert into public.post_media (owner_id, moderation_state) values ($1, 'visible')")).toBe(false);
      for (const statement of [
        "update posts set body = '', state = 'removed'",
        'UPDATE "public"."posts" p SET "moderation_level" = v.level',
        "insert into public.posts (id) values ($1) on conflict (id) do update set erased_at = now()",
        "merge into posts p using v on p.id = v.id when matched then update set state = v.state",
      ]) {
        expect(postColumns.test(statement), statement).toBe(true);
      }
      expect(postColumns.test("insert into public.posts (author_id, body, state) values ($1, $2, 'visible')")).toBe(false);
      expect(postColumns.test("update public.posts_archive set state = 'removed'")).toBe(false);
    });

    test("3f's writers (0027_orders; design, section 6.7): who writes a decision's informed_at, an order's row, its events, an item's closing and a measure's withholding", async () => {
      const all = await functions();
      const writing = (pattern: RegExp) => all.filter((f) => pattern.test(f.definition)).map((f) => f.name);
      // A decision's informed_at: decisions_record forces it at the insert; order_correct writes it, and only to null; and
      // (Task 3, 0028_orders_ledger) order_notices_release tells a held decision, while the two later writers of a
      // decision's mail (decisions_apply's ended seals, decision_actions_check's step 11) hold a telling on a held post.
      expect(writing(/[^a-z_]informed_at (:)?= /)).toEqual(["public.decision_actions_check", "public.decisions_apply", "public.decisions_record", "public.order_correct", "public.order_notices_release"]);
      expect(all.find((f) => f.name === "public.order_notices_release")!.definition).toContain("SET informed_at = clock_timestamp(), author_mail = 'pending'");
      expect(all.find((f) => f.name === "public.order_correct")!.definition).toMatch(/SET informed_at = NULL, author_mail = 'none'/);
      // An order's row: written by order_event_record and order_correct alone (and the command line, as the migrator).
      // Task 4 (0029_orders_retention): erase_order_records deletes it with its events and items once its records are due.
      expect(writing(/(UPDATE|INSERT INTO|DELETE FROM) public[.]legal_orders /i)).toEqual(["public.erase_order_records", "public.order_correct", "public.order_event_record"]);
      // Task 3: the ledger's events (effect_given, reinstated) and the release's notice_released.
      // Task 4: the end of a preservation's preservation_ended, by the system.
      expect(writing(/INSERT INTO public[.]legal_order_events/i)).toEqual(["public.decision_actions_apply", "public.order_correct", "public.order_event_record", "public.order_notices_release", "public.order_preservation_end"]);
      // An item's closing: order_correct closes it; an effect clears it (decision_actions_apply).
      expect(writing(/closed_reason = /)).toEqual(["public.decision_actions_apply", "public.order_correct"]);
      // An item's preservation (design, section 6.7): set and ended by the ledger (decision_actions_apply) and a correction
      // (order_correct), and ended by time by order_preservation_end (Task 4, 0029) alone.
      expect(writing(/preserve_(until|ended_at) = /)).toEqual(["public.decision_actions_apply", "public.order_correct", "public.order_preservation_end"]);
      expect(writing(/withhold_author = /)).toEqual(["public.order_correct"]);
      // The two definer functions pin public alone and name auth's table in full, as every function the migrator owns does.
      for (const name of ["public.order_correct", "public.order_event_record", "public.legal_order_events_confirmed"]) {
        const f = all.find((found) => found.name === name)!;
        expect([f.definer, f.config], name).toEqual([true, ["search_path=public, pg_temp"]]);
      }
      // No function of 0027 holds an interval literal or a number of order_rules(): each is read from there.
      // Nor any of 0029_orders_retention.
      for (const name of ["public.order_hold_end", "public.order_hold_until", "public.order_preserve_until", "public.order_event_record", "public.order_correct", "public.legal_orders_insert",
                          "public.order_preservation_end", "public.order_records_due", "public.erase_order_records", "public.delete_contact_messages"]) {
        expect(all.find((f) => f.name === name)!.definition, name).not.toMatch(/interval '/i);
      }
      const views = (await otherDefinitions()).filter((d) => d.kind === "view" && d.name === "legal_order_clock");
      expect(views.map((v) => /interval '/i.test(v.definition))).toEqual([false]);
    });

    test("measures_in_force runs with its reader's rights and names exactly the contracts' measures", async () => {
      const [view] = await apiDb.execute<{ options: string[] | null; definition: string }>(sql`select c.reloptions as options, pg_get_viewdef(c.oid) as definition from pg_class c where c.oid = 'public.measures_in_force'::regclass`);
      expect(view!.options).toEqual(["security_invoker=true"]);
      const measures = ACTION_KINDS.filter((kind) => MEASURES[kind].lifts === null);
      // 3e: the view names its kinds as text (enum-literals.test.ts: a value 3e added cannot be an enum literal in the
      // migration that adds it), and the seal's own literal as the enum; both forms are read.
      const named = [...view!.definition.matchAll(/'([a-z_]+)'::(?:action_kind|text)/g)].map((m) => m[1]);
      expect([...new Set(named)].sort()).toEqual([...measures].sort());
      // No value of post_state: a migration that adds one cannot change what "in force" means.
      expect(view!.definition).not.toMatch(/post_state/);
      const columns = await apiDb.execute<{ name: string }>(sql`select attname::text as name from pg_attribute where attrelid = 'public.measures_in_force'::regclass and attnum > 0 order by attnum`);
      expect(columns.map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(["id", "kind", "post_id", "media_id", "subject_account_id", "decision_id", "decision_kind", "case_id"]);
    });
  });

  describe("each CHECK written from a contracts constant holds exactly that constant's values", () => {
    /** The quoted values of one CHECK, as the migrated database defines it. */
    const checkValues = async (table: string, name: string) => [...(await checkDefinition(table, name)).matchAll(/'([^']*)'/g)].map((m) => m[1]!).sort();
    /** The one number of a length CHECK. */
    async function checkBound(table: string, name: string): Promise<number> {
      const definition = await checkDefinition(table, name);
      const numbers = [...definition.matchAll(/<= (\d+)/g)].map((m) => Number(m[1]));
      expect(numbers, definition).toHaveLength(1);
      return numbers[0]!;
    }

    test("the 16 Transparency Database categories, on intakes and on decisions", async () => {
      expect(await checkValues("intakes", "intakes_category")).toEqual([...TDB_CATEGORIES].sort());
      expect(await checkValues("decisions", "decisions_category")).toEqual([...TDB_CATEGORIES].sort());
    });

    test("the CSAM path's keywords on intakes, and a decision's keywords", async () => {
      const keywords = Object.values(CSAM_KEYWORDS).filter((keyword): keyword is NonNullable<typeof keyword> => keyword !== null);
      expect(await checkValues("intakes", "intakes_category_keyword")).toEqual([...keywords].sort());
      expect(await checkValues("decisions", "decisions_category_keyword")).toEqual([...DECISION_KEYWORDS].sort());
    });

    test("the six rules, on intakes and on decisions", async () => {
      expect(await checkValues("intakes", "intakes_rule_id")).toEqual([...RULE_IDS]);
      expect(await checkValues("decisions", "decisions_rule_id")).toEqual([...RULE_IDS]);
    });

    test("the bounds of a notice's two texts", async () => {
      expect(await checkBound("intakes", "intakes_explanation_len")).toBe(NOTICE_LIMITS.explanationMax);
      expect(await checkBound("intakes", "intakes_cited_law_len")).toBe(NOTICE_LIMITS.citedLawMax);
    });

    test("the ledger's kinds are the contracts' action kinds, in their order, the two of an order's measure last", async () => {
      const rows = await apiDb.execute<{ label: string }>(sql`select e.enumlabel::text as label from pg_enum e where e.enumtypid = 'public.action_kind'::regtype order by e.enumsortorder`);
      // 3f: the migration orders adds them; they joined ACTION_KINDS with the task that gives effect to an order (Task 3).
      expect(rows.map((row) => row.label)).toEqual([...ACTION_KINDS]);
      expect(ACTION_KINDS.slice(-2)).toEqual([...ORDER_ACTION_KINDS]);
    });

    test("post_state has its four values and 3f's disabled: a seal is a state of images, a disabling one of posts", async () => {
      const rows = await apiDb.execute<{ label: string }>(sql`select e.enumlabel::text as label from pg_enum e where e.enumtypid = 'public.post_state'::regtype order by e.enumsortorder`);
      expect(rows.map((row) => row.label)).toEqual(["visible", "withheld", "removed", "deleted_by_author", "disabled"]);
    });

    test("no check lets a row through on a null: the database holds the null-safe forms", async () => {
      // A CHECK passes when its expression is null. These five are written so that it never is. PostgreSQL stores
      // "is not distinct from" as the negation of "is distinct from" and prints it that way.
      expect(await checkDefinition("intake_items", "intake_items_case")).toContain("(NOT (outcome IS DISTINCT FROM 'not_available'::item_outcome))");
      expect(await checkDefinition("decisions", "decisions_keyword")).toContain("(NOT (ground IS DISTINCT FROM 'illegal'::decision_ground))");
      expect(await checkDefinition("intake_items", "intake_items_statement")).toContain("statement_digest IS NOT NULL");
      expect(await checkDefinition("appeals", "appeals_statement")).toContain("statement_digest IS NOT NULL");
      expect(await checkDefinition("staff_texts", "staff_texts_digest")).toContain("salt ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'");
    });
  });

  describe("appeal_deadline", () => {
    test("it equals the contracts' appealDeadline on every month end of two years, a leap year among them, and on the days around them", async () => {
      // The last three days of each month of 2027 and 2028 (2028 has a 29 February) and the first of the next, at three times of day.
      // Both times as the text toISOString writes, so that nothing depends on how the driver reads a timestamp.
      const rows = await apiDb.execute<{ informed: string; deadline: string }>(sql`
        select to_char(t at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as informed, to_char(public.appeal_deadline(t) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as deadline
          from generate_series('2027-01-01'::timestamp, '2028-12-01'::timestamp, interval '1 month') month,
               generate_series(-3, 0) shift,
               unnest(array[interval '0 hours', interval '12 hours 30 minutes 15.25 seconds', interval '23 hours 59 minutes 59.999 seconds']) time_of_day,
               lateral (select (month + interval '1 month' + make_interval(days => shift) + time_of_day) at time zone 'UTC' as t) s
         order by 1`);
      expect(rows).toHaveLength(24 * 4 * 3);
      for (const row of rows) expect(appealDeadline(new Date(row.informed)).toISOString(), row.informed).toBe(row.deadline);
      // The set really holds the clamp: 31 August 2027 is due on the leap day.
      const august = rows.find((row) => row.informed === "2027-08-31T00:00:00.000Z");
      expect(august?.deadline).toBe("2028-02-29T00:00:00.000Z");
    });

    test("it does not depend on the session's time zone", async () => {
      const deadlines = await withLockTimeout(apiDb, async (tx) => {
        const read = async () =>
          (await tx.execute<{ d: string }>(sql`select to_char(public.appeal_deadline('2027-08-30T23:30:00Z'::timestamptz) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as d`))[0]!.d;
        // 30 August, 23:30 UTC, is already the 31st at +14 and still the 30th at -7: a deadline computed in the session's zone
        // would differ between the two, and from UTC's 29 February.
        await tx.execute(sql`set local time zone 'Pacific/Kiritimati'`);
        const east = await read();
        await tx.execute(sql`set local time zone 'America/Los_Angeles'`);
        return [east, await read()];
      });
      expect(deadlines).toEqual(["2028-02-29T23:30:00.000Z", "2028-02-29T23:30:00.000Z"]);
    });
  });

  describe("the forced columns ignore what an insert supplies", () => {

            returning *, (opened_at = now()) as opened_now`);
          expect(row).toMatchObject({ target_type: "post", target_id: targetId, lane: 2, intake_seq: 0, answered_seq: 0, state_version: 0, oldest_open_at: null, last_decided_at: null, closed_at: null, opened_now: true });

            values ('user', ${newRef()}, ${input.lookupHash ?? null}, ${input.channel ?? "signed_in"}::intake_channel, ${input.reporterId ?? null}::uuid, ${input.contactId ?? null}::uuid, ${input.ruleId ?? null},
                    ${input.allegesIllegal ?? false}, ${input.csam ?? false}, ${input.category ?? TC}, ${input.explanation ?? null}, ${input.bonaFide ?? false},
                    '2001-01-01T00:00:00Z', 'sent', '2001-01-01T00:00:00Z', null)
            returning receipt, receipt_sent_at, erased_at, (received_at = now()) as now`);
        const cases: [string, IntakeInput, string][] = [

          ["a signed-out rule report without a contact", { channel: "signed_out", lookupHash: hex64(), ruleId: "R3" }, "none"],

          values (${caseId}::uuid, ${ada.id}::uuid, 'note', 'a note', ${salt}, ${await textDigest(salt, "a note")}, '2001-01-01T00:00:00Z', null, '2001-01-01T00:00:00Z')
          returning decision_id, confirmed_at, (created_at = now()) as now`);

  describe("the checks of intakes", () => {
    /** One test's intakes, all in a transaction that is rolled back: each insert in a savepoint, its refusal's message or null. */
    const intakes = (fn: (refusal: (input: IntakeInput) => Promise<string | null>, ada: { id: string }) => Promise<void>) =>
      rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {
        const ada = await profile(tx);
        await fn(async (input) => (await within(tx, (sp) => insertIntake(sp, input)))?.message ?? null, ada);
      });

    test("a ground is needed: a rule, an allegation of illegality or the CSAM path", async () => {
      await intakes(async (refusal, ada) => {
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id })).toMatch(/intakes_has_ground/);
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id, ruleId: "R7" })).toMatch(/intakes_rule_id/);
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id, ruleId: "R1" })).toBeNull();
      });
    });

    test("a notice of illegality carries its explanation and its good-faith statement; the CSAM path needs neither", async () => {
      await intakes(async (refusal, ada) => {
        const illegal = { reporterId: ada.id, allegesIllegal: true, category: SPEECH };
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal })).toMatch(/intakes_illegal_elements/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal, explanation: "why" })).toMatch(/intakes_illegal_elements/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal, bonaFide: true })).toMatch(/intakes_illegal_elements/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal, explanation: "why", bonaFide: true })).toBeNull();
        // A CSAM intake alleges illegality with neither, and with no keyword (the "abuse" choice) or one of the three.
        const csam = { channel: "signed_out" as const, csam: true, allegesIllegal: true, category: MINORS };
        expect(await refusal({ ...csam, lookupHash: hex64() })).toBeNull();
        expect(await refusal({ ...csam, lookupHash: hex64(), categoryKeyword: "KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS" })).toBeNull();
        expect(await refusal({ ...csam, lookupHash: hex64(), categoryKeyword: "KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT" })).toMatch(/intakes_category_keyword/);
      });
    });

    test("the CSAM path stores no account and no contact, and is always about the protection of minors", async () => {
      await intakes(async (refusal, ada) => {
        const csam = { csam: true, allegesIllegal: true, category: MINORS };
        expect(await refusal({ ...csam, channel: "signed_in", reporterId: ada.id, lookupHash: hex64() })).toMatch(/intakes_csam/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...csam, channel: "signed_out", contactId: randomUUID(), lookupHash: hex64() })).toMatch(/intakes_csam/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...csam, channel: "signed_out", category: SPEECH, lookupHash: hex64() })).toMatch(/intakes_csam/);
        // Signed in, it still stores no account: the channel is kept, the reporter is not, and the token's hash is needed.
        expect(await refusal({ ...csam, channel: "signed_in", lookupHash: hex64() })).toBeNull();
        expect(await refusal({ ...csam, channel: "signed_in" })).toMatch(/intakes_lookup/);
      });
    });

    test("a user never reports under R2, signed in or out; a moderator's finding may cite it", async () => {
      await intakes(async (refusal, ada) => {
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id, ruleId: "R2" })).toMatch(/intakes_r2_finding_only/);
        expect(await refusal({ channel: "signed_out", lookupHash: hex64(), ruleId: "R2" })).toMatch(/intakes_r2_finding_only/);
        expect(await refusal({ kind: "finding", channel: "staff", findingBy: ada.id, ruleId: "R2", category: MINORS })).toBeNull();
      });
    });

    test("a finding names its finder, comes through the staff channel and never alleges illegality", async () => {
      await intakes(async (refusal, ada) => {
        const finding = { kind: "finding" as const, channel: "staff" as const, findingBy: ada.id, ruleId: "R3" };
        expect(await refusal(finding)).toBeNull();
        expect(await refusal({ ...finding, allegesIllegal: true, category: SPEECH, explanation: "why", bonaFide: true })).toMatch(/intakes_finding_legal/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...finding, findingBy: null })).toMatch(/intakes_finding/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...finding, channel: "signed_in" })).toMatch(/intakes_finding/);
        expect(await refusal({ kind: "user", channel: "staff", ruleId: "R3" })).toMatch(/intakes_finding/);
        expect(await refusal({ kind: "user", channel: "signed_in", findingBy: ada.id, ruleId: "R3" })).toMatch(/intakes_finding/);
      });
    });

    test("a contact belongs to a signed-out notice, a reporter to a signed-in one, and a token's hash to a signed-out or CSAM one", async () => {
      await intakes(async (refusal, ada) => {
        expect(await refusal({ channel: "signed_in", reporterId: ada.id, contactId: randomUUID(), ruleId: "R1" })).toMatch(/intakes_contact_signed_out/);
        expect(await refusal({ channel: "signed_out", reporterId: ada.id, lookupHash: hex64(), ruleId: "R1" })).toMatch(/intakes_reporter_signed_in/);
        expect(await refusal({ channel: "signed_out", ruleId: "R1" })).toMatch(/intakes_lookup/);
        expect(await refusal({ channel: "signed_in", reporterId: ada.id, lookupHash: hex64(), ruleId: "R1" })).toMatch(/intakes_lookup/);
        const hash = hex64();
        expect(await refusal({ channel: "signed_out", lookupHash: hash, ruleId: "R1" })).toBeNull();
        expect(await refusal({ channel: "signed_out", lookupHash: hash, ruleId: "R1" })).toMatch(/intakes_lookup_hash_unique/);
      });
    });

    test("the category is one of the 16, never the terms-and-conditions one on an allegation of illegality; the texts are bounded; the reference has its form", async () => {
      await intakes(async (refusal, ada) => {
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id, ruleId: "R1", category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PORNOGRAPHY_OR_SEXUALIZED_CONTENT" })).toMatch(/intakes_category/);
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id, allegesIllegal: true, category: TC, explanation: "why", bonaFide: true })).toMatch(/intakes_illegal_not_tc/);
        const illegal = { reporterId: ada.id, allegesIllegal: true, category: SPEECH, bonaFide: true };
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal, explanation: "x".repeat(2000), citedLaw: "y".repeat(300) })).toBeNull();
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal, explanation: "x".repeat(2001) })).toMatch(/intakes_explanation_len/);
        expect(await refusal({ ...illegal, explanation: "why", citedLaw: "y".repeat(301) })).toMatch(/intakes_cited_law_len/);
        for (const ref of ["N-ABCDEFGH2", "n-ABCDEFGHJ2", "N-abcdefghj2", "N-ABCDEFGH01", "N-ABCDEFGHJ23", "X-ABCDEFGHJ2"]) expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id, ruleId: "R1", ref }), ref).toMatch(/intakes_ref/);
        const ref = newRef();
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id, ruleId: "R1", ref })).toBeNull();
        expect(await refusal({ reporterId: ada.id, ruleId: "R1", ref })).toMatch(/intakes_ref_unique/);
      });
    });
  });

  describe("the staff_texts CHECK", () => {
    type Save = (text: string | null, salt: string | null, digest: string, erased?: boolean) => Promise<{ message: string; code: string } | null>;
    /** One test's texts on a case of their own, in a transaction that is rolled back; each insert in a savepoint. */
    const texts = (fn: (save: Save, tx: DbTx) => Promise<void>) =>
      rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {
        const ada = await profile(tx);
        const caseId = await openCase(tx, "post", await newPostRow(tx, ada.id));
        const save: Save = (text, salt, digest, erased = false) =>
          run(tx, sql`insert into staff_texts (case_id, author_id, kind, text, salt, digest, erased_at) values (${caseId}::uuid, ${ada.id}::uuid, 'facts', ${text}, ${salt}, ${digest}, ${erased ? sql`now()` : sql`null`})`);
        await fn(save, tx);
      });

    test.each(TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS.map((vector) => [vector.name, vector] as const))("%s: SQL computes the digest the contracts' textDigest computes", async (_name, vector) => {
      expect(await sqlDigest(apiDb, vector.salt, vector.text)).toBe(vector.digest);
    });

    test("a text is stored with the digest the contracts compute for its salt and itself, and with no other", async () => {
      await texts(async (save) => {
        // Fresh salts: a digest names one text, so a vector's own digest could be stored only once.
        for (const vector of TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS) {
          const salt = hex64();
          const digest = await textDigest(salt, vector.text);
          expect(await save(vector.text, salt, digest), vector.name).toBeNull();
          // The same text under the digest of another salt, or of another text, is refused.
          expect((await save(vector.text, hex64(), digest))?.message, vector.name).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
          expect((await save(`${vector.text}.`, salt, digest))?.message, vector.name).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
        }
      });
    });

    test("a digest names one text; a text has a salt; only an erased row has neither", async () => {
      await texts(async (save) => {
        const salt = hex64();
        const digest = await textDigest(salt, "a text");
        expect(await save("a text", salt, digest)).toBeNull();
        expect((await save("a text", salt, digest))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest_unique/);
        expect((await save("a text", null, hex64()))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
        expect((await save(null, hex64(), hex64()))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
        expect((await save(null, null, hex64()))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
        expect((await save("a text", hex64(), hex64(), true))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_digest/);
        // The erased form: text and salt gone, the digest kept.
        expect(await save(null, null, hex64(), true)).toBeNull();
      });
    });

    test("the salt is 32 bytes as lower-case hex: an empty, a short or an upper-case salt is refused, also with the digest it gives", async () => {
      await texts(async (save, tx) => {
        const salt = hex64();
        // hex decodes either case to the same bytes, so the upper-case spelling has the lower-case salt's digest.
        const upper = salt.toUpperCase();
        expect(await sqlDigest(tx, upper, "a text")).toBe(await textDigest(salt, "a text"));
        for (const malformed of ["", salt.slice(2), upper, `${salt}00`]) {
          const err = await save("a text", malformed, await sqlDigest(tx, malformed, "a text"));
          expect(err, JSON.stringify(malformed)).toMatchObject({ code: "23514", message: expect.stringMatching(/staff_texts_digest/) });
        }
        expect(await save("a text", salt, await textDigest(salt, "a text"))).toBeNull();
      });
    });

    test("a text longer than 5000 characters is refused whatever its digest", async () => {
      await texts(async (save, tx) => {
        const salt = hex64();
        const long = "x".repeat(5001);
        expect((await save(long, salt, await sqlDigest(tx, salt, long)))?.message).toMatch(/staff_texts_text_len/);
      });
    });
  });

  test("a decision's keyword needs the ground of the law: on a decision without a ground, or on a rule, it is refused", async () => {
    // The decision is a real one, on a reported post; the migrator then changes its row, the only role that can, in a
    // transaction that is rolled back.
    await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      await staffProfile(tx, mod);
      const { postId } = await imagePost(tx);
      const { caseId } = await report(tx, aPost(postId));
      const decisionId = await decideIn(tx, mod, caseId, { kind: "final", outcome: "no_violation" });
      const keyword = DECISION_KEYWORDS[0];
      const set = (changes: ReturnType<typeof sql>) => run(tx, sql`update decisions set ${changes} where id = ${decisionId}::uuid`);
      const refused = { code: "23514", message: expect.stringMatching(/decisions_keyword/) };
      // A null ground is the row a plain comparison let through: its result is null, and a check passes on a null.
      expect(await set(sql`category_keyword = ${keyword}`)).toMatchObject(refused);
      expect(await set(sql`category_keyword = ${keyword}, ground = 'incompatible', rule_id = 'R1'`)).toMatchObject(refused);
      expect(await set(sql`category_keyword = ${keyword}, ground = 'illegal', legal_reference_digest = ${hex64()}`)).toBeNull();
    });
  });

  test("the limits' row is the migration's: 60 decisions an hour and 300 a day, 400 case opens, 50 findings and 10 reveals a day", async () => {
    // The suite's setup leaves this table alone, so the row read here is the one migration 0015 inserted.
    const rows = await apiDb.execute<Record<string, unknown>>(sql`select id, decisions_per_hour, decisions_per_day, case_opens_per_day, findings_per_day, reveals_per_day from moderation_limits`);
    expect(rows.map((row) => ({ ...row }))).toEqual([{ id: 1, decisions_per_hour: 60, decisions_per_day: 300, case_opens_per_day: 400, findings_per_day: 50, reveals_per_day: 10 }]);
    await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      const err = await run(tx, sql`insert into moderation_limits (id, decisions_per_hour, decisions_per_day, case_opens_per_day, findings_per_day, reveals_per_day, updated_at) values (2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, now())`);
      expect(err?.message).toMatch(/moderation_limits_single_row/);
    });
  });

  test("this file left no row behind: the tables it writes hold what they held before it", async () => {
    expect(await rowCounts(apiDb)).toEqual(before);
  });
});
```

### Replace `apps/api/test/lab/README.md` (whole file)

```markdown
# The contention lab of moderation decisions

`contention.lab.ts` measures what a decision's transaction costs and what it meets (3c design, sections 2 and 12),
against the test database with migration 0016. The design names no place for it; it lives here.

It is a database lab. It issues its statements itself, as SQL: a decision is the lock on its subject's profile row, its
row in `decisions` and its rows in `decision_actions`, whose triggers do the rest; a like, a follow, the author's
deletion and the purge are the statements the social and media repositories issue; the purge's delete is the ordered
delete by owner (`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where owner_id = $1 order by id for
update) returning id`). An intake is the moderation module's `recordIntake`. It uses no code of a later task.

Every measured transaction is rolled back, so the lab leaves no decision, and writes no audit row but one: the R4
removal that the redaction's rounds need committed (the last section) is a real, confirmed decision. The accounts it commits
(the large ones, written in bulk by the migrator, and the pair for the two-session rounds) are removed when it ends.

## Running it

From `apps/api`, with the scratch stack's data services up and the test database migrated:

    node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.lab.config.ts

No suite includes it (its file ends in `.lab.ts`). It takes three to four minutes. Each measurement is one line of JSON
in `.data/lab-contention.jsonl` at the repository's root (or the file `LAB_OUT` names), with `busyPercent`: the share of
processor time, over all cores, that was not idle in the second and a half before the measurement.

## The numbers of 2026-10-04, first run: a saturated machine

PostgreSQL 18 in the scratch stack's container on a Windows machine shared with other work. The machine was saturated
throughout: `busyPercent` read 94 to 99 before every measurement, most of it other projects' containers. These numbers
are upper bounds for this hardware; the second run below, on a quieter machine, is the one the design asks for.

### An account's seal (one session; one image on each post)

| image posts | busy | decision row | seal taken while deciding | answer that ends it | seal for good | lifting it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 97% | 104 ms | 180 ms | 254 ms | 282 ms | 232 ms |
| 5,000 | 99% | 18 ms | 1,123 ms | 1,057 ms | 1,131 ms | 995 ms |

- The seal taken while deciding locks the account's image rows in id order, writes one row of `seal_posts` for each post
  and writes every image row once. At 5,000 image posts the decision and its seal take 1.1 s, 0.19% of the ten minutes a
  step-up challenge lives.
- The seal for good that follows writes every image row twice in one transaction: the answer ends the first seal (each
  row back to visible, 1.06 s at 5,000), and the new seal seals each again (1.13 s). Lifting it is a fourth write (1.0 s).
- No post row is locked by any of them.

### The purge of an account (one session)

| image rows | frozen | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | 99% | 436 ms | 2,228 ms | 5,000 | 2.7 s |
| 5,000 | yes | 98% | 390 ms | 1,862 ms | 0 | 2.3 s |
| 20,000 | no | 94% | 1,471 ms | 6,090 ms | 20,000 | 7.6 s |
| 20,000 | yes | 97% | 1,724 ms | 5,821 ms | 0 | 7.6 s |

- The keep trigger reads the freeze once for each row: about 0.3 to 0.45 ms a row under this load, whether the row is
  then kept or deleted. The research lab's figures under load were 2 to 4 s at 5,000 rows and 7 to 16 s at 20,000; these
  lie at their lower end.
- "Frozen" is an unanswered report of child sexual abuse material about the account: every row is kept, and the delete
  answers none.

### A decision against everything else (two sessions, 40 rounds a pair, each side first in half of them)

Three decisions (an interim withhold of a post; a final removal that closes the post's case; a seal on the author's
account's case followed in the same transaction by the answer that ends it) against six other transactions (a like of
the post; a follow of the author; the author's deletion of the post; the author's purge; a notice of child sexual abuse
material that names the post and its author's account; a report of the post under a rule). Each side holds its locks for
15 ms before it rolls back. `busyPercent` was 96.

| decision | against | both completed | deadlocks | lock timeouts | longest transaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| interim withhold | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 236 ms |
| interim withhold | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 116 ms |
| interim withhold | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 158 ms |
| interim withhold | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 232 ms |
| interim withhold | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 409 ms |
| interim withhold | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 318 ms |
| closing removal | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 183 ms |
| closing removal | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 145 ms |
| closing removal | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 194 ms |
| closing removal | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 171 ms |
| closing removal | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 207 ms |
| closing removal | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 231 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 254 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 210 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 233 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 419 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 264 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 206 ms |

- 720 rounds, no deadlock and no lock timeout. The purge met none here either: the deadlock the design expects of it is
  with an intake that locks the account's image rows, which the intake does not do before Task 3.
- What makes this hold: a decision takes its subject's profile row first, as the author's deletion and the purge do; a
  like and a follow take that row in a mode a decision's does not conflict with; a seal locks image rows only; and an
  intake takes its cases in one order and each post's row only to read it.
- A finding the lab led to, now a test (`moderation-races.test.ts`): a report that arrives while a decision is closing
  its target's case waits where it opens a case (`insert into cases ... on conflict do nothing` waits for the transaction
  that is changing the conflicting row), and then opens a new case without a retry. The retry on `case_closed` is needed
  only when the decision has locked the case and not yet closed it when the report reads it.

| image posts | busy | decision row | seal taken while deciding | answer that ends it | seal for good | lifting it |

| image rows | frozen | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | 28% | 182 ms | 888 ms | 5,000 | 1.1 s |
| 5,000 | yes | 24% | 108 ms | 791 ms | 0 | 0.9 s |

# The lab of the intake's lock statement

`hold.lab.ts` measures what an intake's hold costs and what it meets (3c design, sections 5 and 12, Task 3), at the
repository: `MediaForCases.hold` with an owner pair, which is the statement that locks every image row on an account's
posts when a report of child sexual abuse material names the account
(`select ... from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id where m.post_id = any($1) or m.owner_id = any($2) order
by m.id for key share of m`). It also times the disposal's two statements over the same accounts, and runs the purge
against a notice about a post that quotes its author's own post. It runs against the test database with migration 0016,
through the media repository and the moderation module's own `recordIntake`; the purge is the social repository's
`purgeProfile` with the media repository's `purgeOwner` as its last act. Every measured transaction is rolled back; the
accounts it commits are removed when it ends.

    node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.lab.config.ts test/lab/hold.lab.ts

It takes about a minute and a quarter. Each measurement is one line of JSON in `.data/lab-hold.jsonl` (or the file
`LAB_OUT` names), with `busyPercent` as above. `LAB_ROUNDS` sets how many rounds the two sessions meet by chance (40
unless said).

## The numbers of 2026-10-04

Three runs on the shared Windows machine, PostgreSQL 18 in the scratch stack's container: two before the review of
Task 3 and one after its fixes. The machine was never quiet, most of the load other projects' containers:
`busyPercent` read 14 to 40 before the lock statement's runs of the first run (up to 100 before its last measurements),
14 to 83 before those of the second and 15 to 40 throughout the third. The times are upper bounds.

### The lock statement (`hold` with one owner pair; one image on each post; three runs each, a transaction of its own each)

| attached rows | run | busy | lock statement | WAL written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | first | 29 to 40% | 36, 25 and 21 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 5,000 | second | 64 to 83% | 90, 65 and 26 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 5,000 | third | 23 to 31% | 46, 31 and 28 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 20,000 | first | 14 to 19% | 114, 80 and 69 ms | 1,153, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |
| 20,000 | second | 14 to 76% | 102, 180 and 198 ms | 1,408, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |
| 20,000 | third | 23 to 31% | 151, 123 and 102 ms | 1,153, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |

- The research lab's figures (`lab-gate-k`, H) were 77 ms and 287 kB at 5,000 rows and 102 ms and 1.1 MB at 20,000:
  these agree. The lock writes its mark to each row it takes, though no column changes: about 55 bytes of WAL a row.
- The plan is LockRows over a Sort on `m.id` over a hash join of `post_media` and `posts`, as the design says of the
  owner form. In the test database the lab's account owns most image rows, so `post_media` is scanned whole; the sort
  took 0.6 MB of memory at 5,000 rows and 2.5 MB at 20,000.
- A whole notice on the path for child sexual abuse material that names the account (its rows, the copy of the profile,
  the hold and the snapshot) took 72, 95 and 77 ms at 5,000 rows and 104, 238 and 147 ms at 20,000; one that names a
  post of the account as well took 85, 91 and 80 ms at 5,000 and 743 (at 90% busy), 299 and 147 ms at 20,000.
- The purge's ordered delete (`purgeOwner`) right after such a notice, in the same transaction, deleted no row: 1.4,
  1.6 and 1.3 s at 5,000 rows, 5.6 and 5.5 s (73 to 100% busy) and 3.2 s (31% busy) at 20,000, the keep trigger reading
  the freeze once for each row.

### The disposal's two statements (one batch of `dropDisposable`, and `overdueDeletions`)

The account's rows are all attached. In the first two lines nothing of the account is disposable: its posts are
visible. In the last, the account is reported on the path for child sexual abuse material and every post of it is
deleted, so every row carries a mark of disposal and none may go.

| what | attached rows | busy | `dropDisposable` | `overdueDeletions` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nothing disposable, the freeze a condition of its own (as first built) | 5,000 | 100% | 3,332 ms | 3,332 ms |
| | 20,000 | 97% | 14,226 ms | 13,863 ms |
| nothing disposable, the marks tested first (as built now) | 5,000 | 24% | 18 ms | 8 ms |
| | 20,000 | 40% | 62 ms | 19 ms |
| every row marked and frozen (as built now) | 5,000 | 18% | 1,285 ms | 1,174 ms |
| | 20,000 | 26% | 4,148 ms | 3,666 ms |

- As first built, the predicate was `... and (marks) and (m.post_id is null or not public.post_frozen(m.post_id))`.
  The second condition names `post_media` alone, so the planner made it the filter of that table's scan and called the
  freeze for every attached image row in the table before a mark was tested. The review measured 0.9 s at 5,000 rows
  and 3.4 s at 20,000 on a quieter machine; the first two lines are the same statement on a saturated one.
- Now the marks and the freeze are one condition, `case when (marks) then (m.post_id is null or not
  public.post_frozen(m.post_id)) else false end`: it names all three tables, so it runs where they are joined, and the
  freeze is read only for a row that carries a mark. `media-cases.test.ts` pins that no scan's filter names the
  predicate, under the planner's own plan and under each join method alone.
- What remains is the last pair of lines: a frozen account whose posts are all deleted (a purged account under an
  unanswered report, or under a seal for good) costs one read of the freeze for each kept row, about 0.2 ms, at every
  round of the disposal and at every count of overdue rows, for as long as the freeze lasts.

### The purge against a notice about a post that quotes its author's own post

A report of child sexual abuse material about a post that quotes another is taken in as two items, so a notice about a
post that quotes its author's own post holds two posts of one account for share, in id order, while the purge writes
both. The lab's account has such a pair, four images on each post; the notice names the quoting post and the account.
The notice's side counts the runs the moderation module made, so a deadlock it absorbed by running again shows; nothing
runs a purge again, so a deadlock that picks the purge shows as its error.

By chance (two sessions, each side first in half the rounds, a few milliseconds ahead, each holding its locks for
15 ms before it rolls back):

| purge | rounds | busy | purge | notice | deadlocks | longest transaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| as first built (counters, then the posts in id order) | 200 | 95% | 200 of 200 | 200 of 200, each in one run | 0 | 528 ms |
| as built now (every post locked first, in id order) | 40 | 25% | 40 of 40 | 40 of 40, each in one run | 0 | 139 ms |

Staged (ten rounds a shape: the notice has copied the first of the two posts and is held there, the purge comes to
wait, the notice goes on to the second post):

| purge | the quoting post has the lower id | the quoted post has the lower id and was deleted by its author |
|---|---|---|
| as first built: the counters of what its posts quote, then the posts in id order | 10 of 10: the purge ends with 40P01 | not run |
| the account's posts that are not deleted locked first, in id order | 10 of 10: both complete | 10 of 10: the purge ends with 40P01 |
| every post of the account locked first, in id order (as built now) | 10 of 10: both complete | 10 of 10: both complete |

- As first built, the purge's quote counter wrote the quoted post before the ordered statement asked for the quoting
  one, which the notice held: each waited for the other. The window is one statement of the notice wide, so 200 rounds
  by chance never met it, and every staged round did. PostgreSQL ended the purge each time: a session looks for a
  deadlock once it has waited a second, and the purge was the first to wait. The notice went through in one run. A purge
  that ends this way is finished by the purge job within five minutes.
- Locking only the posts that are not deleted leaves the same wait in the second shape: a live post that quotes (or
  replies to) its author's own deleted post has that post's counter written by the purge, and a report of child sexual
  abuse material holds a deleted post like any other. So the purge locks every post of the account first.
- What stays unordered: the counters of other accounts' posts that the purged account replied to, quoted, liked or
  reposted, which the purge writes after its own posts; and the author's deletion of one post, which writes the post
  and then the post it replied to or quoted.
- Before the review this pair ran with two plain posts (and with the purge as first built): 40 of 40 on both sides in
  both runs, no deadlock, the longest transaction 307 ms at 64% busy and 200 ms at 23%.
- What the two-session tests add (`media-cases.test.ts`): when the notice locks first, the purge waits and then keeps
  every attached row; when the purge deletes first, the notice waits, locks nothing and is stored without an error.

### The contention lab again

`contention.lab.ts` issues the purge's statements as the repositories issue them since Task 3: every post of the
account locked in id order (`select id from posts where author_id = $1 order by id for update`), then the tombstones,
and the ordered delete of the image rows last. Three runs on 2026-10-04 with the intake locking image rows and placing
its holds. The first, before the review, still tombstoned by one ordered statement and met a machine at 9 to 14% busy
(53 and 93 before the two purges of 20,000 rows). The second and the third issue the statements above: the second met
a saturated machine (93 to 100% throughout), so its times say more about the machine than about the change; the third
a quiet one (6 to 16%). "Tombstones" is the lock statement and the update together.

| image rows | frozen | run | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | first | 9% | 170 ms | 891 ms | 5,000 | 1.1 s |
| 5,000 | yes | first | 14% | 120 ms | 827 ms | 0 | 1.0 s |
| 20,000 | no | first | 53% | 603 ms | 4,019 ms | 20,000 | 4.6 s |
| 20,000 | yes | first | 93% | 1,440 ms | 4,249 ms | 0 | 5.7 s |
| 5,000 | no | second | 100% | 481 ms | 3,136 ms | 5,000 | 3.6 s |
| 5,000 | yes | second | 100% | 309 ms | 3,423 ms | 0 | 3.8 s |
| 20,000 | no | second | 100% | 1,934 ms | 8,112 ms | 20,000 | 10.1 s |
| 20,000 | yes | second | 100% | 2,249 ms | 8,467 ms | 0 | 10.7 s |
| 5,000 | no | third | 16% | 91 ms | 827 ms | 5,000 | 0.9 s |
| 5,000 | yes | third | 6% | 103 ms | 730 ms | 0 | 0.8 s |
| 20,000 | no | third | 13% | 442 ms | 2,207 ms | 20,000 | 2.7 s |
| 20,000 | yes | third | 13% | 481 ms | 1,977 ms | 0 | 2.5 s |

Locking the posts first costs nothing that shows: at 5,000 posts the lock statement and the update together took 91
and 103 ms, where the one ordered statement took 170 and 120 ms.

The 18 pairs of 40 rounds: in every run each transaction completed, with no deadlock and no lock timeout; the longest
transaction was 137 ms in the first (12% busy), 562 ms in the second (100% busy) and 116 ms in the third (13% busy).
The account's seal taken while deciding: 84 ms at 1,000 image posts and 2.2 s at 5,000 in the first run (13% busy; 0.4
and 1.1 s in Task 2's runs), 361 ms and 3.3 s in the second, 58 and 156 ms in the third.

### What the lab's tests found

- **A batch that was not one.** `dropDisposable` as the design writes it (`delete from post_media where id in (select
  ... order by id limit $1 for update)`) can delete more than its limit. When the planner joins the delete's rows to
  the sub-select by a nested loop, the sub-select runs again for every row; each run skips the rows this statement has
  deleted already and lets the next ones in. On a fresh test database one call deleted all 60 disposable rows under a
  limit of 25, and with hash joins, merge joins, materialising, hashed aggregation and sorting switched off it deleted
  33 of 36. The repository therefore chooses the batch in a materialized common table expression, which runs once
  whatever the plan (`with batch as materialized (select ... order by m.id limit $1 for update of m) delete from
  post_media where id in (select id from batch) returning id`); `media-cases.test.ts` holds the bound under those
  planner settings. The ordered deletes of the author's deletion and the purge have no limit, so the same re-run changes
  nothing they delete.
- **The freeze read for every row.** The disposal's two statements, above.
- **The purge and its own posts.** The staged rounds, above.

## The numbers of 2026-10-09: the R4 redaction (migration 0018)

`contention.lab.ts` gains one test for `redact_r4_body` (3c design, sections 2 and 6.4): the redaction takes its
decision's case, then the post, then the post's images in id order, the order of `moderation_apply` and of an intake's
locks, and the design asks for it to be measured against both. The post has four images. Its R4 removal is the one
thing this lab confirms with a real staff key (the software authenticator, as `decideForTest` does), because a
redaction acts only on a committed decision; it is dated back seven months, so that it is final for its author. The
redaction itself, and everything that runs against it, is rolled back in every round, so each round finds the decision
due again. The removal's case goes with the lab's accounts at the end; its one audit row stays, as every real
decision's does. Run alone with `-t "the R4 redaction"`.

Two runs: the test alone on a machine busy with other work (`busyPercent` 82), then the whole file on a quieter one
(`busyPercent` 22; the whole file took 122 s).

| the redaction against | rounds | redaction | other side | longest transaction, busy | longest, quieter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (alone, one session) | 1 | ok | | 67 ms | 29 ms |
| an interim withhold on the post's other, open case, whose trigger runs `moderation_apply` on the post | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 233 ms | 68 ms |
| a report under a rule, which locks the post `FOR SHARE` and holds its images | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 125 ms | 104 ms |
| a notice of child sexual abuse material naming the post and its author's account, which locks the images through both | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 123 ms | 83 ms |

- No deadlock and no refusal in 120 rounds of either run, each side first in half of them. The redaction and a decision on the post's
  other case meet at the post's row, which both take `FOR UPDATE` before any image row; the redaction and a report meet
  there too (`FOR UPDATE` against `FOR SHARE`); a notice that reaches the images through the account takes them
  `FOR KEY SHARE`, which the redaction's `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` does not wait for.
- That last pair is the one the design accepts as a race and not as a wait (6.4): a report about the author's account
  that commits between the redaction's check of the freeze and its erasure of the snapshots leaves the body blank, the
  snapshots kept and the decision unmarked, and the round after the answer finishes it. The database test of
  `redact_r4_body` stages exactly that.

## orders/: the lab of authorities' orders (sub-project 3f)

`orders/` is the lab the 3f design rests on (its section 3, LAB A to F), copied here unchanged but for its line ends from
`korbat-scratch/research-3e/lab-3f/`, which lies outside the repository: `RUN.txt` holds every command and the machine it
ran on, `make_proto.py` and `20-tables.sql` the prototype of the design's sections 6.2 and 6.3, `21-helpers.sql` the
API's statements, the lettered SQL files the labs themselves, and `out-*.txt` their raw outputs. It ran on a throwaway
cluster of PostgreSQL 18.1 over the migrations 0000 to 0016. The task that builds the ledger's migration of 3f runs it
again on the 18.6 image, as `RUN.txt` lists it, and compares the outputs.

## The numbers of 2026-10-16: the end of an order's preservation (3f, migration 0029)

The test "3f, Task 4" of `contention.lab.ts` (run it alone with `-t "3f, Task 4"`). One order of eleven posts by one
author, one image each: its first item given effect with a real key and aged past its six months, so every round finds
its preservation due; the other ten given effect in one transaction with a made-up confirmation of their params. Both
sides roll back. PostgreSQL 18 in the scratch stack's container, `busyPercent` 19.

| measured | result |
|---|---|
| `order_preservation_end` alone (one image) | 71 ms |
| the ten-item effect alone | 882 ms |
| 40 rounds of the two, each side first in half of them | 40 ok and 40 ok: no deadlock, no lock timeout; the longest side took 4,823 ms |

- The end takes the cases (the item's decision's and those of the post's other copies) in id order, then the item, the
  post and its image rows; the effect takes the author's profile, the cases through its intake's items, its items' rows
  and then each post. The ten posts and the eleventh are different rows, and the end takes no profile, so the two met
  at no row and neither waited on the other for long.
- Task 3's part of this lab (the ten-item transaction against intakes on the same posts, a seal on one author and the
  purge of another) is not here yet.
```

```ts
import path from "node:path";

import { ageOrderForTest, effectForTest, effectParams, effectWith, orderForTest, removeOrderAlerts } from "../integration/orders-fixtures";

/**
 * The contention lab of moderation decisions (3c design, sections 2 and 12): what a decision's transaction costs and what
 * it meets, measured against the real database with migration 0016. The lab issues the statements itself, as SQL: a
 * decision is its profile lock, its row and its ledger rows, whose triggers do the rest; a like, a follow, a deletion and
 * a purge are the statements the social and media repositories issue. Every measured transaction is rolled back, so the
 * lab leaves no decision. Its one audit row is the R4 removal that the redaction's rounds need committed, which is a real,
 * confirmed decision. The accounts and posts it commits for the two-session rounds and the large accounts are removed at
 * the end. It writes one line of JSON for each measurement, with how busy the machine's
 * processors were just before it. Run it by hand (see README.md); no suite includes it.
 */

/** Where the measurements go, one line of JSON each: the file LAB_OUT names, or lab-contention.jsonl in the repository's .data folder (the lab runs from apps/api). */
const OUT = process.env.LAB_OUT ?? path.resolve(process.cwd(), "../../.data/lab-contention.jsonl");
function line(name: string, result: Record<string, unknown>): void {
  const text = JSON.stringify({ name, at: new Date().toISOString(), ...result });
  mkdirSync(path.dirname(OUT), { recursive: true });
  appendFileSync(OUT, text + String.fromCharCode(10));
  console.log(`LAB ${text}`);
}

/** The share of processor time that was not idle over this many milliseconds, across all cores: how loaded the machine is. */
async function busy(ms = 1500): Promise<number> {
  const read = () => os.cpus().reduce((sum, cpu) => ({ idle: sum.idle + cpu.times.idle, all: sum.all + cpu.times.user + cpu.times.nice + cpu.times.sys + cpu.times.irq + cpu.times.idle }), { idle: 0, all: 0 });
  const before = read();
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
  const after = read();
  return Math.round((1 - (after.idle - before.idle) / Math.max(1, after.all - before.all)) * 100);
}

async function timed(fn: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<number> {
  const start = performance.now();
  await fn();
  return Math.round(performance.now() - start);
}

describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("lab: the contention of moderation decisions", () => {
  let apiDb: Db;
  let authDb: Db;
  let migrateDb: Db;
  let mod: TestStaff;
  let admin: TestStaff;

  let world: DeciderWorld | null = null;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    const config = loadConfig();

    authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH, { max: 2 });
    migrateDb = createDb(process.env.DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE!, { max: 2 });

    await migrateDb.execute(sql`insert into posts (author_id, body, created_at) select ${id}::uuid, 'a lab post', now() - interval '40 days' from generate_series(1, ${posts}::int)`);
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`insert into post_media (owner_id, status, width, height, blurhash) select ${id}::uuid, 'ready', 1200, 800, 'L2Eo_P_3jb_3~qoL' from generate_series(1, ${posts}::int)`);

    await migrateDb.execute(sql`analyze post_media`);

    // otherwise pairs them in a nested loop, which at 20,000 rows is 400 million comparisons.
    await migrateDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await tx.execute(sql`set local enable_nestloop = off`);
      await tx.execute(sql`
        with p as materialized (select id, row_number() over (order by id) as n from posts where author_id = ${id}::uuid),
             i as materialized (select id, row_number() over (order by id) as n from post_media where owner_id = ${id}::uuid)
        update post_media m set post_id = p.id, position = 0, alt_text = 'a lab image' from p join i on i.n = p.n where m.id = i.id`);

    const id = randomUUID();

    const decision = await timed(() => insertDecision(tx, { id, caseId, decidedBy: staff.id, params }));
    const actions: number[] = [];
    for (const action of params.actions) actions.push(await timed(() => insertAction(tx, id, action)));
    return { id, lock, decision, actions };

  /** The same, with the params built inside `tx`: for a single session, where nothing waits for what building them touches. */
  const decisionIn = async (tx: DbTx, staff: TestStaff, subject: string, caseId: string, input: DecisionInput) =>
    decisionWith(tx, staff, subject, caseId, await decisionParams(tx, staff, caseId, input));
  const withStaff = (fn: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<void>) =>
    rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {

        // And its lifting, a correction: every row written a fourth time.
        const lift = await decisionIn(tx, admin, owner.id, caseId, { kind: "correction", reviewsDecisionId: final.id, actions: [act("unseal_media")] });
        line("account seal", {
          posts,
          busyPercent: load,
          interimDecisionMs: interim.decision,
          interimSealMs: interim.actions[0],
          finalDecisionEndsInterimMs: final.decision,
          finalSealMs: final.actions[0],

        });

  test("the purge of an account with 5,000 and with 20,000 image rows, free and frozen", async () => {

    const pause = (tx: DbTx) => tx.execute(sql`select pg_sleep(0.015)`);
    // The params of each decision, built and their texts saved once: every decision here rolls back, so its case keeps its
    // version and its texts stay unconfirmed, and the same params decide again in the next round.
    const withhold = await decisionParams(apiDb, mod, postCase, { kind: "interim", actions: [act("withhold")] });

    const decisions: Record<string, (tx: DbTx) => Promise<unknown>> = {
      "interim withhold of the post": (tx) => decisionWith(tx, mod, author.id, postCase, withhold),

          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay));
          const start = performance.now();
          const outcome = await rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {
            await fn(tx);
            await pause(tx);
          }).then(
            () => "ok",
            (err: unknown) => {
              const fromDatabase = raised(err);
              return fromDatabase ? `${fromDatabase.code} ${fromDatabase.message}` : ((err as { code?: string }).code ?? String(err));
            },
          );
          longest = Math.max(longest, performance.now() - start);
          return outcome;
        };
        const ahead = Math.floor(Math.random() * 8);
        const [a, b] = await Promise.all(round % 2 === 0 ? [side(ending, 0)(), side(effect, ahead)()] : [side(ending, ahead)(), side(effect, 0)()]);
        for (const [who, outcome] of [["preservation end", a], ["effect", b]] as const) counts[`${who}: ${outcome}`] = (counts[`${who}: ${outcome}`] ?? 0) + 1;
      }
      line("preservation end contention", { end: "order_preservation_end of one item", against: "the ten-item effect of the same order", rounds: ROUNDS, busyPercent: load, outcomes: counts, longestMs: Math.round(longest) });
    } finally {
      await removeDecided(migrateDb, posts, []);
      await removeOrderAlerts(migrateDb, started);
    }
  });
});
```

```ts
describe("FindingRequest", () => {

  test("a moderator's finding cites a korbat rule, R2 among them, about a post, an account or a korbat link", () => {
    for (const ruleId of ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"]) expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ruleId }).success, ruleId).toBe(true);
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, target: { kind: "account", handle: "@Some_one" } }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(FindingRequest.parse({ ...finding, target: { kind: "account", handle: "@Some_one" } }).target).toEqual({ kind: "account", handle: "some_one" });
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, target: { kind: "link", url: "https://korbat.example/post/" + POST } }).success).toBe(true);
  });

  test("it has no other ground than a rule: a finding never alleges illegality and never goes the path that records no sender", () => {
    for (const ground of ["illegal", "csam", "order", "law", ""]) expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ground }).success, ground).toBe(false);
    const { ground: _ground, ...withoutGround } = finding;
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse(withoutGround).success).toBe(false);
    // The members of the other grounds are refused, never ignored.
    for (const extra of [{ explanation: "words" }, { bonaFide: true }, { citedLaw: "a law" }, { keyword: "csam" }, { name: "A" }, { email: "a@b.example" }, { turnstileToken: "t" }]) {
      expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ...extra }).success, Object.keys(extra)[0]).toBe(false);

    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ruleId: null }).success).toBe(false);

    expect(FINDING_CATEGORIES).toHaveLength(TDB_CATEGORIES.length - 1);

describe("a saved text", () => {
  const save = { kind: "note", text: "Art. 18 check: no suspicion", salt: HEX, digest: HEX };

  test("is of one of the seven kinds, the recorded choice not to seal among them, with a 32-byte salt and a digest in lower-case hex", () => {
    expect(STAFF_TEXT_KINDS).toEqual(["facts", "reason", "legal_reference", "review_reason", "reveal_reason", "note", "seal_declined"]);
    for (const kind of STAFF_TEXT_KINDS) expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, kind }).success, kind).toBe(true);
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, kind: "statement" }).success).toBe(false);
    for (const bad of [HEX.toUpperCase(), HEX.slice(2), `${HEX}00`, "", "g".repeat(64)]) {
      expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, salt: bad }).success, `salt ${bad}`).toBe(false);
      expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, digest: bad }).success, `digest ${bad}`).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, caseId: CASE }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("the request's schema lets any text through: what a text must be is the route's to refuse, with a code of its own", () => {
    // A text that is too long or holds a control character is answered text_invalid, not invalid_request.
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, text: "x".repeat(STAFF_TEXT_MAX + 1) }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, text: `a${String.fromCharCode(7)}b` }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, text: 5 }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("staffTextProblem: a well-formed text of at most 5000 UTF-16 units, with no control character but the line feed and no invisible direction or zero-width character", () => {
    expect(STAFF_TEXT_MAX).toBe(5000);
    const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);
    expect(staffTextProblem(`two${LF}lines`)).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem("")).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem("x".repeat(5000))).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem("x".repeat(5001))).toBe("too_long");
    // An emoji is two units: 2500 of them fit, and one more unit does not.
    const emoji = String.fromCodePoint(0x1f600);
    expect(staffTextProblem(emoji.repeat(2500))).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem(`${emoji.repeat(2500)}x`)).toBe("too_long");
    // Half of a surrogate pair has no UTF-8 bytes.
    expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(0xd83d)}b`)).toBe("malformed");
    expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(0xde00)}`)).toBe("malformed");
    // NUL and every other C0 control but the line feed.
    for (let code = 0; code < 32; code++) {
      expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(code)}b`), `U+${code.toString(16)}`).toBe(code === 10 ? null : "control");
    }
    // The invisible direction and spacing characters the notice texts refuse too; the joiners scripts and emoji need stay.
    for (const code of [0x202a, 0x202e, 0x2066, 0x2069, 0x200b, 0x2060, 0xfeff]) expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(code)}b`), `U+${code.toString(16)}`).toBe("format");
    for (const code of [0x200c, 0x200d]) expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(code)}b`), `U+${code.toString(16)}`).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem(`r${String.fromCharCode(0xe9)}sum${String.fromCharCode(0xe9)}`)).toBeNull();
  });

  test("the answers: the stored text's id and digest, the person's own drafts with their salts, and a snapshot's id and digest, never content", () => {
    expect(StaffTextSaved.parse({ id: CASE, digest: HEX })).toEqual({ id: CASE, digest: HEX });
    const draft = { id: CASE, kind: "facts", text: "The post names a home address.", salt: HEX, digest: HEX, createdAt: TIME };
    expect(StaffTextsResponse.parse({ texts: [draft] }).texts).toEqual([draft]);
    expect(Object.keys(StaffSnapshotTaken.parse({ id: CASE, digest: HEX, body: "content", media: [] }))).toEqual(["id", "digest"]);
  });
});
```

```ts
 * for word.

  kind,

const reversal = (kind: ReversalKind, more: Partial<DecisionStatement["reversals"][number]> = {}): DecisionStatement["reversals"][number] => ({

      const sealing = (kind: "interim" | "final") =>
        statementParagraphs(statement({ kind, ruleId: "R2", facts: SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_post, reason: kind === "interim" ? SEAL_DRAFTS.reason.deciding : SEAL_DRAFTS.reason.final, source: "notice", measures: [measure("seal_media")] }));
      for (const kind of ["interim", "final"] as const) {
        const out = sealing(kind);
        expect(out, kind).toContain(`This step rests on korbat rule R2, "${r2.title}": ${r2.text}`);
        expect(out.join(" "), kind).not.toMatch(/It breaks korbat rule|korbat found it illegal|korbat is checking/);
      }
      // A seal in the category Protection of minors, on the law: the same, with the law.
      const law = statementParagraphs(statement({ kind: "interim", ground: "illegal", ruleId: null, legalReference: "Section 184b of the criminal code.", source: "notice", measures: [measure("seal_media")] }));
      expect(law).toContain("This step rests on the law: Section 184b of the criminal code.");
      expect(law.join(" ")).not.toMatch(/found it illegal|korbat is checking/);
    });

    test("a decision taken while deciding that seals nothing says what korbat is checking, on a rule and on the law", () => {
      const rule = statementParagraphs(statement({ kind: "interim", ruleId: "R5", measures: [measure("withhold")] }));
      expect(rule).toContain(`korbat is checking this against korbat rule R5, "${r5.title}": ${r5.text}`);
      const law = statementParagraphs(statement({ kind: "interim", ground: "illegal", ruleId: null, legalReference: "Section 241 of the criminal code (threats).", source: "notice", measures: [measure("withhold")] }));
      expect(law).toContain("korbat is checking whether this is illegal. The law in question: Section 241 of the criminal code (threats).");
      // Beside "while it decides", nothing states a finding.
      for (const out of [rule, law]) expect(out.join(" ")).not.toMatch(/It breaks korbat rule|korbat found it illegal/);
    });

    test("a final restriction that seals nothing states what korbat found", () => {
      expect(statementParagraphs(statement())).toContain(`It breaks korbat rule R1, "No sexual or pornographic content": ${getRule("R1", 2)!.text}`);
      expect(statementParagraphs(statement({ ground: "illegal", ruleId: null, legalReference: "Section 241." }))).toContain("korbat found it illegal. The law it rests on: Section 241.");
    });
  });

  describe("the seal's sentences", () => {
    const seal = (sealed: { posts: number; images: number; deletedImages: number }, more: Partial<DecisionStatement["measures"][number]> = {}) => measure("seal_media", { sealed, ...more });
    const sealing = (more: Partial<StatementInput>) => statement({ ruleId: "R2", facts: SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_post, reason: SEAL_DRAFTS.reason.deciding, source: "notice", ...more });

    test("on a post case, while deciding: the images of the post, with their number, and the interim redress", () => {
      const out = statementParagraphs(sealing({ kind: "interim", measures: [seal({ posts: 1, images: 3, deletedImages: 0 })] }));
      expect(out[0]).toBe(`korbat sealed the images of your post of ${POST_TIME} (3 in all): nobody can see them, you included.`);
      expect(out).toContain(`The facts: ${SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_post}`);
      expect(out).toContain(`korbat's reasons: ${SEAL_DRAFTS.reason.deciding}`);
      expect(out.at(-1)).toBe(REDRESS_TEXTS[1].interim);
      // Neither sentence of a seal for good (the rule's own text speaks of both, so they are looked for as whole paragraphs' parts).
      expect(out[0]).not.toContain(W.sealForGood);
      expect(out.at(-1)).not.toContain(W.sealAppeal);
    });

    test("on an account case: every image on the account's posts, with and without posts the author had deleted", () => {
      const live = statementParagraphs(sealing({ kind: "interim", post: null, measures: [seal({ posts: 4, images: 9, deletedImages: 0 })] }));
      expect(live[0]).toBe("korbat sealed every image it held on your posts at that time (9 on 4 posts): nobody can see them, you included.");
      const kept = statementParagraphs(sealing({ kind: "interim", post: null, measures: [seal({ posts: 4, images: 9, deletedImages: 2 })] }));
      expect(kept[0]).toBe(
        "korbat sealed every image it held on your posts at that time (9 on 4 posts): nobody can see them, you included. 2 of them are on posts you had deleted, which korbat had kept under its terms (Your data).",
      );
    });

    test("for good: kept only for the authorities, and the appeal waits until they have assessed the images", () => {
      const out = statementParagraphs(sealing({ reason: SEAL_DRAFTS.reason.final, measures: [seal({ posts: 1, images: 2, deletedImages: 0 })] }));
      expect(out[0]).toBe(`korbat sealed the images of your post of ${POST_TIME} (2 in all): nobody can see them, you included. They are kept only for the authorities korbat reports this to.`);
      expect(out.at(-1)).toBe(`${appeal(DECIDED)} An appeal of a seal waits until the authorities have assessed the images.`);
      const account = statementParagraphs(sealing({ post: null, measures: [seal({ posts: 2, images: 5, deletedImages: 1 })] }));
      expect(account[0]).toBe(
        "korbat sealed every image it held on your posts at that time (5 on 2 posts): nobody can see them, you included. 1 of them is on a post you had deleted, which korbat had kept under its terms (Your data). They are kept only for the authorities korbat reports this to.",
      );
    });

    test("a seal that changed nothing says so: already sealed, or the post or the account deleted", () => {
      const first = (more: Partial<StatementInput>, noEffect: "already" | "deleted") => statementParagraphs(sealing({ kind: "interim", measures: [seal({ posts: 1, images: 2, deletedImages: 0 }, { noEffect })], ...more }))[0];
      expect(first({}, "already")).toBe(
        `korbat sealed the images of your post of ${POST_TIME} (2 in all): nobody can see them, you included. Another decision already keeps these images sealed, so this changes nothing anyone sees now. It stays in force should that decision be reversed.`,
      );
      expect(first({}, "deleted")).toBe(`korbat sealed the images of your post of ${POST_TIME} (2 in all): nobody can see them, you included. You had deleted this post, so this changes nothing anyone sees.`);
      expect(first({ post: null }, "deleted")).toBe("korbat sealed every image it held on your posts at that time (2 on 1 post): nobody can see them, you included. Your account is deleted, so this changes nothing.");
    });

    test("a lifted seal", () => {
      const reviewed = { kind: "final" as const, ground: "incompatible" as const, ruleId: "R2" as const, rulesVersion: 2, legalReference: null, decidedAt: "2026-10-01T09:00:00.000Z" };
      const out = statementParagraphs(statement({ kind: "correction", outcome: "reversed", ground: null, ruleId: null, facts: null, reason: "The authority answered on 2 October 2026.", measures: [], reversals: [reversal("unseal_media")], reviewed }));
      expect(out[0]).toBe("korbat corrected its decision of 2026-10-01 09:00 UTC and reversed it.");
      expect(out[1]).toBe("korbat lifted the seal on these images. If an image is still not shown, another decision listed in Settings, Cases applies.");
    });
  });

  describe("reversals and what ended", () => {
    const reviewed = { kind: "final" as const, ground: "incompatible" as const, ruleId: "R1" as const, rulesVersion: 2, legalReference: null, decidedAt: "2026-10-01T09:00:00.000Z" };
    const correction = (more: Partial<StatementInput>) => statement({ kind: "correction", outcome: "reversed", ground: null, ruleId: null, facts: null, reason: "The post is satire.", measures: [], reviewed, ...more });
    const FIELD = (field: string) => `korbat does not put back your ${field} as it was before the reset: set it again in Settings, Profile if you wish.`;
    const KEPT = `The screen of the decision that reset it shows what it was for at least ${RETENTION.resetValueDays} days.`;
    const KEPT_R4 = `The screen of the decision that reset it shows what it was for at least ${RETENTION.resetValueDays} days, unless korbat had already erased it under rule R4.`;

    test("a correction of a final decision renders that decision's rule from its own row and version, and its reason", () => {
      // The corrected decision was made under rulebook version 1: its rule reads as that version worded it.
      const out = statementParagraphs(correction({ reviewed: { ...reviewed, rulesVersion: 1 }, reversals: [reversal("restore")] }));
      expect(out).toEqual([
        "korbat corrected its decision of 2026-10-01 09:00 UTC and reversed it.",
        `Your post of ${POST_TIME}: korbat lifted this restriction. If your post or image is still restricted, another decision listed in Settings, Cases applies, or its content was erased under korbat's retention rules.`,
        "No automated means were used to find this or to decide it.",
```
