```ts
/**
 * The only file outside `src/social/` may import. Everything else in the module is private and the
 * architecture test fails the build if another file reaches into it.
 */
import type { MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { Db, DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import type { JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import type { MediaForPosts } from "../media";
import type { RateLimitStore } from "../middleware/rate-limit";
import type { ModerationForSocial } from "../moderation";
import { WITHOUT_MEDIA, type SocialDeps, type SocialEvents } from "./context";
import type { StoredPostState } from "./visibility";
import { startExplore } from "./explore";
import { exportProfile, type ProfileExport } from "./flows/export";
import { createSocialRepo, type AccountLockMode, type CapturedPost, type CapturedProfile, type LockedAccount } from "./repo";
import { postStatusRoutes, socialRoutes } from "./routes";

export { SocialError } from "./context";
export { enforceWriteLimit } from "./limits";
export type { SocialDeps, SocialEvents, ViewerId } from "./context";
export type { AccountLockMode, CapturedPost, CapturedProfile, LockedAccount } from "./repo";
export type { ExportedMedia, ExportedPost, ProfileExport } from "./flows/export";

/** What the account module needs from this one (1b design, section 5): the purge of a deleted account, and the data export. */
export interface SocialForAccount {
  /**
   * One transaction that tombstones every post, removes the engagement and graph rows with their
   * counters and anonymises the profile row, keeping its handle; `within` runs inside it, as its last
   * act, for the media rows. Safe to repeat: a second run changes nothing.
   */
  purgeProfile(userId: string, now: Date, within: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<void>): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * The profile, read at once, and its posts with their images, its engagement and its side of the graph,
   * each read in keyset pages of `pageSize` rows (1,000 unless a test says otherwise) as it is iterated.
   */
  exportProfile(userId: string, pageSize?: number): Promise<ProfileExport>;
}

/**
 * What the moderation module needs from this one (3c design, section 5): the locks on profile rows that order a case's
 * transactions against everything else an account does, and the reads a case's evidence and its rules are built from.
 * The moderation module owns no table of this one and never writes to one.
 */
export interface SocialForModeration {
  /**
   * Locks these profile rows in id order, in one statement; with `live`, a missing or deleted account is refused
   * (not_found). Each row answers whether its account is deleted and (3e) whether it is suspended and restricted in its
   * reports, read in the locking statement by the clock.
   */
  lockAccounts(tx: DbTx, ids: readonly string[], mode: AccountLockMode, live?: boolean): Promise<LockedAccount[]>;
  /** The post, locked `for share`, as evidence copies it, or null; its body is empty when its content was erased. */
  capturePost(tx: DbTx, postId: string): Promise<CapturedPost | null>;
  /** The account's handle, display name and bio as evidence copies them, or null. */
  captureProfile(tx: DbTx, accountId: string): Promise<CapturedProfile | null>;
  /**
   * The account a handle names. With `withDeleted`, for a report of child sexual abuse material, also a deleted profile
   * and the account of a handle it has left; without it, only a live profile that holds the handle now.
   */
  findAccountByHandle(handle: string, withDeleted: boolean): Promise<{ id: string; deleted: boolean } | null>;
  /** Who wrote the post, or null when no row has the id. */
  postAuthor(postId: string): Promise<string | null>;
  /** The post's author, state and the post it quotes, or null when no row has the id; no lock. */
  postRef(postId: string): Promise<{ authorId: string; state: StoredPostState; quoteOfId: string | null } | null>;
}

/**
 * The moderation module's interface over the social repository on the pool it is given. A factory of its own, not a
 * member of createSocial's result: the social module's views take facts from the moderation module, which is therefore
 * built between the two.
 */
export function socialForModeration(apiDb: Db): SocialForModeration {
  const repo = createSocialRepo(apiDb);
  return {
    lockAccounts: (tx, ids, mode, live) => repo.lockAccounts(tx, ids, mode, live),
    capturePost: (tx, postId) => repo.capturePost(tx, postId),
    captureProfile: (tx, accountId) => repo.captureProfile(tx, accountId),
    findAccountByHandle: (handle, withDeleted) => repo.findAccountByHandle(handle, withDeleted),
    postAuthor: (postId) => repo.postAuthor(postId),
    postRef: (postId) => repo.postRef(postId),
  };
}

export interface CreateSocialOptions {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** Per-account write limits share the store the per-IP middleware uses. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  logger: Logger;
  /** The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account with CSRF and Origin checked. */
  requireSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's requireFreshAuth: a credential proven in the last five minutes, which a handle change needs on top. */
  requireFreshAuth: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's appendEvent, so profile and handle changes land in auth_events. Without it nothing is recorded (the 2a tests). */
  events?: SocialEvents;
  /** The media module's interface for posts. Without it posts carry no images. */
  media?: MediaForPosts;
  /** The moderation module's interface for views: moderation.forSocial. Without it no post carries the author's chip. */
  moderation?: ModerationForSocial;
  now?: () => Date;
}

export function createSocial(options: CreateSocialOptions) {
  const deps: SocialDeps = {
    repo: createSocialRepo(options.apiDb),
    media: options.media ?? WITHOUT_MEDIA,
    moderation: options.moderation,
    limits: options.rateLimitStore,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
    events: options.events,
  };
  const forAccount: SocialForAccount = {
    purgeProfile: (userId, now, within) => deps.repo.purgeProfile(userId, now, within),
    exportProfile: (userId, pageSize) => exportProfile(deps, userId, pageSize),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    /** The interface the account module uses. */
    forAccount,
    routes: socialRoutes(deps, options.requireSession, options.requireFreshAuth),
    /**
     * 3f (design, section 7.12): GET /api/posts/:id/status, a router of its own that app.ts mounts after the global limit
     * and before the session's resolution. No interface member: nothing outside this module calls it.
     */
    statusRoutes: postStatusRoutes(deps),
    /**
     * Starts the Explore refresh under the shared job lock: a round at once, then one every five minutes. Returns the
     * function that stops the timer.
     */
    startExplore: (lock: JobLock) => startExplore(deps, lock),
  };
}

export type Social = ReturnType<typeof createSocial>;
```

```ts
import { CreatePostRequest, HandleChangeRequest, HandleParam, Pagination, PostId, ProfileEditRequest } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { Hono, type Context, type MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";
import { z } from "zod";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import { errorBody } from "../lib/errors";
import { validate } from "../lib/validate";
import { MediaError } from "../media";
import { SocialError, type SocialDeps, type ViewerId } from "./context";
import { setEngagement, type EngagementKind } from "./flows/engagement";
import { explorePage, exploreStatus, setShowInExplore } from "./flows/explore";
import { blockedList, mutedList, setBlock, setFollow, setMute } from "./flows/graph";
import { createPost, deletePost, getPost, thread } from "./flows/posts";
import { changeHandle, editProfile } from "./flows/profile-edit";
import { followers, following, profile } from "./flows/profiles";
import { bookmarkedPosts, followingTimeline, latestTimeline, likedPosts, profilePosts, profileReplies } from "./flows/timelines";

const PostParam = z.object({ id: PostId });
const ProfileParam = z.object({ handle: HandleParam });

/** Signed out, Explore is its first page only (2c design, section 8): a cursor asks for more, which needs an account. */
const EXPLORE_SIGN_IN = "Sign in to see more of Explore.";

/**
 * Every social endpoint, mounted at `/api`. Handlers only validate, call a flow and shape the
 * response. `guard` is the auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account, with CSRF and
 * Origin already checked for cookie sessions. `fresh` is its requireFreshAuth: a credential proven
 * in the last five minutes, which a handle change needs on top.
 */
export function socialRoutes(deps: SocialDeps, guard: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>, fresh: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>) {
  const r = new Hono<AppEnv>();
  const viewer = (c: Context<AppEnv>): ViewerId => c.get("session")?.userId ?? null;
  const me = (c: Context<AppEnv>): string => c.get("session")!.userId;

  r.onError((err, c) => {
    if (err instanceof SocialError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    }
    // Creating a post attaches its images through the media module, which refuses with its own error type.
    if (err instanceof MediaError) return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    c.get("log").error({ err }, "unhandled error in social route");
    return c.json(errorBody("internal", "Internal error", c.get("requestId")), 500);
  });

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- posts

  r.post("/posts", guard, validate("json", CreatePostRequest), async (c) => c.json(await createPost(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("json")), 201));
  r.get("/posts/:id", validate("param", PostParam), async (c) => c.json(await getPost(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").id)));
  r.delete("/posts/:id", guard, validate("param", PostParam), async (c) => {
    await deletePost(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").id);
    return c.body(null, 204);
  });
  r.get("/posts/:id/thread", validate("param", PostParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await thread(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").id, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );
  // Why the author's own post is in Explore or not; anyone else gets not_found from the flow.
  r.get("/posts/:id/explore", guard, validate("param", PostParam), async (c) => c.json(await exploreStatus(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").id)));

  for (const kind of ["like", "repost", "bookmark"] as EngagementKind[]) {
    r.post(`/posts/:id/${kind}`, guard, validate("param", PostParam), async (c) => c.json(await setEngagement(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").id, kind, true)));
    r.delete(`/posts/:id/${kind}`, guard, validate("param", PostParam), async (c) => c.json(await setEngagement(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").id, kind, false)));
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- timelines

  r.get("/timeline/following", guard, validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await followingTimeline(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/timeline/latest", validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await latestTimeline(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/timeline/explore", validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => {
    const query = c.req.valid("query");
    // Refused here, before the flow reads anything: whatever the cursor holds, a signed-out reader gets the first page only.
    if (!viewer(c) && query.cursor) return c.json(errorBody("unauthenticated", EXPLORE_SIGN_IN, c.get("requestId")), 401);
    return c.json(await explorePage(deps, viewer(c), query));
  });

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- profiles and graph

  r.get("/profiles/:handle", validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await profile(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").handle)));
  r.get("/profiles/:handle/posts", validate("param", ProfileParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await profilePosts(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );
  r.get("/profiles/:handle/replies", validate("param", ProfileParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await profileReplies(deps, viewer(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );
  r.get("/profiles/:handle/followers", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await followers(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );
  r.get("/profiles/:handle/following", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), validate("query", Pagination), async (c) =>
    c.json(await following(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, c.req.valid("query"))),
  );

  r.post("/profiles/:handle/follow", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setFollow(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, true)));
  r.delete("/profiles/:handle/follow", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setFollow(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, false)));
  r.post("/profiles/:handle/block", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setBlock(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, true)));
  r.delete("/profiles/:handle/block", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setBlock(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, false)));
  r.post("/profiles/:handle/mute", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setMute(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, true)));
  r.delete("/profiles/:handle/mute", guard, validate("param", ProfileParam), async (c) => c.json(await setMute(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("param").handle, false)));

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the viewer's private lists

  r.get("/me/likes", guard, validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await likedPosts(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/me/bookmarks", guard, validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await bookmarkedPosts(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/me/blocks", guard, validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await blockedList(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));
  r.get("/me/mutes", guard, validate("query", Pagination), async (c) => c.json(await mutedList(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("query"))));

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the viewer's own profile

  r.patch("/me/profile", guard, validate("json", ProfileEditRequest), async (c) => c.json({ profile: await editProfile(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("json")) }));
  r.post("/me/handle", guard, fresh, validate("json", HandleChangeRequest), async (c) => c.json({ profile: await changeHandle(deps, me(c), c.req.valid("json")) }));
  // "Show my posts in Explore": on and off, with no body, as the app's other switches.
  r.post("/me/explore", guard, async (c) => c.json(await setShowInExplore(deps, me(c), true)));
  r.delete("/me/explore", guard, async (c) => c.json(await setShowInExplore(deps, me(c), false)));

  return r;
}

/**
 * 3f (design, sections 5 and 7.12): GET /api/posts/:id/status, the one question Caddy asks the API for every request of a
 * post's page, so that a status check from outside reads what a person sees. A router of its own, mounted after the
 * global limit and before the session's resolution, as the image files' router is: Caddy's question carries the
 * visitor's cookies, and a route among the module's others would read a session for every page view. It parses the id
 * itself, since the validator would answer a malformed one with a JSON body, and answers 204 exactly when a post with
 * this id is visible, and 404 with no body otherwise (no such post, a malformed id, deleted by its author, withheld,
 * removed or disabled): the same for everyone, so it tells nothing a signed-out read of the post does not, and never 451.
 * No interface carries it: nothing outside this module calls it.
 */
export function postStatusRoutes(deps: Pick<SocialDeps, "repo">) {
  const r = new Hono<AppEnv>();
  r.get("/posts/:id/status", async (c) => {
    const id = PostId.safeParse(c.req.param("id"));
    if (!id.success) return c.body(null, 404);
    const row = (await deps.repo.findPosts([id.data])).get(id.data);
    return c.body(null, row?.state === "visible" ? 204 : 404);
  });
  return r;
}
```

### Replace `infra/caddy/Caddyfile` (whole file)

```text
{
  auto_https off
  admin off
}

# Caddy's own 404 for an API path a site does not serve, in the API's error envelope, so the page's parser reads it as it
# reads the API's own 404. Nothing behind it is asked.
(api_not_found) {
  header -Server
  header Content-Type application/json
  header Cache-Control no-store
  respond `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"No such route"}}` 404
}

# The page's security headers (3a; 3f, section 7.12): one block for the app's files and for a post's page, so every answer
# of the page carries the same ones, whatever status the post's page gets.
(app_page_headers) {
  header {
    Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
    X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
    X-Frame-Options "DENY"
    Referrer-Policy "no-referrer"
    Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()"
    # challenges.cloudflare.com serves the Turnstile widget script and its iframe (sign-in screens).
    Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://challenges.cloudflare.com; frame-src https://challenges.cloudflare.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'"
    -Server
  }
}

# The app's shell, the same bytes for every post's page: the page itself decides what to show.
(app_shell) {
  root * /srv
  rewrite * /index.html
}

# The app's site while it is open (APP_SITE=open, the default).
(app_site_open) {
  # A client from the push network (ntfy and the watcher, 3f) is refused here: until the push site, only cloudflared could
  # reach Caddy. The handles below that reach anything each answer it 403 first: a handle of this matcher alone would be
  # sorted after the path handles. PUSH_SUBNET is the network's fixed subnet, from Compose.
  @push remote_ip {$PUSH_SUBNET}

  # The staff API belongs to the console's site below, on an origin of its own: the app's site never forwards it. Each of
  # these handles matches one path, longer than /api/*, and Caddy puts such handles most specific first, so they come
  # ahead of the API proxy below wherever they are written.
  handle /api/staff {
    import api_not_found
  }
  handle /api/staff/* {
    import api_not_found
  }

  # The API. Its own headers pass through untouched: its CSP is the strict one for JSON and images.
  handle /api/* {
    # Image uploads. The API counts bytes itself and stops at 20 MiB; this is the second line behind it.
    @upload path /api/media
    request_body @upload {
      max_size 25MB
    }
    # Everything else is JSON, and small. The API caps it at 64 KiB too.
    @json {
      not path /api/media
    }
    request_body @json {
      max_size 64KB
    }
    header -Server
    respond @push 403
    reverse_proxy api:3000 {
      # Behind the tunnel cloudflared sets CF-Connecting-IP and the API needs it; anywhere else a
      # client could set it, so Caddy drops it. Decided at build time by the TUNNEL argument.
      import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy
    }
  }

  # A post's page (3f design, sections 5 and 7.12): the app's shell under the status the API gives the post, so that a
  # check from outside reads 404 for a post that is not public and never 451. Caddy asks GET /api/posts/<id>/status, with
  # the visitor's address and cookies as every proxied request carries them (the route reads no session, and the
  # global limit counts the question against the visitor): 204 gives the shell with 200, 404 the same shell with 404,
  # and any other answer (a 429 of the global limit) the shell with 200, as before; handle_errors below does the same
  # when the API cannot be asked. Only the status line differs: the bytes and the headers are the same in every case,
  # which Task 4's first step checked on this image (Caddy 2.11.4).
  handle /post/* {
    respond @push 403
    import app_page_headers
    header Cache-Control "no-cache"
    encode gzip
    reverse_proxy api:3000 {
      import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy
      method GET
      rewrite /api/posts/{http.request.uri.path.1}/status
      @shown status 204
      handle_response @shown {
        import app_shell
        file_server
      }
      @gone status 404
      handle_response @gone {
        import app_shell
        file_server {
          status 404
        }
      }
      handle_response {
        import app_shell
        file_server
      }
    }
  }

  # The web app: static files, the page's security headers, and caching by kind of file.
  handle {
    respond @push 403
    root * /srv
    encode gzip
    import app_page_headers
    # The page is revalidated on every load, so a deploy is seen at once; the hashed bundles never change.
    @immutable path /_expo/* /assets/*
    header @immutable Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
    @page {
      not path /_expo/* /assets/*
    }
    header @page Cache-Control "no-cache"
    try_files {path} /index.html
    file_server
  }

  # A post's page when the API cannot be asked (stopped, or not answering): the shell with 200, as before the status.
  # Every other error is answered as Caddy answers it without this block.
  handle_errors {
    @postpage path /post/*
    handle @postpage {
      import app_page_headers
      header Cache-Control "no-cache"
      encode gzip
      import app_shell
      file_server {
        status 200
      }
    }
  }
}

# The app's site while it is closed (APP_SITE=closed; 3f design, section 7.17, a restore): 503 with one fixed sentence to
# every path, the API's included, and nothing else asked or served. The console's site is unchanged.
(app_site_closed) {
  handle {
    header -Server
    header Content-Type "text/plain; charset=utf-8"
    header Cache-Control "no-store"
    respond "korbat is closed for maintenance. Please come back later." 503
  }
}

# The app's site. APP_SITE (open, the default, or closed) is read when Caddy starts and names the snippet that is the
# site: any other value names no snippet, and Caddy refuses to start rather than leave the site open during a restore.
:8080 {
  import app_site_{$APP_SITE:open}
}

# The staff console (3a design, section 8): a site of its own for the console's own origin, CONSOLE_ORIGIN. It serves the
# console's page and proxies the staff API and nothing else. It is always built and always serves the page; the API alone
# switches the console on, and while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is unset every staff path answers 404, which the page explains. Its
# handles each match two paths or none, so Caddy keeps them in the order written: the staff API, the rest of the API, the
# console's files.
:8090 {
  # A client from the push network (3f) is refused, as on the app's site. This handle's matcher names no path, like the
  # two below, so Caddy keeps it first, as written.
  @push remote_ip {$PUSH_SUBNET}
  handle @push {
    header -Server
    respond 403
  }

  # The staff API, proxied as the app's site proxies /api/*. No header_up Host: the API's staff gate compares the Host the
  # browser sent with CONSOLE_ORIGIN. Caddy still replaces whatever X-Forwarded-* headers a client sent with its own.
  @staff path /api/staff /api/staff/*
  handle @staff {
    # Staff requests are small JSON. The API caps them at 64 KiB too.
    request_body {
      max_size 64KB
    }
    header -Server
    reverse_proxy api:3000 {
      # As on the app's site: the per-IP sign-in limits key on CF-Connecting-IP, which only cloudflared may set.
      import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy
    }
  }

  # The rest of the API is the app's, never the console's.
  @api path /api /api/*
  handle @api {
    import api_not_found
  }

  # The console's page, from /console, a folder outside the app's /srv, so the app's site can never serve it. Its policy
  # is the strict one of section 3: everything from this origin only, no inline script or style, and Trusted Types with no
  # policy, so no HTML or script sink can be used. apps/admin/site-headers.mjs holds the same headers for the development
  # server, and apps/admin/test/console-site.test.ts keeps the two equal.
  handle {
    root * /console
    encode gzip
    header {
      Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'; require-trusted-types-for 'script'; trusted-types 'none'"
      Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
      X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
      X-Frame-Options "DENY"
      Referrer-Policy "no-referrer"
      Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin"
      Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy "same-origin"
      # WebAuthn for the console itself only; no camera, microphone or position for anyone.
      Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), publickey-credentials-get=(self), publickey-credentials-create=(self)"
      -Server
    }
    # The hashed script and stylesheet never change under their names. Everything else, the page above all, is neither
    # stored nor transformed: no-transform stops Cloudflare injecting scripts the policy would block on every page view.
    # `file` holds only when the path names a file of the build, so the page answered for a missing /assets/ name (the
    # fallback below) is never kept for a year under that name.
    @immutable {
      path /assets/*
      file
    }
    header @immutable Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
    @page {
      not {
        path /assets/*
        file
      }
    }
    header @page Cache-Control "no-store, no-transform"
    try_files {path} /index.html
    file_server
  }
}

# The phones' push site (3f design, section 5), for the push hostname (API_PUSH_ORIGIN): only the two topics'
# subscriptions reach ntfy, by GET, which is what the ntfy app sends: the stream a phone holds open (ws, json, sse; both
# topics joined by a comma in one request, in either order), with its replay of what it missed (since=), and the check of
# a user's access (auth). Everything else is Caddy's own 404, ntfy's account API, /v1/config and /v1/stats among them:
# they answer any caller otherwise. Publishing is the watcher's alone, on the push network.
:8091 {
  @subscribe {
    method GET
    path_regexp ^/(korbat-oncall|korbat-all)(,(korbat-oncall|korbat-all))?/(ws|json|sse|auth)$
  }
  handle @subscribe {
    header -Server
    reverse_proxy ntfy:2586 {
      # As on the other sites: a client-set CF-Connecting-IP is dropped unless TUNNEL=on. ntfy reads the client from
      # X-Forwarded-For (behind-proxy); behind the tunnel that header takes CF-Connecting-IP's value (the Dockerfile).
      import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy
      import /etc/caddy/push-header.caddy
    }
  }
  handle {
    header -Server
    respond 404
  }
}
```

```yaml
  tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  logging: *logging

services:
  postgres:
    # PostgreSQL 18. From 18 on the image keeps the cluster under /var/lib/postgresql/<major>/docker, so
    # the volume is mounted one level up and a later major can pg_upgrade inside it. A cluster from the
    # earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) is moved over by scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs.
    image: postgres:18.6-alpine@sha256:77f585114c32fbca283dc835b0596f4e52b51b4c6662d7810b2f4084f60a1873
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 1g
    memswap_limit: 1g
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}
      # The contact point's watcher's role (3f), which 01-roles.sh makes on a new data directory. Not required: a stack
      # without the watcher runs without it.
      KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}
    volumes:
      - pgdata18:/var/lib/postgresql
      - ./postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    # watch: the watcher's own network to the database, which holds nothing else.
    networks: [data, watch]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    # Valkey, the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, under the service name the URLs already use. A password
    # is required: nothing on the data network may read the session cache without it.
    image: valkey/valkey:9.1.2-alpine@sha256:48332870af354a799964c0012ae1194a0bf2bf894eb508f945810596dc2d8d11
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 384m
    memswap_limit: 384m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:?set REDIS_PASSWORD in infra/.env}
    command: ["sh", "-c", "exec valkey-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction --requirepass $$REDIS_PASSWORD"]
    volumes:
    # A fresh volume: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into `redisdata`, and that
    # volume held only transient state (limits, codes in flight, cached sessions, queued image jobs).
      - valkeydata:/data
    networks: [data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "VALKEYCLI_AUTH=$$REDIS_PASSWORD valkey-cli ping | grep -q PONG"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  migrate:
    <<: *node-common
    restart: "no"
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
    command: ["node", "dist/migrate.js"]
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: postgres://korbat_migrate:${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      MIGRATIONS_DIR: /app/migrations
      # `staff.js enroll` runs here, as the migrator, the one role the running API never holds, and records on each link
      # the console's origin and relying party ID it is issued for. Empty, the console is off and enroll refuses.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # 3f: staff.js order-open runs here too, and reads the home state (whether an order is cross-border) and the app's
      # origin (how a link is read, as the console's route reads it). Neither is required: enroll and the migrations run
      # without them, and order-open refuses with one sentence while either is empty.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:-}
    networks: [data]
    depends_on:
      postgres: { condition: service_healthy }

  api:
    <<: *node-common
    # The image's name, the one Compose gives it by default, written out: notify (3f) runs the same image, so it is
    # built once.
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
      args:
        KORBAT_VERSION: ${KORBAT_VERSION:-0.0.0}
    mem_limit: 512m
    memswap_limit: 512m
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      # development or production, from infra/.env; production turns on the guards against test keys, plain-http
      # origins and a relay without TLS. The worker below always runs as production.
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
      PORT: "3000"
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_API: postgres://korbat_api:${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      DATABASE_URL_AUTH: postgres://korbat_auth:${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      REDIS_URL: redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379
      TRUSTED_ORIGINS: ${API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS:-}
      # Which header names the client: the stack refuses to start without a choice.
      TRUST_PROXY: ${API_TRUST_PROXY:?set API_TRUST_PROXY in infra/.env}
      # Auth settings. The stack refuses to start while any of these is missing from infra/.env.
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:?set API_APP_ORIGIN in infra/.env}
      AUTH_HMAC_KEY: ${API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY:?set API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY in infra/.env}
      IP_HASH_KEY: ${API_IP_HASH_KEY:?set API_IP_HASH_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEY: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEY:?set API_TOTP_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      # Encrypts a signed-out notifier's name and address; earlier keys stay accepted for decryption.
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY:?set API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY:?set API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in infra/.env}
      SMTP_URL: ${API_SMTP_URL:?set API_SMTP_URL in infra/.env}
      MAIL_FROM: ${API_MAIL_FROM:?set API_MAIL_FROM in infra/.env}
      TERMS_VERSION: ${API_TERMS_VERSION:?set API_TERMS_VERSION in infra/.env}
      # The verified badge's phone check. off (the default) hides the badge; vonage needs the two credentials.
      VERIFY_PROVIDER: ${API_VERIFY_PROVIDER:-off}
      VONAGE_API_KEY: ${API_VONAGE_API_KEY:-}
      VONAGE_API_SECRET: ${API_VONAGE_API_SECRET:-}
      VERIFY_BRAND: ${API_VERIFY_BRAND:-korbat}
      # Passkeys. Empty values leave the API's defaults: the host of APP_ORIGIN as the RP ID and korbat as the name.
      WEBAUTHN_RP_ID: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID:-}
      WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME:-}
      # The staff console, served by Caddy's second site: the origin staff open it at, and the RP ID staff keys are bound
      # to (empty means the console's hostname). An empty origin switches the console off: every /api/staff path then
      # answers 404. The migrate service gets the same two values for `staff.js enroll`.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # Moderation: the UTC hour of the daily release of decisions to those who reported, the queue's emergency switch, and
      # the retention job's switch, which is off only for a restore window (README, Restoring, step 5).
      MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR: ${API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR:-7}
      MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN: ${API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN:-off}
      MODERATION_RETENTION: ${API_MODERATION_RETENTION:-on}
      # Authorities' orders (3f): whether the alert tick judges the alert channel's health. Empty means on in production;
      # off until the contact point's mailbox exists (README, Upgrading).
      NOTIFY: ${API_NOTIFY:-}
      # The operator's Member State, a state whose facts the contracts hold (DE is filled in), and the published contact
      # point for authorities. Both empty until the owner's list is done; the home state is required once the contact
      # point is set.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      CONTACT_POINT: ${API_CONTACT_POINT:-}
      # Images. The API writes uploads and only reads what the worker stored.
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
      MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES: ${MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES:-2147483648}
      MEDIA_RECONCILE: ${MEDIA_RECONCILE:-on}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
    networks: [app, data]
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      redis: { condition: service_healthy }
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  # The image worker runs the decoder, the most exploitable code in the stack. It has no network at
  # all, no credentials and no capabilities: it reads uploads and writes the store, and that is
  # everything it can reach. The memory limit was sized on worst-case images (2b design, Research).
  worker:
    <<: *node-common
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/worker/Dockerfile
    network_mode: none
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    mem_limit: 768m
    memswap_limit: 768m
    cpus: 1.0
    pids_limit: 64
    tmpfs: ["/tmp:size=64m"]
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads:ro
      - media-store:/media/store
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/media/store/heartbeat', 'utf8')).at < 60000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 4

  # The contact point's watcher (3f design, section 5): the API's image with dist/notify.js, under the profile notify. It
  # reads the contact-point mailbox over IMAP and publishes the alerts to ntfy. On the network watch it reaches PostgreSQL
  # as korbat_notify, whose grants are four tables, and nothing else; on push it reaches ntfy. It never joins data, where
  # the API listens and the limit store is. It exits rather than hang, and Docker starts it again. No setting of it is
  # required by Compose: the program names the one it is missing and exits.
  notify:
    <<: *node-common
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["node", "dist/notify.js"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    # Measured in this image (3f Task 1): about 82 MB resident idle, a peak of 93 MB during a first read of 10,000 old
    # messages, which took 21 seconds and fell back to 81 MB; under this limit the container's peak was 85 MB, with no
    # kill. 128 MB keeps more than a third above that peak.
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:-production}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_NOTIFY: postgres://korbat_notify:${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_USER: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_USER:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK:-}
      NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN:-}
    networks: [watch, push]
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      ntfy: { condition: service_started }
    # The watcher writes the time of every round it ends; two minutes without one is a hang.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - Number(require('fs').readFileSync('/tmp/korbat-notify-beat', 'utf8')) < 120000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # The push server (3f design, section 5), under the profile notify, never linked into korbat's programs: ntfy at its
  # pinned release, reading its users, rights and tokens from infra/ntfy/server.yml (git-ignored, made from
  # server.yml.example), mounted read-only, since Compose would blank the $2a$10$ of a password hash in a variable. Only
  # on push, which is internal: it has no route out, so nothing is forwarded upstream. Its cache and auth files are on its
  # volume, at /var/tmp, the one directory of the image its user may write to.
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.28.0@sha256:6ef4b819f722fccdc036af611c4774cfdc2de821ab74fdd48bbf4c9d6f8973da
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["serve", "--config", "/etc/ntfy/server.yml"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    user: "1000:1000"
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy-data:/var/tmp
    networks: [push]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:2586/v1/health"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 4

  # Caddy serves the web app on port 8080, proxying /api, the staff console on port 8090, proxying only /api/staff, and
  # (3f) the phones' push site on port 8091, proxying only the two topics' subscriptions to ntfy. It runs as its own
  # user, sees only the API and ntfy, and is the only thing cloudflared can reach. A client from the push network (ntfy,
  # the watcher) is refused 403 on the app's and the console's sites.
  caddy:
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: infra/caddy/Dockerfile
      args:
        EXPO_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: ${WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY:?set WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY in infra/.env}
        KORBAT_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
        TUNNEL: ${TUNNEL:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE: ${WEB_BADGE:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL: ${WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL:?set WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL in infra/.env}
    depends_on:
      api: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      # The push network's subnet, which the app's and the console's sites refuse (3f).
      PUSH_SUBNET: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}
      # The app's site, open (the default) or closed: closed answers 503 to every path while a restore is checked (3f,
      # section 7.17). Caddy reads it when it starts and refuses to start on any other value.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
    volumes:
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    networks: [edge, app, push]

  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.1@sha256:b269e8abd07a5bf6f3f4be65d5050b2174eca89c56a0241a8ff32a16aec454e4
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    profiles: ["tunnel"]
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run"]
    environment:
      TUNNEL_TOKEN: ${TUNNEL_TOKEN}
    networks: [edge]
    depends_on:
      - caddy

# cloudflared reaches only Caddy, Caddy reaches only the API and ntfy, and the API alone reaches the data services, but
# for the watcher's own network to PostgreSQL (3f).
networks:
  edge:
  app:
  data:
  # The watcher and PostgreSQL, nothing else. Not internal: the mail host's port 993 is reached through its gateway.
  watch:
  # ntfy, the watcher and Caddy. Internal: no route out. Its fixed subnet is what the app's and the console's sites refuse.
  push:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}

volumes:
  # PostgreSQL 18. The earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) stays until scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs has
  # moved it and you remove it by hand.
  pgdata18:
  valkeydata:
  # Uploads wait here for the worker and are deleted once processed. Nothing in it needs a backup.
  media-uploads:
  # The images korbat serves. Back it up together with the database.
  media-store:
  # Caddy's state, owned by its own user; the earlier root-owned caddydata and caddyconfig volumes can go.
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
  # ntfy's message cache and its auth database (3f). The cache is how a phone gets an alert published while its
  # connection was down; the auth database is rebuilt from infra/ntfy/server.yml at every start.
  ntfy-data:
```

### Replace `packages/contracts/src/moderation.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { Email, OpaqueId, TurnstileToken } from "./auth";
import { hex, sha256, sha256Bytes, sortedJson, utf8 } from "./canonical";
import { MediaId } from "./media";
import { ALERT_CHANNEL_STATES, OrderNoticeFacts, OrderTexts, OrdersUnverified, type OrderGround } from "./orders";
import { FORBIDDEN_FORMAT } from "./text";

// Moderation cases (3c design, section 10): the constants and digests that the database, the API, the console, the app,
// the mails and the terms share. Each is the one source its words and numbers are taken from. This module imports
// nothing from staff.ts, and the index evaluates it first, so staff.ts can read these constants while it loads; an import
// the other way round would be a cycle that fails at load. For the same reason it imports nothing from social.ts, whose
// shapes may come to name this module's constants: what a notice needs of a post's id and of a handle is written here.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- rules, categories and keywords

/** The rulebook's rule ids. @korbat/rules holds the rules themselves; the contracts never import it. */
export const RULE_IDS = ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"] as const;
export type RuleId = (typeof RULE_IDS)[number];

/**
 * The 16 categories of the Commission's Transparency Database (read 2026-10-02), which every intake and decision carries.
 * The migration's CHECK lists are written from this constant, and a database test holds them to it. A value the
 * Commission removes stays here: a kept row may hold it, and only the lists offered for new input drop it.
 */
export const TDB_CATEGORIES = [
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE",
] as const;
export type TdbCategory = (typeof TDB_CATEGORIES)[number];

/** The two categories a notifier never chooses: a rule-only report gets the first, a notifier who is not sure the second. */
type UnofferedCategory = "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" | "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE";
export type TdbFormCategory = Exclude<TdbCategory, UnofferedCategory>;

/** The 14 categories the illegal-ground form shows. */
export const TDB_FORM_CATEGORIES: readonly TdbFormCategory[] = TDB_CATEGORIES.filter(
  (category): category is TdbFormCategory => category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" && category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
);

/**
 * The four choices of the path for child sexual abuse material and the Transparency Database keyword each stores. "abuse"
 * stores none: the database has no keyword for it.
 */
export const CSAM_KEYWORDS = {
  csam: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL",
  deepfake: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL_DEEPFAKE",
  grooming: "KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS",
  abuse: null,
} as const;
export type CsamKeywordChoice = keyof typeof CSAM_KEYWORDS;

/** The keywords a decision on the law may carry: in 3c only the Transparency Database's "Terrorist content". */
export const DECISION_KEYWORDS = ["KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT"] as const;
export type DecisionKeyword = (typeof DECISION_KEYWORDS)[number];

/** The category the composer presets for a decision under each rule. */
export const RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY = {
  R1: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
  R2: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS",
  R3: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",
  R4: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS",
  R5: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE",
  R6: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD",
} as const satisfies Record<RuleId, TdbCategory>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- lanes

/** The queue's lanes: 0 is the most urgent. A case takes the most severe lane of its unanswered items. */
export type Lane = 0 | 1 | 2;

/** R2 and R5 are urgent; R3 and R4 come next; R1 and R6 last. */
const RULE_LANES: Record<RuleId, Lane> = { R1: 2, R2: 0, R3: 1, R4: 1, R5: 0, R6: 2 };

/** The categories that are not in lane 2: violence, public security and self-harm are urgent; six more come next. */
const CATEGORY_LANES: Partial<Record<TdbCategory, Lane>> = {
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE: 1,
};

/**
 * The lane of an intake's items, from its ground alone: nothing is weighted. The CSAM path is urgent whatever else is
 * said. Otherwise it is the more severe of the cited rule's lane and, on a notice that alleges illegality, the category's:
 * only there is the category a claim about the content, where on a rule report or a finding it is korbat's own
 * classification for the Transparency Database.
 */
export function laneFor(input: { ruleId: RuleId | null; allegesIllegal: boolean; csam: boolean; category: TdbCategory }): Lane {
  if (input.csam) return 0;
  const byRule: Lane = input.ruleId === null ? 2 : RULE_LANES[input.ruleId];
  const byCategory: Lane = input.allegesIllegal ? (CATEGORY_LANES[input.category] ?? 2) : 2;
  return byRule < byCategory ? byRule : byCategory;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- limits and periods

/**
 * What one sender may send, published in the terms: intakes an hour and a day per network signed out and per account
 * signed in, the targets one notice names, and the bounds of its two texts in characters (the migration's CHECKs hold
 * the same numbers).
 */
export const NOTICE_LIMITS = {
  signedOut: { perHour: 5, perDay: 20 },

  maxTargets: 10,
  explanationMax: 2000,
  citedLawMax: 300,
} as const;

/** A notice on the CSAM path names at most one account: one such target reaches every image on the account's posts. */
export const CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS = 1;

/** How many months back a case page counts earlier answers to reports of this kind about the same target or author. */
export const SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS = 12;

/** How many rows of a seal's list the case answer carries. */
export const SEAL_LIST_MAX = 500;

/** The author's appeal and the re-examination window, in calendar months (appealDeadline, and appeal_deadline in SQL). */
export const APPEAL_MONTHS = 6;

/** Appeals a day per account, and re-examinations a day per account or network. */
export const DAILY_LIMITS = { appeals: 5, reexaminations: 5 } as const;

/**
 * The numbers of account sanctions, the same as the SQL function standing_rules() returns, which a database test compares
 * member by member: every function and view of the standing ledger reads its numbers from there, and every word of the
 * console and the app from here. Each is a cautious default without a source of its own, flagged for the owner (3e
 * design, section 2): one line to change in each place. It stands here, ahead of the section of account sanctions below,
 * because RETENTION reads three of its numbers.
 */
export const STANDING_RULES = {
  /** How long a strike counts. */
  strikeDays: 90,
  /** The active strikes that open the ladder. */
  ladderStrikes: 3,
  /** The most days of the first, second and third suspension of the ladder. */
  ladderDays: [3, 7, 30],
  /** How long a suspension of the ladder counts toward the next rung. */
  ladderMemoryDays: 365,
  /** The reply window, from the moment korbat's own relay accepted the notice mail, and never less from the decision. */
  replyWindowHours: 168,
  /** The window, from the decision, when the relay refused the address or the mail was given up. */
  undeliveredHours: 336,
  /** The most days of a suspension at once, by its ground. */
  threatDays: 30,
  terroristDays: 30,
  floodDays: 7,
  protectiveDays: 14,
  /** The count without which no flood is found: a condition, never the finding. */
  floodPosts: 20,
  floodMinutes: 60,
  /** The most age of the decision a threat or terrorist suspension rests on, and of the seal for good a protective one rests on. */
  basisAgeDays: 30,
  /** The frame of the reporting counts, by the day a report was sent, and a warning's time of counting. */
  reportFrameDays: 90,
  /** The warning's threshold: marked reports, and their share of the rule reports sent. */
  reportWarnMarks: 5,
  reportWarnShare: 0.5,
  /** The restriction's threshold, in marked reports sent after the warning, and its most days. */
  reportRestrictMarks: 3,
  reportRestrictDays: 30,
} as const;

/**
 * How long 3c keeps each kind of data (the design's section 6.6), published in the terms. Each is a design choice, not a
 * legal figure.
 */
export const RETENTION = {
  /** Content restricted under R4 is erased once the restriction is final: this long after its author was told, or at the answer to their appeal. */
  r4FinalMonths: APPEAL_MONTHS,
  /** An intake's record (its texts and who sent it) goes this long after its last release. */
  intakeDays: 30,
  /** A reset field's old value stays readable this long after a lift that comes before the case's copies are erased. */
  resetValueDays: 30,
  /** A case's evidence waits this long after the case's newest snapshot or draft text. */
  evidenceHours: 24,
  /** Statements are erased this long after the account's deletion. */
  statementMonths: 12,
  /** The access log, and the reveal reasons its rows name. */
  accessLogMonths: 12,
  /** A notifier's contact goes this long after the last day korbat owed the notice something, */
  contactMonths: 6,
  /** and at most this long after the notice when nothing moved that day. */
  contactMaxMonths: 13,
  /** A notifier's confirmation of an address. */
  confirmationDays: 30,
  /** Backups are deleted this long after each was taken. No code of 3c enforces it: the README tells the operator. */
  backupDays: 30,
  /** An unconfirmed staff text is deleted after this long. */
  draftHours: 24,
  /** A mail still unsent this long after it was due is given up. */
  mailGiveUpDays: 5,
  /**
   * 3e (design, sections 6.5, 6.7 and W.7): the text of a reply to a suspension or a termination is kept until it is
   * answered and its decision is final for its author (erase_reply_statements); an unanswered reply keeps it, however
   * old. No clock alone ends it, so it is a phrase, the one the terms print, and no number.
   */
  replyText: "until korbat has answered it and its decision can no longer be appealed",
  /**
   * 3e: the reporting counts (the marks "manifestly unfounded" and the daily tallies of rule reports) are deleted this
   * long after the UTC day their report was sent (forget_report_counts), and with the account. It is the frame of the
   * counts, read from STANDING_RULES and never typed twice.
   */
  reportCountDays: STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays,
  /**
   * 3e: the ledger rows of strikes, suspensions, terminations, warnings and retired handles are kept with their decision,
   * as every row of the ledger is; what ends is their use, after these days: a strike's counting, a suspension's memory
   * toward the next rung, and a warning's counting. Each is STANDING_RULES' own number.
   */
  standingRecord: { strikeDays: STANDING_RULES.strikeDays, ladderMemoryDays: STANDING_RULES.ladderMemoryDays, warningDays: STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays },
} as const;

/** The most items one decision marks "manifestly unfounded" (a default, flagged with the other numbers). */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- measures

/**
 * The ledger's kinds, in the order of the database's action_kind: 3c's seven measures and five reversals, then 3e's six
 * measures (a strike, a suspension, a termination, a retired handle, a warning about reporting and a restriction of it)
 * and four reversals (3e design, section 10.1); then 3f's measure of an authority's order and its reversal (3f design,
 * section 10.1), which only an order decision and its correction hold.
 */
export const ACTION_KINDS = [
  "withhold",
  "remove",
  "seal_media",
  "withhold_media",
  "remove_media",
  "reset_display_name",
  "reset_bio",
  "restore",
  "unseal_media",
  "restore_media",
  "restore_display_name",
  "restore_bio",
  "strike",
  "suspend",
  "terminate",
  "retire_handle",
  "warn_reporting",
  "restrict_reporting",
  "overrule",
  "lift_suspension",
  "unretire_handle",
  "lift_reporting",
  "disable_by_order",
  "reinstate_by_order",
] as const;
export type ActionKind = (typeof ACTION_KINDS)[number];

/**
 * What a measure acts on: a post, one image of it, every image its case reaches, one of an account's two fields, the
 * account itself (a strike, a suspension or a termination), its handle, or its reports under the rules.
 */
export type MeasureTarget = "post" | "image" | "images" | "display_name" | "bio" | "account" | "handle" | "reporting";

export interface MeasureSpec {
  /** A decision taken while deciding (interim) may hold it. */
  interim: boolean;
  /** A decision that decides the case (final) may hold it. */
  final: boolean;
  /** For a reversal, the measures it lifts (it names exactly one row of them); null for a measure. */
  lifts: readonly ActionKind[] | null;
  target: MeasureTarget;
  /** The words for it in the composer, the statement and the terms. */
  label: string;
}

/**
 * Every kind of the ledger: whether it is taken while deciding, when the case is decided, or is a reversal; its target;
 * and its label. A post or one image is withheld only while deciding and removed only when the case is decided; a seal
 * and a field reset are either. A reversal is neither: the database's triggers say which decision may hold one.
 */
export const MEASURES = {
  withhold: { interim: true, final: false, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Withhold the post" },
  remove: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Remove" },
  seal_media: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "images", label: "Seal the images this case reaches" },
  withhold_media: { interim: true, final: false, lifts: null, target: "image", label: "Withhold one image" },
  remove_media: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "image", label: "Remove one image" },
  reset_display_name: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "display_name", label: "Reset display name" },
  reset_bio: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "bio", label: "Reset bio" },
  restore: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["withhold", "remove"], target: "post", label: "Lift the restriction of the post" },
  unseal_media: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["seal_media"], target: "images", label: "Lift the seal" },
  restore_media: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["withhold_media", "remove_media"], target: "image", label: "Lift the restriction of one image" },
  restore_display_name: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["reset_display_name"], target: "display_name", label: "Lift the reset of the display name" },
  restore_bio: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["reset_bio"], target: "bio", label: "Lift the reset of the bio" },
  // 3e (design, section 18, W.1). Each measure of 3e is taken only when the case is decided, and none while deciding.
  strike: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Strike" },
  suspend: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Suspend the account" },
  terminate: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Terminate the account" },
  retire_handle: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "handle", label: "Retire the handle" },
  warn_reporting: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "reporting", label: "Warn about reporting" },
  restrict_reporting: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "reporting", label: "Restrict reporting" },
  overrule: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["strike"], target: "account", label: "Overrule the strike" },
  lift_suspension: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["suspend", "terminate"], target: "account", label: "Lift the suspension" },
  unretire_handle: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["retire_handle"], target: "handle", label: "Give the handle back" },
  lift_reporting: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting"], target: "reporting", label: "Lift the reporting measure" },
  // 3f (design, section 18, W.1): neither is taken while deciding or when a case is decided; only an order decision holds
  // the first, and only the correction of one the second.
  disable_by_order: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Disabled for an order" },
  reinstate_by_order: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["disable_by_order"], target: "post", label: "Reinstate after an order" },
} as const satisfies Record<ActionKind, MeasureSpec>;

/** The fourteen measures and the ten reversals, each list in the ledger's order: what a statement's data keeps apart. */
export const MEASURE_KINDS = [
  "withhold",
  "remove",
  "seal_media",
  "withhold_media",
  "remove_media",
  "reset_display_name",
  "reset_bio",
  "strike",
  "suspend",
  "terminate",
  "retire_handle",
  "warn_reporting",
  "restrict_reporting",
  "disable_by_order",
] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];
export type MeasureKind = (typeof MEASURE_KINDS)[number];
export const REVERSAL_KINDS = ["restore", "unseal_media", "restore_media", "restore_display_name", "restore_bio", "overrule", "lift_suspension", "unretire_handle", "lift_reporting", "reinstate_by_order"] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];
export type ReversalKind = (typeof REVERSAL_KINDS)[number];

/** The three kinds whose action entry also signs `days` and `announced` (3e design, section 10.4). */
export const TIMED_KINDS = ["suspend", "terminate", "restrict_reporting"] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];
export type TimedKind = (typeof TIMED_KINDS)[number];

/**
 * The console's fixed drafts of the facts and the reason of a seal (3c design, section 10). Nobody at korbat opens images
 * that are reported as child sexual abuse material, so none of these says or implies that korbat found them to be such
 * material, and each reason says that korbat's staff do not open them: the statement then tells its author what korbat
 * knows and no more. The composer fills them in, and the moderator may edit them. The two `added` drafts are for a case
 * whose suspect items korbat added for a quoted post: they never say that this post was reported, and name no other post.
 */
export const SEAL_DRAFTS = {
  facts: {
    notice_post: "korbat received a notice that reports images of this post as child sexual abuse material.",
    notice_account: "korbat received a notice that reports this account for child sexual abuse material. It does not say which images, so korbat sealed every image on the account's posts.",
    notice_added: "korbat received a notice about content on korbat that shows this post's images and reports them as child sexual abuse material.",
    finding_post: "A moderator reported images of this post as possible child sexual abuse material.",
    finding_account: "A moderator reported images on this account's posts as possible child sexual abuse material. korbat sealed every image on the account's posts.",
    finding_added: "A moderator reported content on korbat that shows this post's images as possible child sexual abuse material.",
  },
  reason: {
    deciding: "korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them. It hides them from everyone, you included, until an admin has answered the report.",
    final:
      "korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them. An admin found the report credible enough to keep the images sealed and to report them to the police, who can assess them.",
  },
} as const;

/**
 * The facts draft of a seal, chosen from the suspect items its decision considers: a notice's draft when any of them came
 * from a user's notice, else a finding's; the `added` form when every one of them is an item korbat added for a quoted
 * post (or a re-examination of one), else the post's or the account's by the case's target.
 */
export function sealFactsDraft(target: "post" | "account", items: readonly { source: "user" | "finding"; added: boolean }[]): string {
  if (items.length === 0) throw new Error("a seal's facts are drafted from the suspect items its decision considers: there is no suspect item");
  const from = items.some((item) => item.source === "user") ? "notice" : "finding";
  const about = items.every((item) => item.added) ? "added" : target;
  return SEAL_DRAFTS.facts[`${from}_${about}`];
}

/**
 * One measure or reversal as a decision's confirmed params name it: its kind, and for an image measure the image; for a
 * suspension, a termination and a restriction of reporting also its days and whether it is announced (3e design,
 * section 10.4).
 */
export interface DecisionActionParams {
  kind: ActionKind;
  mediaId: string | null;
  days?: number | null;
  announced?: boolean;
  /** 3f: a reinstatement after an order signs its ground (staff.ts, ReinstateAction). */
  orderGround?: OrderGround;
}

/**
 * The one order a decision's actions are confirmed in: by kind and then by image, each compared as a string, an action
 * without an image first. The console sorts with it before it asks for the key, and the params' schema refuses any other
 * order, so the same decision always has the same hash.
 */
export function compareDecisionActions(a: DecisionActionParams, b: DecisionActionParams): number {
  if (a.kind !== b.kind) return a.kind < b.kind ? -1 : 1;
  const [left, right] = [a.mediaId ?? "", b.mediaId ?? ""];
  return left < right ? -1 : left > right ? 1 : 0;
}

/** Why a moderator reveals who sent a report: the choices of the reveal dialog. The reason itself is a saved text. */
export const REVEAL_REASON_CATEGORIES = ["impersonation_claim", "abuse_of_reporting", "legal_requirement", "other"] as const;
export type RevealReasonCategory = (typeof REVEAL_REASON_CATEGORIES)[number];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- errors

/**
 * Every code the moderation flows put in ErrorEnvelope.error.code: what sending a report or a notice, reading its
 * status, asking for a re-examination, appealing, taking a report in, deciding a case and reviewing an appeal raise, and
 * what the console's case routes answer (a text that cannot be saved, an image that is not shown, a source that cannot
 * be revealed). The routes may also answer the shared invalid_request, onboarding_required, not_found, rate_limited and
 * service_unavailable, and the staff routes the staff codes. The codes the database keeps to itself (moderation_column,
 * quote_item_missing, read_committed_only) are not among them: no route answers one.
 */
export const ModerationErrorCode = z.enum([
  "notice_link_invalid",
  "notice_link_offsite",
  "human_check_failed",
  "staff_cannot_report",
  "notice_not_found",
  "already_reported",
  "appeal_not_open",
  "appeal_exists",
  "reexamination_not_open",
  "reexamination_exists",
  "case_changed",
  "case_closed",
  "staff_recused",
  "staff_target",
  "admin_required",
  "reviewer_conflict",
  "decision_cap",
  "profile_changed",
  "snapshot_mismatch",
  "snapshot_erased",
  "text_not_found",
  "invalid_decision",
  "text_invalid",
  "text_quotes_user",
  "image_refused",
  "reveal_refused",
  // 3e (design, section 10.5): a rule report of an account whose reports are restricted, a reply to a measure that takes
  // none, a decision whose strike is missing or not due, a second standing measure, and a termination under R2.
  "reporting_restricted",
  "reply_not_open",
  "strike_mismatch",
  "standing_conflict",
  "ground_not_established",
  // 3f (design, section 10.6): a message at the contact point that already has its disposition; and Task 2's order
  // records: a named message that is not there, an order of the same state, authority and reference (which carries the
  // order that stands), a closed order, an event the order's state does not take, an extension after the release.
  "message_handled",
  "order_needs_message",
  "order_exists",
  "order_closed",
  "order_event_refused",
  "already_released",
  // Task 3 (giving effect): an effect signed on facts the order no longer has; an unverified DSA Article 9 order without
  // an admin's urgent; the day's order decisions of one account; korbat's appeal of an order's decision.
  "order_changed",
  "order_not_verified",
  "order_cap",

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- reports and notices

/**
 * The rules a report or a notice may cite. R2 is offered nowhere: a report of child sexual abuse material goes a path of
 * its own, which records no sender, and only a moderator's finding cites R2 (the database refuses a user's intake that
 * does).
 */
export const REPORT_RULE_IDS = ["R1", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"] as const satisfies readonly RuleId[];
export type ReportRuleId = (typeof REPORT_RULE_IDS)[number];

/** How many characters the name a signed-out notifier gives may have. */
export const NOTICE_NAME_MAX = 100;

/** Any control character but the line feed. */
const TEXT_CONTROL = /[^\P{Cc}\n]/u;
/** Any control character at all: a name is one line. */
const LINE_CONTROL = /\p{Cc}/u;

const NOT_WELL_FORMED = { message: "half of a surrogate pair is not text" };
const NO_CONTROL = { message: "control characters are not allowed" };
const NO_FORMAT = { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" };
const SOME_TEXT = { message: "some text is needed" };

/**
 * A free text of a notice. The server stores it as it was written or refuses it, and never changes it: a well-formed
 * string with some text in it, no control character but the line feed, none of the invisible direction and spacing
 * characters, and at most `max` characters as PostgreSQL's char_length counts them, which is what the tables' CHECKs hold.
 */
const noticeText = (max: number) =>
  z
    .string()
    // A character outside the basic plane is two UTF-16 units, so this bound never refuses what the count below accepts.
    .max(2 * max)
    .refine(isWellFormed, NOT_WELL_FORMED)
    .refine((text) => !TEXT_CONTROL.test(text), NO_CONTROL)
    .refine((text) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(text), NO_FORMAT)
    .refine((text) => text.trim().length > 0, SOME_TEXT)
    .refine((text) => Array.from(text).length <= max, { message: `at most ${max} characters` });

/** The name a signed-out notifier may give: one line under the same rules. */
const NotifierName = z
  .string()
  .max(2 * NOTICE_NAME_MAX)
  .refine(isWellFormed, NOT_WELL_FORMED)
  .refine((name) => !LINE_CONTROL.test(name), NO_CONTROL)
  .refine((name) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(name), NO_FORMAT)
  .refine((name) => name.trim().length > 0, SOME_TEXT)
  .refine((name) => Array.from(name).length <= NOTICE_NAME_MAX, { message: `at most ${NOTICE_NAME_MAX} characters` });

/** A post's id in the lower case PostgreSQL returns, so an id written in any case names the same row. */
const TargetPostId = z.uuid().transform((id) => id.toLowerCase());

/** A handle as a notice names it: an optional leading @, then the 3 to 20 characters handles may contain, kept in lower case. */
const TargetHandle = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .regex(/^@?[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,20}$/)
  .transform((value) => value.replace(/^@/, "").toLowerCase());

/**
 * A link as a notice gives it: an http or https address of at most 300 characters, kept as written. Whether it is an
 * address of this korbat, and of what, the route decides.
 */
const TargetLink = z.url({ protocol: /^https?$/ }).max(300);

/**
 * What a report or a notice names: a post by its id, optionally with the one of its images that is meant; an account by
 * its handle; or a korbat link, which the server parses. Nothing else can be named, and nothing can be attached.
 */
export const NoticeTarget = z.discriminatedUnion("kind", [
  z.strictObject({ kind: z.literal("post"), id: TargetPostId, mediaId: MediaId.optional() }),
  z.strictObject({ kind: z.literal("account"), handle: TargetHandle }),
  z.strictObject({ kind: z.literal("link"), url: TargetLink }),
]);
export type NoticeTarget = z.infer<typeof NoticeTarget>;

const NoticeTargets = z.array(NoticeTarget).min(1).max(NOTICE_LIMITS.maxTargets);
const ReportRule = z.enum(REPORT_RULE_IDS);

/** The categories an illegal-ground notice may carry: the 14 the form shows, and "not specified" for someone who is not sure. */
const NoticeCategory = z.enum([...TDB_FORM_CATEGORIES, "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE"] as const);

/** The four choices of the path for child sexual abuse material. */
const CsamChoice = z.enum(Object.keys(CSAM_KEYWORDS) as [CsamKeywordChoice, ...CsamKeywordChoice[]]);

/**
 * One report or notice, by its ground. Each ground is a strict shape, so a member that belongs to another ground is
 * refused rather than ignored:
 *   - `rule`: it breaks a korbat rule (any but R2), with an optional explanation;
 *   - `illegal`: an Art. 16 notice that it is illegal, with the category, the explanation and the statement of good
 *     faith the Article asks for, optionally the law, a rule it also breaks and, from someone signed out, a name and an
 *     address (a signed-in sender's contact is their account, and the route refuses either from them);
 *   - `csam`: the path for child sexual abuse material, which asks no name or address and records no sender; its
 *     explanation and statement are optional, and it names at most CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS accounts, counted by the
 *     handles as named (the route counts again once the links are parsed).
 * `turnstileToken` is the human check of a signed-out sender; a signed-in sender's is ignored.
 */
export const NoticeRequest = z.discriminatedUnion("ground", [
  z.strictObject({
    ground: z.literal("rule"),
    ruleId: ReportRule,
    targets: NoticeTargets,
    explanation: noticeText(NOTICE_LIMITS.explanationMax).optional(),
    turnstileToken: TurnstileToken.optional(),
  }),
  z.strictObject({
    ground: z.literal("illegal"),
    targets: NoticeTargets,
    category: NoticeCategory,
    citedLaw: noticeText(NOTICE_LIMITS.citedLawMax).optional(),
    explanation: noticeText(NOTICE_LIMITS.explanationMax),
    bonaFide: z.literal(true),
    ruleId: ReportRule.optional(),
    name: NotifierName.optional(),
    email: Email.optional(),
    turnstileToken: TurnstileToken.optional(),
  }),
  z
    .strictObject({
      ground: z.literal("csam"),
      targets: NoticeTargets,
      keyword: CsamChoice,
      explanation: noticeText(NOTICE_LIMITS.explanationMax).optional(),
      bonaFide: z.boolean().optional(),
      turnstileToken: TurnstileToken.optional(),
    })
    .refine((notice) => new Set(notice.targets.flatMap((target) => (target.kind === "account" ? [target.handle] : []))).size <= CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS, {
      message: `a notice of this kind names at most ${CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS} account`,
      path: ["targets"],
    }),
]);
export type NoticeRequest = z.infer<typeof NoticeRequest>;

/** A notice's public reference: N- and ten base32 characters. */
export const NoticeRef = z.string().regex(/^N-[A-Z2-7]{10}$/);

/**
 * The answer to a report or a notice. The token comes only with a notice sent signed out or on the path for child sexual
 * abuse material: it opens the status page, and is shown once.
 */
export const NoticeResponse = z.object({ ref: NoticeRef, token: OpaqueId.optional() });
export type NoticeResponse = z.infer<typeof NoticeResponse>;

/** What the status page sends: the reference with the notice's own token, or with the token of a mail's link. */
export const NoticeStatusRequest = z.strictObject({ ref: NoticeRef, token: OpaqueId });
export type NoticeStatusRequest = z.infer<typeof NoticeStatusRequest>;

/** The page's two buttons, for which only the token of a mail's link works: "I sent this", or "stop korbat's mails about reports to this address". */
export const NoticeContactRequest = z.strictObject({ ref: NoticeRef, token: OpaqueId, choice: z.enum(["confirm", "stop"]) });
export type NoticeContactRequest = z.infer<typeof NoticeContactRequest>;

/**
 * The longest statement an appeal or a request for a re-examination may carry, in characters as PostgreSQL's
 * char_length counts them: what the CHECKs of `appeals` and `intake_items` hold.
 */
export const STATEMENT_MAX = 2000;

/**
 * What the person may add to an appeal or to a request for a re-examination: free of form and optional, under the
 * rules of every free text of a notice. Left out when they wrote nothing.
 */
const Statement = noticeText(STATEMENT_MAX).optional();

/**
 * POST /api/notices/reexamine: a notifier asks korbat to decide an item of their notice again, with the notice's own
 * token or the token of a mail's link, as for the status page. `position` is the item's place on that page, 1 to 20:
 * an item korbat added for a quoted post is asked about like any other, by its own position.
 */
export const NoticeReexamineRequest = z.strictObject({ ref: NoticeRef, token: OpaqueId, position: z.number().int().min(1).max(20), statement: Statement });
export type NoticeReexamineRequest = z.infer<typeof NoticeReexamineRequest>;

/** POST /api/moderation/items/:item/reexamine: the same, for an item of a report the signed-in account sent, named by its id. */
export const ReexamineRequest = z.strictObject({ statement: Statement });
export type ReexamineRequest = z.infer<typeof ReexamineRequest>;

/** POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/appeal: the author's appeal of a final decision that restricts them. */
export const AppealRequest = z.strictObject({ statement: Statement });
export type AppealRequest = z.infer<typeof AppealRequest>;

/**
 * POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/reply (3e design, sections 7.6 step 9 and 10.2): the person's one reply to the
 * suspension or termination a decision holds, with an optional text under the text rules, at most REPLY_TEXT_MAX
 * characters. The server makes its salt and digest, as for an appeal.
 */
export const ReplyRequest = z.strictObject({ statement: noticeText(REPLY_TEXT_MAX).optional() });
export type ReplyRequest = z.infer<typeof ReplyRequest>;

/** The answer to a reply (201): when the database filed it, and whether it came before the start, which it then holds. */
export const ReplyResponse = z.object({ filedAt: z.iso.datetime(), onTime: z.boolean() });
export type ReplyResponse = z.infer<typeof ReplyResponse>;

/**
 * The answer to a request for a re-examination (201): the positions of the items that are now examined again, in
 * order. One, or two when the item is a report of child sexual abuse material about a post that quotes another and the
 * item korbat added for the quoted post could be examined again too: korbat then examines both.
 */
```
